# Phase F2: the native carve - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** The native side splits along the package line, the way the carts and the Launchpad did. A neutral `system`
package holds the contract every console implements and the engine drives; `sameboy` and `mesen` hold their consoles
with their own build functions, ROM gates, button enums and node types; `host-io` holds the host MIDI nodes and the
engine host I/O service; the `testing` package gains the C++ test helpers both console test binaries use; the mGB ROM
becomes an embedded resource a package declares; `txiki` and `efsw` become shell libraries a product opts into; and the
Mesen static library stops carrying the consoles RetroPlug never runs. `retroplug-core` dissolves, `SystemNodes.cpp`
goes, and the closed sets go with them: `SystemFactory`, `SystemBackend`, `CoreBackends`, `registerCoreBackends`, the
`SystemConfig` variant, `SystemKind` and the `kind()` check. A system node builds its own core: its package's build
function rides `rp.host.systems/2` in the request, and the engine recognises a system node by its descriptor's
`category`. **F2 changes no audio:** strict parity, the kit and render baselines, the `buildGraph` and role goldens, the
script and protocol digests, `edio-golden.json`, both device images and the `bliptoaster` pack's bytes hold unmodified.
The one re-record is the `[packages]` golden, in the task that causes it; Task 6 is the acceptance run.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md), whose section 11 ("As
built") records the build and which Task 5 lands, sections 1 to 10 corrected in place to what the prototype found.
Task 1 lands the `system` package and the build seam (the request's `build` and `config`, `rp.host.systems/2`,
`Engine::buildSystem` on `request.build`, category-based recognition, the deleted factory and kind check, the
null-build-function and fixture-console cases, and the planner's `PlanCheck` that refuses a system node which built no
core). Task 2 lands the consoles, `host-io`, the dissolved `retroplug-core`, the product order, the one re-record, the
two console test binaries, the moved clang-cl step and the boundary fixtures. Task 3 lands the embed member, the
per-package object library, the product's `rp_embedded_resources()` table, `putResource` on it, and `mGB.gb` in
`packages/mgb`. Task 4 lands `retroplug-tjs-runtime` and `retroplug-file-watcher`, the `FileWatcher` interface, the
backend on bare QuickJS and the configure check that keeps the three out of the binaries that must not carry them.
Task 5 lands Mesen's three options, the filter table, the 123 guards, the two-way build script, the measurements and
the docs. Task 6 is the acceptance run.

**Tech stack:** CMake 3.28 (`retroplug_package_library`, `retroplug_product`, the manifest reader in
`cmake/packages.cmake`, `bin2c`), C++20 with no exceptions and no RTTI in a device pack, Catch2 for the test binaries,
the vendored Mesen 2 (`deps/mesen`, upstream `b9fa69d`, in-tree), SameBoy with its two tracked patches, `efsw` and
`tjs`/`qjs` as vendored libraries, the Pico SDK only where Task 6 rebuilds the device images, and the F1 package
generator (`packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`). No submodule moves, no dependency version changes.

**Spec:** [modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md) and
[package-split.md](package-split.md) (F2 is the third of its four phases). The mechanism it builds on is F1's
([modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md) section 4 and section 11, and spec/06's "Adding a
package" and "A console package's native half"), the shape it copies is the N8 pack's
([modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md)), the seam it replaces is C4's
([modular-graph-phase-c4-design.md](modular-graph-phase-c4-design.md) section 6, which Task 1 corrects in place), and
[modular-graph-phase-f1-plan.md](modular-graph-phase-f1-plan.md) is a plan executed the way this one is.

**Provenance:** every code block below was built and run before this plan was written, on the scratch branch
`proto/f2-native` in this worktree, on top of the design commit `a1373899d`: five commits, one per task (Task 6 is the
acceptance run and commits nothing), each reviewed by Opus and amended until its review passed, with every fix folded
into the commit it belongs to. A block that creates a file is that file as the prototype commit left it; one that
changes a file is the prototype's diff of it, so `git apply` it from the step's text; a move is a `git mv` block
followed by the prototype's diff of its new path; a deletion is a `git rm`. Each task's verification is its stage's own
run of `/tmp/f2pro/tip-verify.sh` and the legs its fix pass re-ran (each task's suites step says which run each figure is
from); Task 6's is the final verification (`/tmp/f2pro/s5fv-*.log`), run at the prototype's code. Every expected pass,
test count and figure is quoted from the stage reports in /tmp/f2pro, those logs, the design's record or the user's
decisions, which is what the generator checks; a figure no log records is said to be so, and the step asks for it. When
this plan was generated it was replayed in a scratch clone of `a1373899d`, every block written, moved or applied in
order, and each task committed with the command given: each commit's tree came out exactly as the prototype's, and each
commit message as its. The prototype commits, by task:

- Task 1 `e8adc1d90`: F2 stage 1: the system package, and a core built by the function its node carries
- Task 2 `4afbfc6ec`: F2 stage 2: the consoles, host I/O, the product order and the tests
- Task 3 `46f115966`: F2 stage 3: embedded resources a package declares, and the product's table
- Task 4 `eed3668db`: F2 stage 4: txiki and efsw as the shell's opt-in libraries
- Task 5 `0049161f9`: F2 stage 5: Mesen's per-console compile-out, and the docs pass
- Task 6 is the acceptance run and commits nothing.


**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (`a1373899d`).** The design was written before the prototype;
this plan follows what was built, and Task 5 lands the design with section 11's record and sections 1 to 10 corrected in
place. In short (a bullet quotes the design where it uses quotation marks):

- **A system node that built no core costs a refused plan, not a null slot.** The design trusted the descriptor's
  category. The stage 1 review found that a type declaring `"system"` and building nothing would leave a null slot
  for the audio thread to dereference in a release build, where the old `assert(e.core)` is compiled out. The
  planner gained a `PlanCheck` seam (`PlanInput::check`, run after every node has activated and before the plan is
  published, through the planner's own rollback), `Engine::publishGraph` passes the engine's `sys-<id>: no-core`
  check, and both script hosts refuse a pack whose type declares the category. A red-first case per path; the
  planner path is red by removing `~SystemNode`'s destroy, not the check, since `GraphHost::setGraph` drops a
  refused outcome on its error path.
- **The Game Boy logo the SMS gate checks is `mesen`'s private copy.** Stage 2 first put one `RomLogo.hpp` in
  `system`; the review found it made the neutral contract know a console, and `sameboy/RomFormat.hpp` and
  `mesen/RomFormat.hpp` now hold their own 48 bytes. `mesen` may not depend on `sameboy`, so a shared header was the
  only exclusion-free alternative and it was the wrong one.
- **A test may declare a fixture dependency, and a compile definition is a reach.** `sameboy`'s test binary opens
  `mgb`'s ROM file, which the native boundary check refused; a test target may now use a package's `devDependency`
  for a fixture file, judged by the target's own properties (a link, a source, an include directory, a compile
  definition). The review found the first pass blind to the quoted `-DNAME="path"` form the tree writes, which stage
  5's fix pass closed with `_retroplug_unquote_path` and a quoted fixture on each side.
- **The two console test binaries share a native library, `retroplug-testing`.** `CountingAllocator` had three
  copies (the shell's, `mesen`'s and `launchpad`'s) and `LinkRomModel.hpp` needed a home on both sides of the
  n8/mesen edge; the `testing` package's native half holds them and only a `RP_TEST_BINARY` may link it (a configure
  guard, `retroplug_check_test_helpers`, refuses anything else). It is an OBJECT library because a replaced
  `operator new` in an archive member is never pulled in.
- **An embed's symbol is derived once, and a device product emits no table.** `rp_embed_<package>_<id>` is computed
  by one function and a collision (the review's own pair: `lsdj` + `launchpad_kit` against `lsdj-launchpad` + `kit`)
  is refused at configure, `_len` objects included. The table is a function-local static (its rows read extern
  lengths), and a device product emits none: an empty one changed both box images through the new symbol, which is
  why the images stay byte-identical.
- **The runtime-libraries check names every step of the path, and `EXEMPT` empties.** The check first printed
  `target -> library`, cutting at the first edge; it now walks the closure keeping the chain (`a -> b -> tjs`) and
  refuses a guarded name no target has. `retroplug-classid-test` links no backend (it links the runtime library), so
  it leaves the list. `retroplug-watcher-test` still linked the backend for `HostRpcService` itself until stage 5's
  fix pass gave the service a fake `FileWatcher` and moved the service's own gate case to the audio test, which the
  interface Task 4 landed made possible; with that, the test links the watcher library alone and
  `retroplug_check_products` has no `EXEMPT` argument any more.
- **The ~296 KB every backend product lost is efsw, not txiki.** `HostRpcService`'s constructor named
  `NativeFileWatcher`, so a binary that linked the backend pulled its object and, through it, efsw;
  `TjsHostRuntime.cpp.o` is 10 KB and a binary that creates no txiki runtime never pulled it. The design's
  expectation (the render host shrinks most) holds in relative terms only, and the compile-out is the phase's real
  size change.
- **The compile-out is fewer lines and more guards than the design's estimate, and its missed-guard proof is
  repeatable.** 123 `#if MESEN_ENABLE_*` blocks, about 260 added lines, in six files, against the design's ~300
  lines. A `-O0` Debug build found two guards the Release link had folded away, and became a mode of its own:
  `tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh --off` builds the library at `-O0` with the three options OFF and fails on any
  undefined symbol that names a compiled-out unit (red shown with a guard removed), while the script's ON mode
  asserts the four console counts in the CLI, so a run whose options did not take effect fails instead of printing
  four zeros. The filter table's rows are `|` and `,` separated because a `;` flattens a CMake list, and its regex
  is anchored to the source root.
- **`N8ReliableLink`'s test split is eleven and three, not eight and the rest.** The sender-only cases went to the
  N8 pack's own test binary and the three cases from the emulated FIFO role on went with `mesen`, and the
  reliable-link model both compare against (`LinkRomModel.hpp`) lives in `retroplug-testing`, which both test
  binaries may declare, rather than in `n8`'s test tree (a second door for one header).
- **The two console test binaries are `/bigobj` and off `/W4 /WX` on Windows.** Their sources compiled in
  `retroplug-audio-test` and `retroplug-engine-graph-test`, neither of which was ever on the warning list; the first
  Windows run decides whether they can join. `retroplug_add_test_binary` adds `/bigobj` itself, so every test binary
  in a package directory gets it.
- **The build function is a plain pointer and the config a `const void*`, as designed.** No caller needed a closure:
  the node makes its settings' config on the stack, hands its address to `rp.host.systems/2` and the build function
  copies it before returning, so nothing outlives the call.


**The re-records, and the one that only looks like one.** `product-registrations.json` is the phase's only golden that
moves, and what moves is one type's position: `rp.sameboy.gb` sits at position 21 in every product (after `rp.n8.nes`,
where `native`'s entries were) and at position 13 after the re-record (after the Launchpad pack's two, where `sameboy`
is listed); every product still holds the same 28 types, no id and no descriptor moves, and the file keeps the design
commit's formatting, two spaces and the same key order, so the diff is the one type's move in each of the nine rows and
nothing else (nine lines out, nine in). It is Task 2's, by the command the test documents
(`RP_PRODUCT_REGISTRATIONS_UPDATE=1 ... "[packages-dump]"`, whose own output is reflect-cpp's four-space format; the
step re-indents it to the old shape, and the test parses the file, so the shape is free and the content is what holds).
The design asked for the re-record in a commit of its own; the prototype folded it into stage 2's commit, one commit per
stage, and this plan follows the prototype's trees because the replay holds every commit to its. Strict parity, the kit
and render baselines, the `buildGraph` and role goldens, the script and protocol digests, `edio-golden.json`, both
device images and the pack's bytes never move: their legs are in every task's suites step.

**The user's decisions** (`.superpowers/f-split/decisions.md`, the F2 entries; the design was approved section by
section):

- **One phase for the whole native list, and a carve, not a feature.** The neutral contract, the two consoles,
  `host-io`, the embed seam, the two opt-in libraries and the compile-out land together, in five prototype stages
  and five plan tasks. Nothing the phase computes moves: parity, the kit and render baselines, the digests, the
  images and the pack's bytes are the design's own proof, and a change in any of them is a bug to find.
- **The node builds its own core (the user's choice B).** `SystemBuildFn` rides the request; `Engine::buildSystem`
  keeps its bookkeeping (the live-id check before the build, the snapshot slot, the plan's slot) and the roadmap's
  "generated `registerCoreBackends` per product" becomes "there is none". `SystemKind`, `kind()` and the cores'
  `kKind` go with the factory, and the C4 case that refused another console's kind is retired in favour of the
  null-build-function case and the fixture console.
- **The contract's home is a package, and `MemoryType` stays closed.** `system` depends on `node-sdk` alone and
  needs neither `rpcpp` nor reflect-cpp of its own (one moved header includes `rfl/Bytestring.hpp`, which the node
  SDK's PUBLIC link supplies). `MemoryType` is a wire enum of nine regions mirrored in TS: a package that wanted a
  tenth would change the wire and the debug RPCs, and it is the design's one recorded residual.
- **`mesen` declares `n8`.** `NesN8FifoRole` speaks BlipToaster's reliable link from the cart's side, so the include
  that `retroplug-core` reached through a genex becomes a declared dependency; `kExpansionVolume{Min,Max,Default}`
  stops being a copy and `rp.mesen.nes` reads the pack's constants. The edge runs one way: `n8` imports neither
  `mesen` nor `system`.
- **Mesen's compile-out is three options, default ON, set OFF at the root.** NES, GBA and SMS are always built;
  `SNES` covers the Game Boy (Super Game Boy couples them both ways). The library drops 138 of 426 translation units
  and 12.3 MB of 31.1 MB of objects, and the products are about 3.4 MB smaller. A further console switch is one row
  in the filter table.
- **The proof is headless, and no step touches a device.** The carve changes no byte the cart or the box sees, and
  the device images build none of it. `sdl:pipewire`, `reaper:all`, a fresh-clone build, `pnpm build:mesen-all`, its
  `--off` mode and the two consumer suites are the legs no prototype stage ran, and Task 6 runs them. The nine
  Windows items, the first macOS and arm64 builds and the first CI run are **owed to the user** and stated in full
  at the end of Task 6.
- **The model routing, which this plan's execution follows:** the prototype's stages were written by DeepSeek and
  reviewed stage by stage (and, at the end, whole) by Opus, with Flash-Next as the fallback; the design document was
  drafted by Sonnet; this plan was generated by DeepSeek from the prototype's record. The user's routing for the
  phases sets the plan's implementers, the acceptance run and the follow-ups, as F1's and F3's do.
- **What only the record backs.** The design's section 11 is the description of what was built and of what no log
  records; the stage reports in `/tmp/f2pro` are the working record (which run each figure is from, every review
  finding and its fix, the departures a fix pass forced), and `results.md` is the controller's log of them, with
  each verdict and call. Where this plan quotes a figure, it quotes the report or log that states it; where nothing
  does, it says so and asks for the count.


**Hardware safety: this plan touches no hardware, ever.** The rig this plan was generated on has a real NES with an N8
flash cart, a Pico box, a probe, a Zoom L6 and MIDI interfaces attached, and this machine's ALSA sequencer lists them.
Nothing in this plan may list, open, write to, claim, flash or reconfigure any of it. The rules:

- **Never touch the NES, the N8, the Pico box, the probe or the Zoom L6.** No serial port is opened, no `n8-*` CLI
  command runs against a device, nothing is flashed to a Pico, and no `picotool`, `openocd`, `probe-rs` or `dfu-util`
  command is run. Every device-related step in this plan happens on a **build**: `pnpm device:check` and
  `pnpm device:box` compile their images and run the check's plan in an arena, and both are built and never flashed.
- **Nothing that lists or opens a system MIDI port may run, with one exception.**
  `tools/run-sdl-controller.sh` (`pnpm sdl:controller`) is that exception: it sets `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` itself, from
  its two ALSA fakes' full port names, and **refuses** a caller who preset the variable; its listing pass runs before
  anything is claimed, and it fails the run when a listed port is not one of its fakes. Run it as `pnpm sdl:controller`,
  never a bare `retroplug-sdl`, and never with the variable preset.
- **`pnpm sdl:smoke` and `pnpm sdl:pipewire` run under a scratch `RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR` with
  `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW=RP_NO_PORT`, a list that matches nothing** (an EMPTY list means every port, so the
  nothing-matching list has to name something). Both set it themselves; do not remove it, and do not export a list of
  your own.
- **Never run `amidi`, `aconnect`, `aseqdump`, `aplaymidi`, `acpi_listen` or any other port tool against this machine's
  devices**, and never `git`-checkout or build with a saved enabled `controlSurface` in the real
  `~/.config/retroplug`: a saved, enabled pair is claimed at startup and its close bytes go out at quit, which is why
  the SDL tools take a scratch config dir.
- **`retroplug-device-mode-test`, `test:plugin`, `test:native`, `pnpm test` and the CLI legs open no port**: their MIDI
  fakes are scripted openers in C++ and TypeScript. If a run of one of them seems to be waiting on MIDI, stop and
  report it rather than reaching for a queueing tool.
- `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure (two tracked patches). That is expected; never stage, reset or
  stash it, and never touch any submodule (`deps/dpf.js` and everything under it included).

**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**

- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's links are relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to the worktree
  root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 6 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own, named for what it fixes). A commit message is a subject line, a blank line, then the body, and the
  prototype's bodies are quoted whole: use `git commit -F -` as the blocks show. No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with"
  trailer. Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context lines of older code and of the specs): leave those be.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself. Never bare `git stash`, never switch branches with uncommitted work in the tree, and never `rm -rf build` to
  fix CMake: investigate.
- **Every whole-file block below (a `Create`) is followed by the `sed -n` range that extracts it from this plan and by
  the blob hash the file must have:** write or extract the file, then `git hash-object <path>` must print the hash the
  step quotes, which is the prototype commit's blob. **Every diff block is followed by its extraction, a
  `git apply --check`, and the blob hash of each file it changes**, so an applied diff is the prototype's bytes and not
  just something that applies. **Every `patch` block is a TEMPORARY mutation**: apply it, watch the run fail or print
  what the step says, then reverse it with the range the next command gives, so the task's tree is what the commit
  expects.
- **A moved file keeps its include text** (`system/SystemBase.hpp` is `packages/system/native/src/system/SystemBase.hpp`
  on disk and `system/SystemBase.hpp` to an includer), which is why almost every move below is byte identical and the
  few that changed carry a small diff. A moved file whose bytes changed is diffed ONCE, after its `git mv`, as its new
  path; never apply that diff before the move.
- **A binary move is never quoted.** `resources/roms/mGB.gb` moves to `packages/mgb/rom/mGB.gb` with `git mv`, and Task
  3 checks two hashes instead: the blob `git hash-object` prints (the same at both paths) and the size.
- **`pnpm-lock.yaml` is a manifest change's companion, and only one install runs, ever:** the steps that change a
  package's dependencies place the lockfile's diff as it stands and then run
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, which must leave the lockfile's bytes alone (the step quotes its blob).
  Never run a bare `pnpm install`: offline, a non-frozen one re-resolves the lockfile and silently prunes every other
  platform's optional packages. Tasks 1, 2 and 3 each bring one diff; Task 4 and Task 5 change no manifest's
  dependencies.
- **The generated modules are never committed.** `packages/retroplug/src/generated/{packages,protocol,scriptNodes}.ts`
  are written by `packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`, gitignored, and regenerated by the runners,
  `pnpm typecheck` and the CMake `retroplug-ts-packages` target. A worktree a prototype build ran in may hold three of
  them, untracked and stale: Task 1 Step 1 deletes them either way, and no `git status` list below shows them. If one
  ever does, the `.gitignore` entry is wrong: stop and report it.
- **ONE golden is re-recorded, in Task 2, and NOTHING ELSE IS.** Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`, `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`,
  `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE` or
  `RP_PRODUCT_REGISTRATIONS_UPDATE` other than at the one step that re-records `product-registrations.json`. Tasks 1,
  3, 4 and 5 re-record nothing, and prove it: strict parity (30 files, 250 cases), the kit and render baselines, and
  the `git status` lists show no golden. The device images and the pack's bytes are hashed in every task and must not
  move.
- **Case counts are exact. Assertion totals are exact too, with three exceptions:** a run of
  `retroplug-engine-graph-test` that includes `[engine-jobs]` reports a total that moves from run to run (its threaded
  cases assert in loops), so does `retroplug-launchpad-test`'s (its cases count in loops), and so does the
  ThreadSanitizer run of `[script-pack]`; for those the case count must match and the total is the prototype's, quoted
  for scale. Catch2 pads its `test cases:` columns with spaces, which the quotes below collapse to one. `pnpm test`'s
  final line counts FILES; a case total is quoted from a report and is not the runner's own line.
- **`pnpm typecheck`'s project count moves with the tree:** `Scope: 21 of 22 workspace projects` at Task 1 (the
  baseline is `20 of 21`; Task 1 adds `system`) and `22 of 23` from Task 2 on (`host-io`; `testing` and `mgb` gain
  nothing to typecheck, since neither gains TypeScript that is not already covered). Quote the line your step gives, and
  treat a *different* count at the same task as a finding.
- The Catch2 binaries and `retroplug-render-host-test` are `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` or outside the default build:
  `cmake --build build` does not rebuild them, so a library edit needs the target built by name before a run
  (`pnpm test:plugin`, `test:n8` and `test:native` build theirs first), and a size or symbol measurement needs them
  built first too (Task 5's report records the trap). `tools/build-device-check.sh` and `tools/build-box.sh` build the
  exporter in the desktop build themselves. **A new or removed CMake source, a new package, or a manifest change needs
  `cmake -S . -B build` first**, and every task that adds a package needs that configure, because
  `retroplug_product()` refuses a package it was never told about.
- **A `pnpm install` is needed before a configure that reads a new package's `node_modules` link**, and before a
  configure that reads a new product-list entry: each task's frozen install comes before its configure, and Task 1 and
  Task 2's steps check the two links exist.
- The build trees were last built at the prototype's tip, so each task's first build re-runs CMake and recompiles what
  changed; that is expected. `build-device/`, `build-box/` and `pico/n8-host/build/` hold the prototype's images and
  `build/` its bytecode; Task 5 hashes them without rebuilding its own way, and Task 6 rebuilds all of it from removed
  dirs. **The prototype's `deps/mesen` objects are stale:** a removed source's object file stays on disk, so a Mesen
  object count must read `ar t build/deps/mesen/libmesen.a`, never `*.o` files under the build directory.
- **`sdl:controller` is Linux only and needs `libasound2-dev` and an ALSA sequencer**, which this devcontainer has. It
  is not in CI. Its five legs run against `tools/fixtures/fake-launchpad.c` and nothing else, and the hardware-safety
  rules above are what make that true.
- **When a step's result differs from its Expected, stop and report.** A different exit status, case count or quoted
  text is a finding. Three exceptions: an assertion total the rule above calls moving; a predicted failure whose
  failing file, case or target is the one predicted but whose wording differs (the mutation steps say which are
  predicted); and a trap probe's quoted lines, whose object path and `(.text.startup.main+0x...)` offsets are this
  devcontainer's and this binutils' (the device scripts judge a probe by its own object and the two symbol names,
  `__wrap__Znwj` and `__wrap_malloc`, and that check is the pass criterion). Never edit code, a test or a golden to
  make a step pass. In Tasks 1 to 5 each task's tree must equal its prototype commit, so a real defect found there is
  reported, not fixed; a fix belongs to a commit of its own after the plan.
- **Track progress outside the committed plan:** never tick its checkboxes. Ticking one modifies
  `docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-plan.md`, and every task's expected `git status` list would then gain a line it does not
  show.
- The Windows build has not seen this tree (the prototype is local and Linux-only), so an MSVC-only warning or error is
  a real finding to report, not a stale quote: Task 6 states the nine owed items, and no step below builds on Windows.
  macOS and the arm64 Linux CI job have not run either: `build.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch`, pull requests and
  pushes to `main` only, so their first run is a dispatched run or a PR the user starts. **No step below needs a real
  device, and none may touch one.**

## File structure

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `packages/system/` | the contract: `SystemBase` and the capability interfaces, `SystemId`, `InputCapacity`, the transport triples with `SeqlockCopy`, `MidiTypes`, the build request and `SystemBuildFn`, `HostSystems` (`rp.host.systems/2`) and `EngineSyncTrace`, the generic `SystemNode` template with the neutral knob helpers, and the core-only utilities (Task 1) |
| `packages/sameboy/`, `packages/mesen/` | each console's native half: its systems and configs, its ROM gate and button enum, its build function, its node types and package entry (Task 2), and `mesen`'s declared `n8` edge |
| `packages/host-io/` | `HostIoNodes` (`rp.host.midi-in` / `-out`) and `EngineHostIo` (`rp.engine.host-io/3`) with the constants the engine reads (Task 2) |
| `packages/native/` | the shell: `Engine`, `SystemTable`, `SnapshotRegistry`, `OfflineJobs`, the RPC services, the script/render/compiler hosts, `SampleCache`, `FileSync`, lodepng, the products, and the two opt-in libraries `retroplug-tjs-runtime` and `retroplug-file-watcher` (Tasks 2, 4) |
| `packages/testing/native/` | `retroplug-testing`: `CountingAllocator` and `LinkRomModel.hpp`, an OBJECT library only a test binary may link (Task 2) |
| `packages/mgb/` | the ROM as an embedded resource: `rom/mGB.gb` and the manifest's `embed` entry (Task 3) |
| `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/graph/` | the planner's `PlanCheck` seam (`Planner.hpp`, `GraphHost.cpp`), the generated `rp_embedded_resources()` declarations (`Packages.hpp`), and the MicroQuickJS host's category refusal (Tasks 1, 3) |
| `cmake/packages.cmake` | the manifest reader's `embed` member and `native` object, the embed symbol and table generation, the compile-definition and devDependency rule, `retroplug_check_test_helpers`, `retroplug_check_runtime_libraries` (Tasks 2, 3, 4) |
| `cmake/bin2c.cmake`, `cmake/check-embeds.cmake`, `cmake/refused-script-pack.cmake`, `cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake` | the embed generator, the two configure-fixture drivers, and the boundary check's definition rule |
| `deps/mesen/` | the vendored Mesen 2 tree, in-tree: the three `MESEN_ENABLE_*` options, the filter table, and 123 `#if` guards in six files (Task 5) |
| `tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh` | the two-way Mesen build: all three consoles ON in Release against the CLI, and `--off` at `-O0` against the archive's undefined symbols (Task 5) |
| `packages/native/test/packages/` | the configure fixtures: the boundary refusals and holds, the embed read/refuse cases, the embed-collision projects, and the product with no embeds (Tasks 2, 3, 4) |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | the workspace's edges, one diff per task that changes a manifest's dependencies (Tasks 1, 2, 3) |
| `docs/`, `spec/`, `AGENTS.md` | each task's prose, the design's as-built record and the live docs (Task 5), and the dead links each move repoints (Tasks 1, 2) |

---

### Task 1: the system package, and a core built by the function its node carries

Design sections 2, 3 and 9's first stage. The contract moves out of the shell into `packages/system` - `SystemBase` and
the capability interfaces, `SystemId` and the shared types, `InputCapacity`, the transport triples with their seqlock,
`MidiTypes`, the core-only utilities, the host's `rp.host.systems/2` struct and the engine's sync trace - and with it the
generic `SystemNode` template and the console-neutral knob helpers that `SystemNodes.cpp` used to hold as code. The
package has no TypeScript and registers no node type: its manifest names one target, which is the form the reader
already allows.

The stage's real subject is the seam. A system node now builds its own core: its package's `SystemBuildFn` and a
`const void*` to the console config its settings made ride the request across `rp.host.systems/2`, `Engine::buildSystem`
keeps its checks and its order and calls `request.build`, and the engine recognises a system node by its descriptor's
`category` instead of walking two packages by name. `SystemFactory`, `SystemBackend`, `CoreBackends`,
`registerCoreBackends`, the `SystemConfig` variant, `SystemKind` and every core's `kKind` are deleted, and with them the
C4 case that refused a core built with another console's kind: the node hands its own package's function and config, so
the two cannot disagree.

The review's finding shapes the stage's two refusals. A type that declares `category: "system"` and builds no core would
leave a null slot for the audio thread to dereference in a release build, where the old `assert(e.core)` is gone, so the
planner gained a `PlanCheck` seam (run after every node has activated and before the plan is published, through its own
rollback) and both script hosts refuse a pack whose type declares the category. The four node types stay in the shell
this stage, with the four console build functions; Task 2 moves them into their packages.

The task's first step moves and deletes only; nothing is built until Step 11, because no step before it leaves a tree
that compiles.

**Files:**

- Create (7): `cmake/refused-script-pack.cmake`, `packages/native/test/device-mode/script-packs/system-category/index.ts`, `packages/system/native/CMakeLists.txt`, `packages/system/native/src/system/HostSystems.hpp`, `packages/system/native/src/system/SystemBuild.hpp`, `packages/system/native/src/system/SystemNode.hpp`, `packages/system/package.json`
- Move (20 files, each by the `git mv` its step prints; 2 of them changed too and carry that file's diff after its move): from `packages/native/src/system/`, `packages/native/src/transport/`, `packages/native/src/util/`
- Modify (44 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 6 under `packages/native/src/system/mesen/`; 5 under `packages/native/test/engine-graph/`; 4 under `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/graph/`; 4 under `spec/`; 3 under `docs/`; 3 under `packages/native/src/host/graph/` and the rest)
- Delete (4): `packages/native/src/system/CoreBackends.cpp`, `packages/native/src/system/CoreBackends.hpp`, `packages/native/src/system/SystemFactory.cpp`, `packages/native/src/system/SystemFactory.hpp`

Create `packages/system/native/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# The system package (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 2): the contract every console implements and the
# engine drives, and the console-neutral plumbing around it. Added by retroplug_package(system) (cmake/packages.cmake);
# a product that lists it registers nothing (its manifest names a target and no entry), but every console's package is
# built on it beside the shell.
#
# Its include root, src/, is where each of these keeps the path it is included by ("system/SystemBase.hpp",
# "transport/MidiTypes.hpp", "util/Gain.hpp"), so a core's source reads the same whichever package it sits in.
#
# It depends on node-sdk and nothing else: DebugTarget.hpp's register and profiler types ride reflect-cpp's
# rfl/Bytestring.hpp, which node-sdk brings (its library links reflect-cpp), and the SystemNode template is written in
# the SDK's node authoring layer (graph/node.hpp). Nothing here includes rpcpp.
retroplug_package_library(retroplug-system
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/SystemBase.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/SystemCapabilities.cpp
    # processAlive only, so <windows.h> stays in one TU rather than in every includer of the header (the NES core pulls
    # it in through NesEverdriveFifo.hpp).
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/util/ProcessId.cpp)
target_include_directories(retroplug-system PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-system PUBLIC retroplug-node-sdk)
````

comment that says why the id moved (`/1`'s request carried a `SystemConfig` variant a node built against `/2` would
misread). `system/SystemBuild.hpp` is `SystemBuildFn` and `SystemBuildRequest`: the ROM, SRAM and savestate seeds, the
ROM's name, the block's maximum frames, `build` and the opaque `config` pointer. `system/SystemNode.hpp` is the
`SystemNode<Self, Core, Settings>` template `SystemNodes.cpp` used to define as code - its `activate`, its ports, its
params, its block and its teardown - plus the console-neutral knob helpers (`knobs::labelAt`, `literalOf`, `Within`,
`Label`, `valueOf`, `same`, `moved`, the output and gain constants and the inputs list). The template has no default
settings type: that would be one console's, and the console packages own theirs.

````cpp
#pragma once

// The system services a system node asks its host for through rp_host.get_interface
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 5, docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 3): the builder it
// hands a SystemBuildRequest to, and the engine's sync trace. They live in the system package rather than the shell's
// host/graph/HostServices.hpp because they are what the contract is about - the nodes bind them, the engine implements
// them - and a console's package carries them without reaching the shell. The device links (rp.host.devices/2) and the
// job reports (rp.host.jobs/1) a device's node takes, and the staged message (rp.stage/1) it presents, are the node
// SDK's (graph/rp_device.h, graph/rp_jobs.h, graph/rp_stage.h), and the engine's host I/O (rp.engine.host-io/3) is the
// shell's until the host-io package owns it.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "graph/rp_node.h"
#include "system/SystemBuild.hpp"

class SystemBase;

namespace rp::host {

#define RP_HOST_SYSTEMS_INTERFACE "rp.host.systems/2"
// A system node building its core where it runs. [control]: build and destroy both run there, build inside the setGraph
// that activates the node and destroy at the reclaim that frees the plan which last ran it (or as a refused plan
// unwinds). A node's resources are pinned by its instance already, so a build reads bytes rather than files.
struct HostSystems {
    void* ctx;
    // Build the core of the system `system`, from the ROM and seeds the node's resources hold, the config its settings
    // made, and the build function its package carries. Null, with the reason in *err, for a request that names no
    // build function, a ROM that console's gate refuses, a boot the core refuses, an id that is live (held by a node of
    // any plan not yet reclaimed) and a full snapshot pool. A core built here is the node's until `destroy`: the host
    // claimed its snapshot slot under `system` and keeps it among its live cores, so the plan's table and the control
    // plane see it at once.
    //
    // /2: the request carries a build function and an opaque config pointer where /1 carried a SystemConfig variant, so
    // the host no longer picks a backend by the alternative it held. A node built against /1 would read the config as a
    // variant, which is why the id moved; every consumer is in tree (the system nodes, the tests' rigs).
    SystemBase* (*build)(void* ctx, std::uint64_t system, SystemBuildRequest request, rp_error* err);
    // The node is giving up a core it built: release its snapshot slot, leave the live cores and delete it.
    void (*destroy)(void* ctx, SystemBase* core);
};

// The engine's sync trace (HostSyncTrace): a system node records the bytes its `bytes` input feeds the core's byte
// device, so across systems a block's bytes are in plan order, one system's after another's, where the kernel
// stage's were in its emission order. The trace is a diagnostic, and nothing reads that order. Nothing while the
// trace is off. [audio]
#define RP_ENGINE_SYNC_TRACE_INTERFACE "rp.engine.sync-trace/1"
struct EngineSyncTrace {
    void* ctx;
    void (*bytes)(void* ctx, std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size);
};

}  // namespace rp::host
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "system/SystemTypes.hpp"  // SystemId

class SystemBase;

struct SystemBuildRequest;

// A system to build (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 5): the bytes a system node's resources hold, the
// ROM's name, and the console config its settings make. Every core is built this way, so there is one boot path per
// console, and the node whose package owns the console carries the function that reads it
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 3): the host builds what the request names, and knows no console.
//
// [control]: the build runs inside the setGraph that activates the node that asked for it, so `config` points at a
// config the node holds for the call and `build` runs synchronously. A build function is a plain function pointer, with
// no capture, because the node's type names it, and it consumes the request: the ROM is moved into the core rather than
// copied a second time.

// `id` is the system the core is built under, `request` what to build it from (its `config` is the console's, which
// only this function reads), `sampleRate` the rate the plan runs at, and `why` receives a refusal's reason. Returns an
// already-onActivate'd core, or null: for a ROM the console's gate refuses, a boot the core refuses, or a request that
// carried no config (the node passes the one its settings made, so a config of the wrong console's is a bug no build
// function can see through the void pointer).
using SystemBuildFn = std::unique_ptr<SystemBase> (*)(SystemId id, SystemBuildRequest&& request, double sampleRate,
                                                      std::string* why);

struct SystemBuildRequest {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> rom;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> sram;       // battery RAM seed (may be empty)
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> savestate;  // savestate seed (may be empty)
    // The ROM's file stem. A Master System or Game Gear core stages its ROM as a file and takes its battery stem from
    // that name, and now that its ROM is bytes it has nothing else to name the file by; empty keeps the core's "rom".
    std::string  romName;
    // The largest block the plan this core is built for will run, in frames; 0 for a build outside a plan (a test, a
    // tool), which then keeps the console's default. It is reserved before the core activates, so its audio ring and
    // its per-block scratches are sized to the plan from the start rather than to the default and then grown
    // (docs/modular-graph-phase-c4-design.md section 4). A host that grows its block later reserves again, through
    // SystemBase::reserveAudio on the reactivation that is quiescent with respect to the core.
    std::uint32_t maxBlockFrames = 0;
    // The node's package's build function, and the console config its settings made, which only that function reads (a
    // SameBoyConfig, a MesenNesConfig): the node holds the config for the duration of the call. `build` null is a
    // request that names no console, which the host refuses before it claims anything.
    SystemBuildFn build  = nullptr;
    const void*   config = nullptr;
};
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The generic system node (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 2): what every console's node shares, and the
// knob helpers its settings are written with. A console's package keeps its settings type and the settings themselves;
// this header keeps the part that is no console's - the load of the core through the host's builder, the settings and
// params that reach it, the connected-output mask, the node's inputs, and prepare / step / finish mapped one to one
// onto the core's block triad.
//
// It is a header because a console's package is where its node type lives, and every one of them instantiates this
// template from its own translation unit. It depends on node-sdk (graph/node.hpp for the authoring layer and
// graph/rp_stage.h for the staged message), on the system contract it is part of (SystemBase, the build request, the
// host's services) and on nothing else.

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <limits>
#include <optional>
#include <span>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <type_traits>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include <rfl/Literal.hpp>
#include <rfl/Result.hpp>
#include <rfl/Validator.hpp>
#include <rfl/enums.hpp>
#include <rfl/parsing/schema/ValidationType.hpp>

#include "graph/CanonicalJson.hpp"
#include "graph/node.hpp"
#include "graph/rp_stage.h"
#include "system/HostSystems.hpp"
#include "system/SystemBase.hpp"
#include "system/SystemBuild.hpp"
#include "transport/MidiTypes.hpp"

namespace rp::host {

// The knobs' value types. An enum knob is a label as the role configs spell it
// (packages/sameboy/ts/enums.ts, packages/mesen/ts/enums.ts), which is the name of its C++ enumerator with the first
// letter lowercased:
// SameBoyModel::CgbC is "cgbC", SameBoyHighpass::RemoveDcOffset "removeDcOffset", SameBoyModel::Auto "auto". So the
// enumerators are native's one spelling of every label: Label<E> is the rfl::Literal made of them, which reads exactly
// those strings (anything else refuses the settings), lists them in the descriptor's schema, and maps back to its
// enumerator by position (valueOf). Never an ordinal: the document and a saved project carry the same word
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-c2-design.md section 3). labelAt and same's Literal overloads name
// rfl::internal::StringLiteral, an internal reflect-cpp type, so a reflect-cpp bump is to check them.

namespace knobs {

template <class E, std::size_t I>
constexpr auto labelAt() {
    constexpr std::string_view name = rfl::get_enumerator_array<E>()[I].first;
    std::array<char, name.size() + 1> chars{};
    for (std::size_t k = 0; k < name.size(); ++k) chars[k] = name[k];
    if (chars[0] >= 'A' && chars[0] <= 'Z') chars[0] = static_cast<char>(chars[0] - 'A' + 'a');
    return rfl::internal::StringLiteral<name.size() + 1>(chars);
}

template <class E, std::size_t... I>
rfl::Literal<labelAt<E, I>()...> literalOf(std::index_sequence<I...>);

// A number refused outside [R::min, R::max], as a settings value out of its range is refused anywhere (a document is
// checked, never quietly changed; the store clamps every knob to the same range before it publishes), with the range
// in the descriptor's schema. The bounds ride a type rather than template values: a floating-point template argument
// is beyond some of the compilers the build supports.
template <class R>
struct Within {
    template <class T>
    static rfl::Result<T> validate(T value) noexcept {
        if (value >= R::min && value <= R::max) return value;  // NaN is refused too
        return rfl::error("Value expected to be between " + rp::graph::jsNumber(R::min) + " and " +
                          rp::graph::jsNumber(R::max) + ", but got " + rp::graph::jsNumber(value) + ".");
    }
    template <class T>
    static rfl::parsing::schema::ValidationType to_schema() {
        using V = rfl::parsing::schema::ValidationType;
        return V{V::AllOf{.types_ = {V{V::Minimum{.value_ = rfl::Variant<double, int>(R::min)}},
                                     V{V::Maximum{.value_ = rfl::Variant<double, int>(R::max)}}}}};
    }
};

template <class E>
using Label = decltype(literalOf<E>(std::make_index_sequence<rfl::get_enumerator_array<E>().size()>{}));

template <class E>
E valueOf(const Label<E>& label) {
    return rfl::get_enumerator_array<E>()[label.value()].second;
}

// Whether a knob is to be applied: present in `to`, and absent from `from`, what was applied last, or another value
// there. A knob absent from `to` is never applied, so a field a document drops leaves the core as it is.
inline bool same(bool a, bool b) { return a == b; }
template <rfl::internal::StringLiteral... L>
bool same(const rfl::Literal<L...>& a, const rfl::Literal<L...>& b) { return a.value() == b.value(); }
template <class T, class... V>
bool same(const rfl::Validator<T, V...>& a, const rfl::Validator<T, V...>& b) { return a.value() == b.value(); }
template <class F>
bool moved(const std::optional<F>& to, const std::optional<F>& from) { return to && !(from && same(*from, *to)); }

}  // namespace knobs

// The output lanes a plan can wire to one node: the stack array prepare() and finish() collect them in is this wide, so
// no node type's port count (the Game Boy's four stems, a NES's five channels) passes it.
inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxOutputs = 16;

// The params (docs/modular-graph-phase-c2-design.md section 3): what is worth playing, automating or modulating, so
// each is also a control input, its value in the document and its live edits through Engine::setParam. Every system
// node has `gain`, in dB over the range the store clamps a gain to (systemSettings.ts GAIN_MIN / GAIN_MAX); a console
// with a param beyond it declares that one beside its own type (the NES's expansion volume). The range is one constant,
// used by the param's declaration and by the node's own clamp of a wire-driven value.
inline constexpr double kGainMinDb = -90.0;
inline constexpr double kGainMaxDb = 12.0;
using GainParam = rp::float_param<"Gain", rp::range{kGainMinDb, kGainMaxDb, 0}, "dB">;

// What a param's last-applied value holds before the core has been given any: no value equals it, NaN included.
inline constexpr double kUnapplied = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();

// The inputs every system node has (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 3.1), each mapped onto the core
// call SystemBase already has. A type declares them in its `inputs`, under these names.
//
//   serialIn  bytes   pushSerialIn(frame, byte), one call per byte
//   midi      events  onMidi; a message longer than a MidiEvent holds goes down pushCoreBytes, unframed
//   bytes     bytes   pushCoreBytes(frame, data, size, flush), the flush flag riding RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH
//   buttons   events  pressButton(button, down), from a 2-byte payload [button, down]

// What every system node shares: the core it builds, its settings and params reaching that core, the connected-output
// mask, its inputs, and prepare / step / finish mapped one to one onto the core's block triad. `Self` declares its
// params (`gain` at least), supplies finish's lanes, may write output queues after the core has run (writeQueues), and
// applies its own knobs (apply) and any param beyond the gain (applyParams).
//
// A node builds its core at activation from the bytes its resources hold (rp.host.systems/2,
// docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 5). The core is the host's: the snapshot slot under the system id, the
// live cores, and the delete when the node is destroyed. Which fields a build reads is rebuild_key's, the
// construct-time fields among them. The build itself is the node's own package's (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md
// section 3): `Self::kBuild` is the function the request carries and the config `Self::config` makes is its subject, so
// the host that runs it knows no console, and the cast below has no console to disagree with.
//
// Only a new core rebuilds (rebuild_key): every other setting is a knob the node applies to the core it has, so its
// prepare reads nothing a commit writes and setGraph never waits on a system node's commit (stateless_prepare). A
// commit only points `settings` at the new settings (on_settings never allocates); the node applies what moved at the
// start of its next block, before the core's prepareForBlock, and everything present once at activation, as it takes
// or builds its core, before that core first runs. What the core was given is `applied`, a Settings::Applied, which is
// the live knobs alone: the fields carrying a string (romName, sdRoot, the resource refs) all rebuild the node or move
// a resource, which no application sees, so the copy the node makes when it applies a commit, on the block thread,
// copies no string. So a setting lands at the node's next prepare, after every host command queued behind its plan
// (the host drains its ring before it runs a block): a caller that must act on the restarted core renders a block
// first, since a RAM write or staged core bytes sent after a model change reach the core it is about to replace. Each
// knob is guarded twice, first by `moved` against what this node last applied, so a document's unchanged field is not
// re-applied even where the core was changed by another path, then by the core's own setter where it has one
// (setFastBoot and a NES's setRemoveSpriteLimit write unconditionally). A palette change re-applies the display group
// and restarts nothing, while a model change restarts the core and a region change resets it
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-c2-design.md section 4). A settings field the type does not know is ignored (node.hpp
// reads with rfl::DefaultIfMissing and no rfl::NoExtraFields), so a misspelt knob plans and does nothing.
//
// A param's value reaches the core at the start of each block whose control stream moves it, before the core's
// prepareForBlock and after the settings (a model's restart first, then the levels), each value-guarded against the
// value the core was given last: a publish carrying the value the core already has calls nothing. Every one is given
// at the node's first block, before the core's first prepareForBlock: a node reads its params only in a block (the
// host binds its control streams there, and lands the document's values in them as it adopts the plan), and a core a
// node has built runs nothing before that. The first value is snapped into the core, whose gain smoother
// starts at 0 dB, so the node plays its first sample at the document's level; every later gain change is smoothed by
// the core, as every gain edit is.
template <class Self, class Core, class S>
struct SystemNode {
    using Settings = S;
    // What the core was given (the live knobs alone, per Settings::Applied): trivially copyable, since the block thread
    // writes it, so a string-valued live knob would have to be added here deliberately rather than ride a copy of the
    // whole settings.
    using Applied = typename Settings::Applied;
    static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<Applied>,
                  "a settings application must not allocate on the block thread");
    static auto rebuild_key(const Settings& s) { return s.key(); }
    static constexpr bool stateless_prepare = true;

    const HostSystems*                     systems = nullptr;  // null when the host offers no builder
    const EngineSyncTrace*                 trace = nullptr;  // null when the host keeps none
    Core*                                  core = nullptr;  // owned
    std::array<std::uint8_t, kMaxOutputs>  connected{};
    const Settings*                        settings = nullptr;  // the committed ones, alive until the next commit
    Applied                                applied{};           // the live knobs the core was given last (none before)
    bool                                   pending = false;     // settings committed and not yet applied
    double                                 gainApplied = kUnapplied;  // the gain param's value the core has, in dB

    SystemNode() = default;
    SystemNode(const SystemNode&) = delete;
    SystemNode& operator=(const SystemNode&) = delete;
    // Destroyed on the control thread, at reclaim once no plan runs it or as a refused plan is unwound. The core it
    // built is the host's to release (its snapshot slot, and the live-core map, go with it); a node that never built
    // one has no core, and build throws before setting it when the host offers no systems service.
    ~SystemNode() {
        if (core) systems->destroy(systems->ctx, core);
    }

    void bind_host(const rp_host* h) noexcept {
        systems = static_cast<const HostSystems*>(h->get_interface(h, RP_HOST_SYSTEMS_INTERFACE));
        trace = static_cast<const EngineSyncTrace*>(h->get_interface(h, RP_ENGINE_SYNC_TRACE_INTERFACE));
    }

    // rp.stage/1: a message a host aimed at this node, straight into its core's ingress (Engine::stageNodeMidi's
    // path). The UI's knob traffic reaches the core whatever the project's musical routing does, and to the node
    // whose menu it came from. Frame 0: a knob has no musical position.
    rp_host_stage staged{this, &stageFn};
    static bool stageFn(void* ctx, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, double) {
        return static_cast<SystemNode*>(ctx)->stageMessage(data, size);
    }
    // pushCoreBytes, not onMidi, where the core has a raw ingress: onMidi is the MIDI-FRAMED door, and the NES role's
    // implementation clamps every event to MidiEvent::kDataSize and ignores dataExt (NesN8FifoRole.cpp), so a SysEx
    // through it arrives as its first four bytes and the cart waits forever for an F7 that was thrown away.
    // pushCoreBytes is the raw door a protocol node's bytes reach the core through, with no framing and no cap. A core
    // with no raw ingress falls back to the framed one, where a channel message still fits; nothing longer goes.
    bool stageMessage(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
        if (core == nullptr || data == nullptr || size == 0) return false;
        if (core->hasCoreBytesIn()) {
            // flush=false: a flush DISCARDS whatever the device still holds, which for the N8 FIFO is the performance
            // queued behind this. A settings message is not a barrier; it joins the stream.
            core->pushCoreBytes(0, data, size, false);
            return true;
        }
        if (size > ::MidiEvent::kDataSize) return false;
        ::MidiEvent ev{};
        ev.frame = 0;
        ev.size = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size);
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) ev.data[i] = data[i];
        core->onMidi(&ev, 1);
        return true;
    }
    const void* get_interface(std::string_view id) noexcept { return id == RP_STAGE_INTERFACE ? &staged : nullptr; }
    void on_settings(const Settings& s) noexcept {
        settings = &s;
        pending = true;
    }

    // A create that names no system refuses here rather than planning a document whose node would run nothing
    // (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 3). A node also names its ROM; the seeds are optional (a blank
    // battery is legitimate).
    static std::optional<std::string> validate(const Settings& s) {
        if (s.system == 0)
            return std::string("a system node names the system it builds ({\"system\": <id>, \"rom\": \"res:N\"})");
        if (s.rom.empty()) return std::string("a system node names its ROM as {\"rom\": \"res:N\"}");
        return std::nullopt;
    }

    // The first activation builds the core the settings name, and gives it every knob the settings carry; later ones
    // (a re-activation) keep it. A core is built at the rate the plan runs at, which Engine::setSampleRate re-rates. A
    // plan that is then refused destroys it as it unwinds. Either way the core learns the largest block it will run
    // before it runs one: a build is handed the plan's maximum, so the core sizes its audio ring, its tap's rings and
    // its per-block scratches to it as it activates (a default-sized core would keep that memory for a small host
    // block's whole life), and a plan that grows a host's block reactivates the whole graph quiescent, where
    // reserveAudio moves the sizes with no block in flight.
    bool activate(double, std::uint32_t maxFrames) {
        if (core) {
            core->reserveAudio(maxFrames);
            return true;
        }
        // The config `Self::config` makes lives for this call and no longer: the build runs synchronously inside it,
        // and only `Self::kBuild` reads it.
        const auto config = static_cast<Self*>(this)->config(*settings);
        build(&config, maxFrames);
        core->reserveAudio(maxFrames);
        return true;
    }

    // Build the core the settings name, through rp.host.systems/2, with the bytes this instance's resources pinned, the
    // config its settings made, the plan's largest block and the build function its package carries: the build applies
    // the config and reserves that block before onActivate, and boots and restores the seeds there, so a non-default
    // model never restarts the core it just restored. A failure throws its reason, which rp::detail::activateFn reports
    // and the planner shows as activate-failed on this node. `config` is what `Self::config` made, and `Self::kBuild`
    // alone reads it.
    void build(const void* config, std::uint32_t maxBlockFrames) {
        if (!systems) throw std::runtime_error("the host offers no system builder (rp.host.systems/2)");
        SystemBuildRequest request;
        request.rom = bytesOf(settings->rom);
        request.sram = bytesOf(settings->sram);
        request.savestate = bytesOf(settings->state);
        request.romName = settings->romName.value_or(std::string());
        request.maxBlockFrames = maxBlockFrames;
        request.build = Self::kBuild;
        request.config = config;
        rp_error err{};
        SystemBase* made = systems->build(systems->ctx, settings->system, std::move(request), &err);
        if (!made)
            throw std::runtime_error(err.message[0] ? std::string(err.message) : std::string("the core did not build"));
        // The cast is by construction, which is why nothing checks it: the function that built the core is this type's
        // own, so a core of another class is a package's broken build function and not something a document or a host
        // can ask for.
        core = static_cast<Core*>(made);
        // The build applied the config, so its fields are on the core already: `applied` is seeded with the settings'
        // live knobs, less what the config does not carry, so the node's own first application finds them equal and
        // calls nothing (a model change would restart the core and lose the savestate the build restored). What is left
        // over is a live knob, which reaches the core now.
        applied = settings->liveKnobs();
        static_cast<Self*>(this)->configApplied(applied);
        applySettings();
    }

    static std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytesOf(const auto& field) {
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> out;
        if (const rp_bytes* bytes = field.bytes()) out.assign(bytes->data, bytes->data + bytes->size);
        return out;
    }

    // A type whose config carries none of its knobs clears them here, so the node's first block applies them.
    void configApplied(Applied&) const noexcept {}

    void applySettings() noexcept {
        static_cast<Self*>(this)->apply(*settings, applied);
        applied = settings->liveKnobs();
        pending = false;
    }
    // A core with no knobs of its own (the GBA, the SMS).
    void apply(const Settings&, const Applied&) noexcept {}

    void ports_changed(std::span<const std::uint8_t> mask) noexcept {
        connected.fill(0);
        std::copy_n(mask.begin(), std::min(mask.size(), connected.size()), connected.begin());
    }

    static AudioBlockInfo info(const rp::Block& b) {
        const rp_transport& t = b.transport();
        return AudioBlockInfo{b.frames(), t.sample_rate, t.tempo, t.ppq, (t.flags & RP_TRANSPORT_PLAYING) != 0};
    }

    // An unlinked system: prepare, step until it has the block, finish - a coupled group of one.
    void process(const rp::Block& b) noexcept {
        prepare(b);
        while (core->stepIfBelowTarget(b.frames())) {
        }
        finish(b);
    }
    // The knobs that moved, the params that moved, then the inputs, are applied here, where process starts too: a
    // linked Game Boy's coupled group prepares every member (rp.step/1) before any of them steps, and never calls
    // process. Knobs first, because a model change restarts the core before its inputs reach it, and because this
    // prepare is where a setting lands.
    void prepare(const rp::Block& b) noexcept {
        if (pending) applySettings();
        static_cast<Self*>(this)->applyParams();
        applyInputs();
        // The core learns how many lanes this block drains before it steps: a core whose step gates on a ring of its
        // own fills the one finish() will read, and finishBlock gets the same count. Only the lane COUNT is wanted
        // here, so this is the same lookup finish() makes, into a throwaway array.
        std::array<float*, 2 * kMaxOutputs> lanes{};
        core->setBlockLanes(static_cast<Self*>(this)->lanes(b, lanes));
        core->prepareForBlock(info(b));
    }

    // Each param's latest value this block, where it differs from what the core has: a change anywhere in the block
    // lands at its start. This one for a type whose one param is its gain. A value a wire carries is clamped to the
    // param's range here, as the planner and setParam clamp a document's or a live edit's.
    void applyParams() noexcept { applyGain(); }
    void applyGain() noexcept {
        const double latest = static_cast<Self*>(this)->params.gain.latest();
        if (latest != latest) return;  // NaN reaches a param only over a wire, and moves nothing
        const double db = std::clamp(latest, kGainMinDb, kGainMaxDb);
        if (db == gainApplied) return;
        // The core's smoother starts at 0 dB, so its first value is snapped: a node placed at -90 dB is silent from
        // its first sample rather than ramping down from unity. Later edits ramp as every gain edit does.
        core->setGainDb(static_cast<float>(db), gainApplied != gainApplied);
        gainApplied = db;
    }
    bool step(std::uint32_t target) noexcept { return !core->stepIfBelowTarget(target); }

    // finishBlock adds into its lanes, so they start at zero. Every other connected audio output is written too
    // (the ABI's rule), as silence.
    void finish(const rp::Block& b) noexcept {
        std::array<float*, 2 * kMaxOutputs> lanes{};
        const std::size_t n = static_cast<Self*>(this)->lanes(b, lanes);
        for (std::uint32_t o = 0; o < b.raw.output_count && o < connected.size(); ++o)
            if (connected[o] && b.output(o).kind == RP_PORT_AUDIO)
                for (std::uint32_t c = 0; c < b.output(o).u.audio.channel_count; ++c)
                    std::memset(b.output(o).u.audio.channels[c], 0, b.frames() * sizeof(float));
        for (std::size_t l = 0; l < n; ++l) std::memset(lanes[l], 0, b.frames() * sizeof(float));
        core->finishBlock(info(b), lanes.data(), n);
        static_cast<Self*>(this)->writeQueues(b.frames());
    }
    void writeQueues(std::uint32_t) noexcept {}

    // Each input in queue order, the inputs in the order the kernel stage the kernel node replaced fanned its sinks
    // out: serialIn, midi, bytes, buttons. The order matters on the NES, where MIDI and bytes land in the same FIFO
    // (a flushed byte message drops the MIDI queued ahead of it). Before prepareForBlock, as that stage ran before
    // the core.
    void applyInputs() noexcept {
        auto& in = static_cast<Self*>(this)->inputs;
        for (const rp_message& m : in.serialIn.messages())
            for (const std::uint8_t byte : in.serialIn.data(m)) core->pushSerialIn(m.frame, byte);
        for (const rp_message& m : in.midi.messages()) {
            const auto data = in.midi.data(m);
            if (data.empty()) continue;
            // Longer than a MidiEvent holds (a SysEx, or several messages staged as one run): the core's raw byte
            // path, unframed and uncapped. A core with no byte device (SameBoy's mGB speaks 3-byte messages only)
            // ignores it, which also keeps a dangling MidiEvent::dataExt out of SameBoy's queued copy.
            if (data.size() > ::MidiEvent::kDataSize) {
                core->pushCoreBytes(m.frame, data.data(), data.size(), false);
                continue;
            }
            ::MidiEvent ev{};
            ev.frame = m.frame;
            ev.size = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(data.size());
            for (std::size_t j = 0; j < data.size(); ++j) ev.data[j] = data[j];
            core->onMidi(&ev, 1);
        }
        for (const rp_message& m : in.bytes.messages()) {
            const auto data = in.bytes.data(m);
            if (data.empty()) continue;
            if (trace) trace->bytes(trace->ctx, m.frame, data.data(), data.size());
            core->pushCoreBytes(m.frame, data.data(), data.size(), (m.flags & RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH) != 0);
        }
        for (const rp_message& m : in.buttons.messages()) {
            const auto data = in.buttons.data(m);
            if (data.size() >= 2) core->pressButton(data[0], data[1] != 0);
        }
    }

    // The stereo mix as lanes 0 and 1.
    static std::size_t mixLanes(const rp::Block& b, std::array<float*, 2 * kMaxOutputs>& lanes) {
        lanes[0] = b.output(0).u.audio.channels[0];
        lanes[1] = b.output(0).u.audio.channels[1];
        return 2;
    }
};

}  // namespace rp::host
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The engine's seam: the build function, the category, the null-build refusal**

`Engine::buildSystem` keeps its five checks in order (the `setGraph` window, 0, beyond a system id, a live id) and
adds one before anything is claimed: a request that names no build function is refused with its own reason, so it
claims no snapshot slot and no live id. It then calls `request.build` where it called the factory. The factory member,
its forward declaration and the constructor's `registerCoreBackends(*factory_)` are gone. `isSystemNodeType` takes the
registry the planner already holds and answers `descriptor.category == "system"`: the engine's last edge to a console
package goes with it, and `Engine.cpp` now includes `graph/rp_stage.h` itself, which used to arrive through
`HostServices.hpp`. `publishGraph` passes the `PlanCheck` that refuses a null slot after every node has activated; the
surviving `assert(e.core)` is a backstop, and its comment says so. `host/HostServices.hpp` keeps only `EngineHostIo`
(`rp.engine.host-io/3`), which Task 2 moves to `host-io`, and `SystemNodes.{hpp,cpp}` lose the template and the
console-neutral helpers to the package and the `SystemConfig` variant to the request. The four node types stay, each
with `static constexpr SystemBuildFn kBuild` naming its console's build function and a `config()` returning its own
struct, and the template's `activate` makes that config on the stack and hands its address across.

-// What every system node shares: the core it builds, its settings and params reaching that core, the connected-output
-// mask, its inputs, and prepare / step / finish mapped one to one onto the core's block triad. `Self` declares its
-// params (`gain` at least), supplies finish's lanes, may write output queues after the core has run (writeQueues), and
-// applies its own knobs (apply) and any param beyond the gain (applyParams).
-//
-// A node builds its core at activation from the bytes its resources hold (rp.host.systems/1,
-// docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 5). The core is the host's: the snapshot slot under the system id, the
-// live cores, and the delete when the node is destroyed. Which fields a build reads is rebuild_key's, the
-// construct-time fields among them.
-//
-// Only a new core rebuilds (rebuild_key): every other setting is a knob the node applies to the core it has, so its
-// prepare reads nothing a commit writes and setGraph never waits on a system node's commit (stateless_prepare). A
-// commit only points `settings` at the new settings (on_settings never allocates); the node applies what moved at the
-// start of its next block, before the core's prepareForBlock, and everything present once at activation, as it takes
-// or builds its core, before that core first runs. What the core was given is `applied`, a Settings::Applied, which is
-// the live knobs alone: the fields carrying a string (romName, sdRoot, the resource refs) all rebuild the node or move
-// a resource, which no application sees, so the copy the node makes when it applies a commit, on the block thread,
-// copies no string. So a setting lands at the node's next prepare, after every host command queued behind its plan
-// (the host drains its ring before it runs a block): a caller that must act on the restarted core renders a block
-// first, since a RAM write or staged core bytes sent after a model change reach the core it is about to replace. Each
-// knob is guarded twice, first by `moved` against what this node last applied, so a document's unchanged field is not
-// re-applied even where the core was changed by another path, then by the core's own setter where it has one
-// (setFastBoot and a NES's setRemoveSpriteLimit write unconditionally). A palette change re-applies the display group
-// and restarts nothing, while a model change restarts the core and a region change resets it
-// (docs/modular-graph-phase-c2-design.md section 4). A settings field the type does not know is ignored (node.hpp
-// reads with rfl::DefaultIfMissing and no rfl::NoExtraFields), so a misspelt knob plans and does nothing.
-//

-// prepareForBlock and after the settings (a model's restart first, then the levels), each value-guarded against the
-// value the core was given last: a publish carrying the value the core already has calls nothing. Every one is given
-// at the node's first block, before the core's first prepareForBlock: a node reads its params only in a block (the
-// host binds its control streams there, and lands the document's values in them as it adopts the plan), and a core a
-// node has built runs nothing before that. The first value is snapped into the core, whose gain smoother

-struct SystemNode {

-    static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<Applied>,

-    static auto rebuild_key(const Settings& s) { return s.key(); }
-    static constexpr bool stateless_prepare = true;
-
-    const HostSystems*                     systems = nullptr;  // null when the host offers no builder
-    const EngineSyncTrace*                 trace = nullptr;  // null when the host keeps none
-    Core*                                  core = nullptr;  // owned
-    std::array<std::uint8_t, kMaxOutputs>  connected{};
-    const Settings*                        settings = nullptr;  // the committed ones, alive until the next commit
-    Applied                                applied{};           // the live knobs the core was given last (none before)
-    bool                                   pending = false;     // settings committed and not yet applied
-    double                                 gainApplied = kUnapplied;  // the gain param's value the core has, in dB

-    SystemNode(const SystemNode&) = delete;
-    SystemNode& operator=(const SystemNode&) = delete;

-    // rp.stage/1: a message a host aimed at this node, straight into its core's ingress (Engine::stageNodeMidi's

- [ ] **Step 6: The plan check's seam, and the two script hosts that refuse the category**

`Planner.hpp` gains `PlanCheck` (a callable returning an optional `PlanError`) on `PlanInput`, and `Planner.cpp`'s
builder runs it in the `run()` chain after `linkedSteps()` and before `build()`, so a refusal goes through the
planner's own rollback. `GraphHost::setGraph` gains the fourth parameter and threads it into `planDocument`. Both
script hosts refuse a pack whose type's descriptor declares the category, before the registry sees a type:
`ScriptHost::loadInto` on the desktop path the engine's packs take, and `MqjsHost::openControl` on the device and
toolchain path, each with a comment pointing at the other.

/ `buildGbaCore` / `buildSmsCore`: the `SystemBuildFn` signature, the config cast from the request's `const void*` to
the package's own type, the ROM gates and the boot code moved verbatim, and Mesen's three private helpers became
file-local `build*System`. Each node type carries its `kBuild`. `SmsAudio.test.cpp` gains `system/InputTypes.hpp`,
which it used to reach through `SystemBase.hpp`: one of the two includes that only arrived transitively, which the

- [ ] **Step 8: The tests, and the fixture console**

The C4 kind matrix is retired from `EngineGraph.test.cpp` (the twelve-way document, its six `STATIC_REQUIRE`s,
`NodeRig::reportKind` and `KindWrapper`), and three cases replace it. The null-build refusal, `[b2][systems]`. The
fixture console, `[b2][systems]`: a test-only package (`rp.test.fixture`, types `rp.test.fixture-console` and
`rp.test.fixture-console-no-build`) whose node declares category `"system"`, reuses `system/SystemNode.hpp` over a
`StubCore` (silence, one stereo stream, counts blocks) and its own build function, is placed with
`Engine::addNodePackage`, planned as `sys-<id>` with its slot, run a block, and freed at the reclaim with
`StubCore::live == 0` - the engine builds, slots, runs and frees a console it has never heard of, with no engine edit
naming one. And the no-core refusal, which needs a fixture type that declares the category and never calls
`rp.host.systems/2` (`rp.test.fixture-console-no-core`): the document is refused with `sys-<id>: no-core: ...`,
nothing is claimed, the running system is the same pointer and still runs a block. `NodeRig` loses the factory,
`KindWrapper` and `reportKind`, and its `buildSystem` calls `request.build` (refusing a null one with the engine's
words, in the engine's order). `SystemNode.test.cpp`'s `[.][bench]` boot table holds one build lambda per console
(config and `SystemBuildFn`) instead of a variant, and copies the ROM into the request before `t0` so the timed region
is the console's build. `Planner.test.cpp` gains the check's own case (a `PlanCheck` refusing inside `plan()` destroys
the instances it activated; a calling check leaves them). `OfflineJobs.test.cpp` gains `system/HostSystems.hpp`'s
include. `ScriptPacks.test.cpp`'s refused case gains the definition that declares the category, and the pack fixture
beside it is the toolchain's half of the same refusal. **Watch all three fail first.** They were observed red against
the pre-change engine, and two of the red proofs are in `/tmp/f2pro`: `s1-red-fixture.log` (the fixture console,
`Filters: "*console package*"`: `REQUIRE( e.setGraph(...).ok )` with expansion `false`) and `s1-red-nullbuild.log`
(`Filters: "*names no build function*"`: the refusal's text came back as the slots error, `": slots: the slots and the
document's system nodes name different systems"`), both recorded before the recognition change. Step 12 reproduces
them on this tree, and the no-core case and the script-pack refusals too.
