````diff
+// A console package the test owns (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 8): a type that declares category
+// "system", on the system package's SystemNode template, over a stub core and a build function of its own. Nothing in
+// the engine names it; what places it is the descriptor, and what builds its core is the function its own request
+// carries.
+
+// What that console's build function reads from the request: the node's `tag` knob, so a case can hold that the config
+// its settings made reached its own build.
+struct FixtureConfig {
+    int tag = 0;
+};
+
+// The stub core: silence, and one stereo stream. The node zeroes the lanes before finishBlock, so this writes nothing,
+// and counts what it was asked so a case can hold that its triad ran.
+class StubCore final : public SystemBase {
+public:
+    StubCore(SystemId id, int tag) : SystemBase(id), tag_(tag) { ++live; }
+    ~StubCore() override { --live; }
+
+    void onActivate(double) override { activated_ = true; }
+    void onSampleRateChanged(double) override {}
+    std::vector<ChannelStream> channelLayout() const override { return {{"Mix", true}}; }
+    void finishBlock(const AudioBlockInfo&, float* const*, std::size_t) override { ++blocks_; }
+
+    int  tag() const { return tag_; }
+    bool activated() const { return activated_; }
+    int  blocks() const { return blocks_; }
+
+    // How many stub cores exist: a case holds that the host destroyed the one it built when its plan went.
+    static inline int live = 0;
+
+private:
+    int  tag_;
+    bool activated_ = false;
+    int  blocks_ = 0;
+};
+
+// The console's build: what every console's does, in a few lines. It reads its config, builds the core from it and
+// activates the core at the plan's rate, so the host gets the core exactly as an activated one is (SystemBuild.hpp).
+std::unique_ptr<SystemBase> buildFixtureCore(SystemId id, SystemBuildRequest&& request, double sampleRate,
+                                             std::string*) {
+    const auto* cfg = static_cast<const FixtureConfig*>(request.config);
+    auto core = std::make_unique<StubCore>(id, cfg ? cfg->tag : -1);
+    core->onActivate(sampleRate);
+    return core;
+}

+// The fixture console's settings: the shared fields a system node has, and the console's one construct-time knob.
+struct FixtureSettings {

+    rp::resource_ref<"sram">   sram;
+    rp::resource_ref<"state">  state;
+    std::optional<std::string> romName;

+
+    struct Key {

+        std::optional<std::string> romName;
+        std::optional<int>         tag;
+        bool operator==(const Key&) const = default;

+    struct Applied {};

+struct FixturePorts {
+    struct {
+        rp::bytes_in  serialIn;
+        rp::events_in midi;
+        rp::bytes_in  bytes;
+        rp::events_in buttons;
+    } inputs;
+    struct { rp::audio_out<rp::stereo> mix; } outputs;
+    struct { rp::host::GainParam gain; } params;
+};
+
+// One node type per build function the package offers: the console's, and one that names none, which is the request the
+// host refuses before a build.
+template <SystemBuildFn Build>
+struct FixtureConsole : rp::host::SystemNode<FixtureConsole<Build>, StubCore, FixtureSettings>, FixturePorts {
+    static constexpr const char* id = Build ? "rp.test.fixture-console" : "rp.test.fixture-console-no-build";
+    static constexpr const char* name = Build ? "Fixture console" : "Fixture console with no build";
+    static constexpr const char* category = "system";
+    static constexpr SystemBuildFn kBuild = Build;
+
+    // The console has one stream: the mix, as lanes 0 and 1.
+    std::size_t lanes(const rp::Block& b, std::array<float*, 2 * rp::host::kMaxOutputs>& out) const {
+        out[0] = b.output(0).u.audio.channels[0];
+        out[1] = b.output(0).u.audio.channels[1];
+        return 2;
+    }
+    static FixtureConfig config(const FixtureSettings& s) { return FixtureConfig{s.tag.value_or(0)}; }
+};
+
+// A node type that declares category "system" and builds nothing. The category is the promise the engine trusts (it
+// recognizes a system node by it and reads its core back from the plan's slot), so a type that never calls
+// rp.host.systems/2 is the promise broken, and the engine refuses the document rather than publish a plan whose slot for
+// it is null.
+struct NoCorePorts {
+    struct {} inputs;
+    struct { rp::audio_out<rp::stereo> mix; } outputs;
+    struct {} params;
+};
+
+struct FixtureConsoleWithoutCore : NoCorePorts {
+    struct Settings { std::uint64_t system = 0; };
+
+    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.fixture-console-no-core";
+    static constexpr const char* name = "Fixture console that builds nothing";
+    static constexpr const char* category = "system";
+    static constexpr const char* version = "1.0.0";
+
+    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {}
+};
+
+const rp_package* fixtureConsolePackage() {
+    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<FixtureConsole<buildFixtureCore>>(),
+                                                 rp::node_type<FixtureConsole<nullptr>>(),
+                                                 rp::node_type<FixtureConsoleWithoutCore>()};
+    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.test.fixture","version":"1.0.0"})",
+                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
+    return &kPackage;
+}

+TEST_CASE("a request that names no build function is refused with its own reason, claiming nothing",
+          "[engine-graph][b2][systems]") {
+    // The host builds what the request names, and a request that names no build function names no console: refused
+    // before the build, so the refusal costs no snapshot slot, no live id and no core
+    // (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 3). The fixture package's second type carries no build function,
+    // which is the one way a request reaches the host without one: only a node's activation calls buildSystem.
+    Engine e(kRate);
+    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(fixtureConsolePackage()));
+    const std::uint32_t rom = e.putResource("rom", readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH));
+    REQUIRE(rom != 0);
+    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(1, rp::host::test::kGbType, rom), {1})).ok);
+    SystemBase* running = e.findSystem(1);
+    REQUIRE(running != nullptr);
+    const std::size_t cores = e.liveSystemCount(), slots = e.registry().liveCount();
+
+    const auto r = e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(2, "rp.test.fixture-console-no-build", rom), {2}));
+    CHECK(refusal(r) == "sys-2: activate-failed: the request names no build function (rp.host.systems/2)");
+    CHECK_FALSE(e.coreLive(2));
+    CHECK(e.findSystem(1) == running);
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == cores);
+    CHECK(e.registry().liveCount() == slots);
+    CHECK(e.resourcePinCount(rom) == 1);  // the running plan's own node still holds it
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a console package the engine has never heard of plans, builds, runs and frees its core",
+          "[engine-graph][b2][systems]") {
+    // The category is the whole of what the engine knows about a system node (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md
+    // section 3): the fixture package is placed through the harness seam, its document names sys-<id> like any other
+    // system node, and the engine builds, slots, runs and frees the core with no engine edit naming the console.
+    Engine e(kRate);
+    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(fixtureConsolePackage()));
+    REQUIRE(StubCore::live == 0);
+    const std::uint32_t rom = e.putResource("rom", readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH));
+    REQUIRE(rom != 0);
+    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(1, "rp.test.fixture-console", rom, R"("tag":7)"), {1})).ok);
+
+    auto* core = dynamic_cast<StubCore*>(e.findSystem(1));
+    REQUIRE(core != nullptr);
+    CHECK(core->tag() == 7);     // the config its settings made reached its own build function
+    CHECK(core->activated());    // and the build activated it, as the contract says
+    CHECK(StubCore::live == 1);
+    CHECK(e.coreLive(1));
+    CHECK(e.registry().liveCount() == 1);
+
+    // A block runs it: the node's triad and finish reach the stub, and the lanes come back zeroed.
+    std::vector<float> lanes(2 * 256, 1.0f);
+    float* outs[2] = {&lanes[0], &lanes[256]};
+    e.processBlock(256, outs, 2);
+    CHECK(core->blocks() == 1);
+    CHECK(std::all_of(lanes.begin(), lanes.end(), [](float f) { return f == 0.0f; }));
+
+    // The reclaim frees it through the contract: the plan it ran in went with the empty document.
+    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(rp::host::test::stereoDocument({}), {})).ok);
+    e.reclaim();
+    CHECK_FALSE(e.coreLive(1));
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == 0);
+    CHECK(e.registry().liveCount() == 0);
+    CHECK(StubCore::live == 0);
+    CHECK(e.resourcePinCount(rom) == 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a type that declares category \"system\" and builds no core refuses the document, publishing nothing",
+          "[engine-graph][b2][systems]") {
+    // The promise the category signs (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 3): a system node builds its core
+    // through rp.host.systems/2 in its first activation, and the plan's slot for it is what the audio thread reads. A
+    // document that places a type which builds nothing is refused before the plan is published, unwinding what its
+    // nodes' activations built, and the plan already running is untouched. The document places a fixture console beside
+    // the broken type, so the sibling's core, slot and pin are what the refusal has to give back: a single no-core node
+    // would prove only that nothing was built.
+    Engine e(kRate);
+    REQUIRE(e.addNodePackage(fixtureConsolePackage()));
+    REQUIRE(StubCore::live == 0);
+    const std::uint32_t rom = e.putResource("rom", readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH));
+    REQUIRE(rom != 0);
+    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(builtRequest(builtDoc(1, rp::host::test::kGbType, rom), {1})).ok);
+    SystemBase* running = e.findSystem(1);
+    REQUIRE(running != nullptr);
+    const std::size_t cores = e.liveSystemCount(), slots = e.registry().liveCount();
+
+    const std::string res = "res:" + std::to_string(rom);
+    const std::string document =
+        R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sys-2","type":"rp.test.fixture-console","settings":{"system":2,"rom":")" + res +
+        R"("}},{"id":"sys-3","type":"rp.test.fixture-console-no-core","settings":{"system":3,"rom":")" + res +
+        R"("}},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+           "wires":[{"from":"sys-2.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"}]})";
+    const auto r = e.setGraph(builtRequest(document, {2, 3}));
+    CHECK(refusal(r) == "sys-3: no-core: declares category \"system\" and built no core: a system node builds its "
+                        "core through rp.host.systems/2 in its first activation");
+    // The sibling built, and the refusal unwound it: no core, no slot, no pin of its own.
+    CHECK_FALSE(e.coreLive(2));
+    CHECK(StubCore::live == 0);
+    CHECK_FALSE(e.coreLive(3));
+    CHECK(e.findSystem(1) == running);       // nothing of the refused plan was published
+    CHECK(e.liveSystemCount() == cores);
+    CHECK(e.registry().liveCount() == slots);  // nor did either node keep a snapshot slot
+    CHECK(e.resourcePinCount(rom) == 1);       // the running plan's node still holds its ROM
+
+    // The running plan runs a block, as it did.
+    std::vector<float> lanes(2 * 256, 0.0f);
+    float* outs[2] = {&lanes[0], &lanes[256]};
+    e.processBlock(256, outs, 2);
+}

+TEST_CASE("a PlanCheck's refusal destroys the instances the plan activated, inside plan()", "[graph][planner]") {
+    // Nothing a refused plan activated outlives plan(), which this holds: the instances die with ~Instance, and the
+    // Builder's own node list destroys any the fill never reached. The rollback's clear()/reset() run after that and are
+    // unobservable today (a refusal precedes the fill on every path that can error), so this is the contract, not the
+    // rollback line: the count would only move if ~Instance stopped destroying.
+    PlannerRig rig;
+    const auto parsed = parseGraphDocument(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"a","type":"rp.test.counted"},
+                                                        {"id":"b","type":"rp.test.counted"}],"wires":[]})");
+    REQUIRE(parsed.has_value());
+    const GraphDocument& document = parsed.value();
+    const int before = Counted::live;
+    // The check runs once every node has activated (Planner.hpp): the instances it refuses are the ones to unwind.
+    const PlanCheck refuse = []() -> std::optional<PlanError> {
+        return PlanError{"", "", "plan-check", "the engine's own check refused the plan"};
+    };
+    const PlanCheck accept = []() -> std::optional<PlanError> { return std::nullopt; };
+    // What GraphHost::planDocument fills: nothing live or in flight, since this plan follows none, and no rp_host, which
+    // rp.test.counted's create takes no use of (a node that did would read the null).
+    const std::map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<Instance>>      nothingLive;
+    const std::map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<FeedbackFront>> nothingFeedback;
+    PlanInput in;
+    in.doc = &document;
+    in.registry = &rig.registry;
+    in.resources = &rig.resources;
+    in.live = &nothingLive;
+    in.feedback = &nothingFeedback;
+    in.sampleRate = 48000.0;
+    in.maxFrames = 64;
+    in.check = &refuse;
+    const PlanOutcome refused = plan(in);
+    REQUIRE(refused.errors.size() == 1);
+    CHECK(refused.errors[0].code == "plan-check");
+    CHECK(refused.storage == nullptr);
+    CHECK(refused.instances.empty());
+    CHECK(Counted::live == before);
+    // The same document, its check accepting: both instances are the plan's and live until the outcome goes.
+    in.check = &accept;
+    {
+        const PlanOutcome accepted = plan(in);
+        REQUIRE(accepted.errors.empty());
+        CHECK(accepted.instances.size() == 2);
+        CHECK(Counted::live == before + 2);
+    }
+    CHECK(Counted::live == before);
+}
````

Create `packages/native/test/device-mode/script-packs/system-category/index.ts`:

````ts
// The system-category pack: one node whose descriptor declares category "system", which a native type alone may do. A
// system node builds a core through rp.host.systems/2 in its first activation, and a script node builds none, so the
// type would be lined up against a plan slot that stayed null (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 3). The
// MicroQuickJS host refuses it where a pack's types are registered (graph-runtime's MqjsHost::openControl), which the
// device-pack toolchain's run of every pack meets, so the toolchain refuses to build this pack: a test fixture of that
// refusal (packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake, cmake/refused-script-pack.cmake), never built by a product.
import { defineNode, events } from "@retroplug/core/defineNode";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "@retroplug/core/register";

export const coreNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.systemcategory.core",
  category: "system",
  ports: { out: events.out() },
  create: () => ({ process() {} }),
});

registerScriptNodes([coreNode]);
````

- [ ] **Step 9: The configure: the refusals, the test target, the Windows include root**

`cmake/refused-script-pack.cmake` is new: it runs the device-pack toolchain over a pack it must refuse and fails the
build when the toolchain compiles it, naming the host's own words. `packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake` gives it a
target, `retroplug-system-category-pack-refused`, a dependency of `retroplug-device-mode-test`, so `pnpm test:plugin`
runs it (a build step, so no suite's case or skip counts move); it also links `retroplug-system` into
`retroplug-graph-test`, which now reads `system/InputCapacity.hpp` from the package rather than the engine tree's
include root. The root `CMakeLists.txt` widens the clang-cl SameBoy command's header glob and its `-I` roots by the
package's three directories (the one Windows-side change this stage makes, reasoned and not run). `warnings.cmake`
puts `retroplug-system` on the `/W4 /WX` list, and `packages/native/CMakeLists.txt`'s header comment and the target
lists follow the moves.

Create `cmake/refused-script-pack.cmake`:

````cmake
# cmake -DNODE=<node> -DSCRIPT=<build-device-pack.mjs> -DENTRY=<index.ts> -DNAME=<pack> -DHEAP_BYTES=<n>
#       -DOUT=<dir> -DPACK_DIR=<dir> -DMQJS=<mqjs> -DRUNNER=<retroplug-mqjs-run> -P cmake/refused-script-pack.cmake:
# runs the device-pack toolchain over a pack it must refuse, and fails the build if it does not, naming the toolchain's
# own words. The toolchain is the fixture: a rule that stopped firing (a pack whose type promises a core it cannot build)
# would otherwise ship a node the engine lines up against a slot that stays null.
#
# It runs when the binary the pack is held for is built rather than at configure, because the toolchain needs the built
# mqjs compiler and runner (retroplug-mqjs-run) and Node.
foreach(_arg NODE SCRIPT ENTRY NAME HEAP_BYTES OUT PACK_DIR MQJS RUNNER)
    if(NOT ${_arg})
        message(FATAL_ERROR "refused-script-pack.cmake: pass -D${_arg}=<value>")
    endif()
endforeach()
execute_process(
    COMMAND "${NODE}" "${SCRIPT}" --entry "${ENTRY}" --name "${NAME}" --heap-bytes "${HEAP_BYTES}"
            --out-dir "${OUT}" --pack-dir "${PACK_DIR}" --mqjs "${MQJS}" --runner "${RUNNER}"
    RESULT_VARIABLE _result OUTPUT_VARIABLE _output ERROR_VARIABLE _output)
if(_result EQUAL 0)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "refused-script-pack.cmake: the toolchain compiled the ${NAME} pack; the MicroQuickJS host "
                        "must refuse a type whose descriptor declares category \"system\":\n${_output}")
endif()
set(_reason "declares category \"system\", and a script node cannot build a core")
string(FIND "${_output}" "${_reason}" _at)
if(_at EQUAL -1)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "refused-script-pack.cmake: the toolchain refused the ${NAME} pack, but not with "
                        "\"${_reason}\":\n${_output}")
endif()
message(STATUS "refused-script-pack.cmake: the toolchain refused the ${NAME} pack, as it must")
````

````diff
-### `SameBoyBackend`
+`Engine::buildSystem` runs on the control thread (heavy, non-RT) and refuses, in this order, a build outside the
+`setGraph` that activates the node, 0, an id above a system id, an id that is live, a request that names no build
+function, and a build that returns null (with its reason); only then does the snapshot slot get claimed, after the
+build has paid for its boot. The function it calls returns an **already-`onActivate`'d** system. The bytes come from the
+node's resources (its `build` copies them out of the pins its instance holds into the request, and the core takes them
+from there), so nothing on this path reads a file or decodes a role config.
+
+A system node is recognised by its descriptor: the type's `category` is `"system"`, read from the `NodeRegistry` the
+engine already holds for the planner, so `publishGraph` lines a document's `sys-<id>` nodes up against the plan's slots
+without naming a package. The category is a promise the engine holds the type to, since a slot's core is what the audio
+thread reads: a document whose plan leaves a slot without a core is refused before it is published (unwinding what its
+nodes' activations built, as a refused activation does), and a script pack's type may not declare the category at all,
+because a script node cannot build a core.
+
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f2pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````bash
F2 stage 1: the system package, and a core built by the function its node carries

The console-independent half of packages/native moves into a native-only
package, @retroplug/system, at the include paths it already had: SystemBase
and the capability interfaces, SystemId and the shared types, InputCapacity,
the transport triples with their seqlock, the MIDI event, and the core-only
utilities (Determinism, Gain, ExpSmoother, ProcessId). HostSystems
(rp.host.systems/2) and EngineSyncTrace split out of host/graph/HostServices.hpp
into it, and the generic SystemNode template with the console-neutral knob
helpers moves out of SystemNodes.cpp into a header, so the four node types left
there instantiate it rather than own it.

The build seam changes shape as the design's section 3 has it: a system node's
request carries the build function its own package exports and an opaque
pointer to the config its settings made, so Engine::buildSystem keeps its
bookkeeping (the live-id check, the snapshot claim, the plan's slot) and names
no console. A request naming no build function is refused with its own reason
before anything is claimed. SystemFactory, SystemBackend, CoreBackends,
registerCoreBackends, the SystemConfig variant, SystemKind, SystemBase::kind()
and the four cores' kKind are deleted; SameBoyBackend::build and
MesenBackend::build become the plain functions rp::sameboy::buildCore and
rp::mesen::buildNesCore / buildGbaCore / buildSmsCore, unchanged in what they
gate and boot. isSystemNodeType reads the registered type's descriptor category
instead of walking two packages by name.

Tests: the C4 kind matrix is retired with the kind check it held (the C4 design
carries a dated note), and two cases are added red-first - a request with no
build function, refused and claiming nothing, and a fixture console package the
engine has never heard of, whose category-"system" node plans, builds, slots,
runs and frees its stub core through addNodePackage with no engine edit naming
it. NodeRig and the build paths in SystemNode.test.cpp and EngineGraph.test.cpp
use the build functions directly.

Docs: spec/02's core-backends section becomes the build seam's, spec/01 stops
naming the factory, and every link to a moved or deleted file is fixed.

The category check lives where only the planner sees the moment. GraphHost::setGraph gained an optional PlanCheck
(Planner.hpp), which the planner runs in its chain after linkedSteps() and before build(), so a refusal takes the same
rollback a failed activation does and nothing is published: the running plan, its cores, its snapshot slots and its
pins are untouched. Engine::publishGraph passes one that walks the plan's table being filled and holds every
category-"system" slot to a built core. A script pack's type may not declare the category either, and each host refuses
it where its types register: ScriptHost::loadInto (the desktop path) parses each descriptor and refuses the pack before
the registry sees any of its types, and MqjsHost::openControl (the device and toolchain path) refuses the same one,
since a toolchain build compiles a pack's types through the other host.

The refused document's case places a fixture console beside the broken type, so the refusal has a sibling's core, slot
and pin to give back. Breaking the planner's rollback does not turn it red: GraphHost drops a refused PlanOutcome, and
the instances it holds release their cores as they are destroyed either way. Removing ~SystemNode's destroy is what the
case catches, which is what it holds.
````

### Task 2: the consoles, host I/O, the product order and the tests

Design sections 2, 7 and 9's second stage. `sameboy`, `mesen` and `host-io` leave the shell, `retroplug-core` dissolves,
and the product list is reordered so `mesen` sits after `n8`, which it now declares. The consoles keep their include text
and their file names (`system/sameboy/SameBoySystem.hpp`, `system/mesen/MesenNesSystem.hpp`, `host/graph/HostIoNodes.hpp`),
so almost every move is byte identical; the node types move out of `SystemNodes.cpp` into each package's own node file
(`SameBoyNode.cpp`, `MesenNode.cpp`), and the console knob helpers, the settings structs and the build functions go with
them. `mesen` declares `n8` - `NesN8FifoRole` includes its reliable-link header - and `rp.mesen.nes` reads the pack's
`kExpansionVolume*` constants, so the shell's copy and its `STATIC_REQUIRE`s go.

The test split is the stage's second half: `retroplug-audio-test`'s console files become `retroplug-sameboy-test` (7
cases) and `retroplug-mesen-test` (80, `engine-graph`'s `MesenShared` among them), `N8ReliableLink`'s sender-only cases
go to the N8 pack's own test binary (11) and the three from the emulated FIFO role on go to `mesen`'s, and the C++
helpers both need (`CountingAllocator`, `LinkRomModel.hpp`) go to a new native half of the `testing` package. The shell
keeps `EngineSampleRate`, `NesSplitRouting`, `EngineInvoker` and `Dither`: each drives a real `Engine`, which is the
shell's rule.

The stage's one re-record is `product-registrations.json`, and it is Step 7's own step. The review's findings shape three
parts of it: the boundary check gains a compile-definition rule and a `devDependency` door for a test's fixture file, a
configure guard keeps `retroplug-testing` out of every target that is no test binary, and the Game Boy logo the SMS gate
checks becomes `mesen`'s private copy (the stage first put one in `system`, and this tree has the per-package version).

- [ ] **Step 3: The three packages' manifests and CMakeLists**

`packages/host-io` is `@retroplug/host-io`: no TypeScript, one native item `{ "target": "retroplug-host-io", "entry":
"rp_host_io_package", "device": false }`, and `node-sdk` as its only dependency. Its library compiles
`HostIoNodes.cpp` and is where `rp.engine.host-io/3` lives; the include text stays `host/graph/...`, so `Engine.cpp`
and the tests include what they did. `sameboy`'s and `mesen`'s CMakeLists are the console packages':
`retroplug_package_library` over the package's sources, `src/` as the include root, links to `retroplug-system`,
`retroplug-node-sdk` and - for `sameboy` - the `sameboy` core, and for `mesen` - `retroplug-n8` and the third-party
`mesen`. `sameboy`'s carries the Windows `clang-cl` step behind `if(WIN32)` (the root CMakeLists' block is gone), with
its include roots rewritten to the package's own directories, the contract's and the node SDK's, its header glob over
the same, and its `DEPENDS` on the boot-ROM target. `packages/testing/native/CMakeLists.txt` is `retroplug-testing`:
an OBJECT library (`CountingAllocator.cpp`), because a replaced `operator new` in an archive member is never pulled
in, `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`, and a `src/` include root.

Create `packages/host-io/package.json`:

````json
{
  "name": "@retroplug/host-io",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "description": "The host's own I/O as node types: rp.host.midi-in and rp.host.midi-out, and the engine's rp.engine.host-io/3 service they read, with the staging bounds the engine sizes from them.",
  "dependencies": {
    "@retroplug/node-sdk": "workspace:*"
  },
  "retroplug": {
    "native": { "target": "retroplug-host-io", "entry": "rp_host_io_package", "device": false }
  }
}
````

Create `packages/host-io/native/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# The host-io pack's native half (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 2): the host's own I/O as node types,
# rp.host.midi-in and rp.host.midi-out, and the engine service they read (rp.engine.host-io/3, host/graph/HostServices.hpp)
# with the staging bounds the engine sizes its queues from. Added by retroplug_package(host-io) (cmake/packages.cmake).
#
# It depends on the node SDK alone and includes nothing of the shell's; the engine implements the service, and the
# engine's own translation unit reads the bounds, which is the shell's edge on this package and not this package's on the
# shell.
#
# Its include root is src/, and the include paths keep their text: "host/graph/HostIoNodes.hpp" and
# "host/graph/HostServices.hpp" are what the engine and the tests spell.

retroplug_package_library(retroplug-host-io
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/host/graph/HostIoNodes.cpp)
target_include_directories(retroplug-host-io PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-host-io PUBLIC retroplug-node-sdk)
````

Create `packages/mesen/native/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# The Mesen pack's native half (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 2): the NES, GBA and SMS/GG cores over the
# vendored `mesen` library, their configs, the global init and the NES debug session, the video and audio devices, the
# shared block tail, the emulated N8 FIFO and its reliable link role, the SMS sync role, the consoles' button tables and
# ROM gates, the three build functions their nodes' requests carry (rp.host.systems/2), and the three node types. Added by
# retroplug_package(mesen) (cmake/packages.cmake).
#
# It builds on the system package's contract and on the node SDK, and declares the N8 pack: NesN8FifoRole speaks
# BlipToaster's reliable link (transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp) from the cart's side, and rp.mesen.nes's expansion-volume
# bounds are the pack's (n8/N8Node.hpp), so the emulated chip and the real cart's register are set from one range. The
# edge runs one way: n8 imports neither this package nor the contract, and its TS names no console.
#
# Its include root is src/, and the include paths keep their text: "system/mesen/MesenNesSystem.hpp" and
# "debug/Cc65DbgParser.hpp" are what the sources and the engine's tests spell.

# --- retroplug-mesen: the rp_mesen_package entry and rp.mesen.nes / .gba / .sms
# (src/system/mesen/MesenNode.cpp), over the three systems and their build functions (src/system/mesen/MesenBackend.cpp).
retroplug_package_library(retroplug-mesen
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/MesenNesSystem.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/MesenGlobalInit.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/MesenNesDebugSession.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/MesenVideoDevice.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/MesenGbaSystem.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/MesenSmsSystem.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/roles/NesN8FifoRole.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/roles/SmsSyncRole.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/MesenBackend.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/mesen/MesenNode.cpp)
target_include_directories(retroplug-mesen PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-mesen
    PUBLIC  retroplug-system    # SystemBase, the capability interfaces, the build request, the host's system services
            retroplug-node-sdk  # graph/node.hpp, the authoring layer SystemNode instantiates
            retroplug-n8        # transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp (NesN8FifoRole), n8/N8Node.hpp's expansion-volume range
            mesen)              # deps/mesen: the emulator, and the headers MesenBlockOps and MesenBoot include

# --- the pack's test binary (cmake/test-binary.cmake), built by name; sources resolve against this directory.

# Guards what the three consoles compute without an Engine: the NES APU's flush window, the per-channel taps and the
# stereo-mod pins re-summing to the mix, the emulated N8 FIFO (its byte scheduling, the Edio status protocol, and the
# reliable-link role the N8 pack's sender talks to), the NES and SMS teardown survival, the SMS/GG boot, visible geometry
# and PSG, the GBA's firmware choice and block triad, the shared drain tail, and Mesen's own shared pieces this fork
# patches for the block thread. Every case builds its core (or its role) directly, so this binary links no shell target;
# the sender's half of the reliable link is the N8 pack's own test binary's. Run by `pnpm test:plugin`.
retroplug_add_test_binary(
    NAME     retroplug-mesen-test
    SOURCES  test/NesApuLatency.test.cpp         # runtime NES APU flush window (live apuLatencyMs knob)
             test/NesN8FifoTiming.test.cpp       # host MIDI-in keeps its intra-block offset into the N8 FIFO
             test/NesEverdriveFifo.test.cpp      # Edio status protocol leaves no stale byte to desync MIDI parsing
             test/NesStems.test.cpp              # NES stereo-mod pins re-sum to the mix (spec/10 step 5)
             test/NesTeardown.test.cpp           # the NES twin of SMS's construct/destruct guard
             test/SmsAudio.test.cpp              # SMS/GG boot, visible geometry, non-silent PSG, teardown survival
             test/GbaFirmware.test.cpp           # each GBA system loads ITS bios, not whichever landed last
             test/GbaAudio.test.cpp              # the GBA block triad terminates and fills a block
             test/MesenBlockOps.test.cpp         # the shared drain tail blanks a short ring
             test/MesenShared.test.cpp           # ClearState's empty state, and the notification dispatch's copy
             test/N8ReliableLink.test.cpp        # the emulated cart FIFO's side of the reliable link
    LIBS     retroplug-mesen                    # the consoles, their roles, and mesen's own headers
             retroplug-testing                  # CountingAllocator, and LinkRomModel.hpp: the ROM's link rules
    DEFS     RP_BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PATH="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/roms/bliptoaster.nes"
             RP_SMS_ROM_PATH="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/roms/smsggdj_v0_45.sms"
             RP_GG_ROM_PATH="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/roms/smsggdj_v0_45.gg")
````

````cmake
# The SameBoy pack's native half (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 2): the Game Boy core, its config and
# boot ROMs, the Game Boy button table, its ROM gate, the build function rp.sameboy.gb's request carries
# (rp.host.systems/2), and the node type itself. Added by retroplug_package(sameboy) (cmake/packages.cmake). It builds on
# the system package's contract (SystemBase, the build request and function, the host's system services, the SystemNode
# template) and on the node SDK, which the template is written in; it links no shell target.
#
# Its include root is src/, and the include paths keep their text: "system/sameboy/SameBoySystem.hpp" is what the
# engine's tests and the node's own translation unit spell, as it was before the carve.

# --- retroplug-sameboy: the rp_sameboy_package entry and rp.sameboy.gb (src/system/sameboy/SameBoyNode.cpp), over
# SameBoySystem (the core), SameBoyBackend (the build function) and the boot ROMs sameboy_bootroms generates into the
# build tree (cmake/sameboy_bootroms.cmake, included by cmake/sameboy.cmake). The manifest entry is not `device`: a Game
# Boy builds on a desktop host's control thread, and nothing of this tree is a device build's.
if(WIN32)
    # SameBoySystem.cpp #defines GB_INTERNAL to reach SameBoy's internal struct view and GNU-extension headers, which MSVC
    # cl.exe cannot parse, so on Windows clang-cl (MSVC-ABI) compiles it into retroplug-samebsys and this library links
    # that. Elsewhere the source compiles in place. The one RetroPlug C++ that needs the internal view (verified with
    # rpc-schema-dump -k 0); everything else compiles under cl.exe because GB_INTERNAL is PRIVATE to the sameboy target.
    find_program(RP_CLANG_CL clang-cl
        HINTS "$ENV{VCINSTALLDIR}Tools/Llvm/x64/bin"
              "C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Community/VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin"
        REQUIRED)
    set(_sb_src "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/sameboy/SameBoySystem.cpp")
    set(_sb_obj "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/sameboy-clang/SameBoySystem.cpp.obj")
    # A custom command gets no header scan, so it rebuilds on the headers listed here and nothing else. A stale object is
    # not a slow build but a crash: change a class layout or a vtable (SystemBase's virtuals) and the MSVC objects agree on
    # the new one while this one keeps the old, every slot after the change off by one. These are the trees its includes
    # reach: the console's own, the contract it implements (system/, transport/, util/), the node SDK's util/
    # (util/FixedQueue.hpp) and sameboy's Core headers; the boot-ROM headers sameboy_bootroms generates come with
    # DEPENDS below, which orders them before this command but does not list them as inputs.
    file(GLOB _sb_headers CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/sameboy/*.hpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/system/native/src/system/*.hpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/system/native/src/transport/*.hpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/system/native/src/util/*.hpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/node-sdk/native/src/util/*.hpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/deps/sameboy/Core/*.h")
    add_custom_command(
        OUTPUT "${_sb_obj}"
        COMMAND "${RP_CLANG_CL}" /nologo /c /MT /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG /EHsc /std:c++20 /Zc:__cplusplus
            "/FI${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/sameboy-clang/sameboy_version.h"
            # GB_DISABLE_* MUST match the sameboy core or GB_gameboy_t's layout diverges.
            -DGB_DISABLE_TIMEKEEPING -DGB_DISABLE_DEBUGGER
            -DNOMINMAX -DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN -DNOGDI -D_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS
            "-I${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src"                    # the console: system/sameboy/
            "-I${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/system/native/src"     # the contract: system/, transport/, util/
            "-I${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/node-sdk/native/src"   # util/FixedQueue.hpp
            "-I${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/deps/sameboy/Core"
            "-I${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/generated"
            "-I${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/_deps/reflectcpp-src/include"
            "/Fo${_sb_obj}" "${_sb_src}"
        DEPENDS "${_sb_src}" ${_sb_headers} sameboy_bootroms
        COMMENT "clang-cl (sameboy) SameBoySystem.cpp"
        VERBATIM)
    add_library(retroplug-samebsys STATIC "${_sb_obj}")
    set_target_properties(retroplug-samebsys PROPERTIES LINKER_LANGUAGE CXX)
    set(_sb_sources "")
else()
    list(APPEND _sb_sources "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/sameboy/SameBoySystem.cpp")
endif()

retroplug_package_library(retroplug-sameboy
    ${_sb_sources}
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/sameboy/SameBoyBackend.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/system/sameboy/SameBoyNode.cpp)
target_include_directories(retroplug-sameboy PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-sameboy
    PUBLIC  retroplug-system     # SystemBase, the build request and function, the SystemNode template's contract
            retroplug-node-sdk   # graph/node.hpp, the authoring layer SystemNode instantiates
            sameboy              # deps/sameboy: the emulator, and the boot ROM headers sameboy_bootroms generates
    )
# On Windows the core's source is the clang-cl object above; a PUBLIC dependency, so nothing else has to remember it.
if(WIN32)
    target_link_libraries(retroplug-sameboy PUBLIC retroplug-samebsys)
endif()

# --- the pack's test binary (cmake/test-binary.cmake), built by name; sources resolve against this directory.

# Guards the Game Boy's audio path: the four per-channel taps and the mix they re-sum to, the serial port's capture
# timing against the host's MIDI-in, and every SameBoyModel (SGB variants included) booting and rendering. No Engine:
# each case builds the core the build function would (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 8), so this binary
# links no shell target. Run by `pnpm test:plugin`.
retroplug_add_test_binary(
    NAME     retroplug-sameboy-test
    SOURCES  test/SameBoyStems.test.cpp
             test/SameBoySerialTiming.test.cpp   # host MIDI-in keeps its intra-block sample offset over serial
             test/SameBoyModels.test.cpp         # every SameBoyModel boots + renders
    LIBS     retroplug-sameboy
    DEFS     RP_MGB_ROM_PATH="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/roms/mGB.gb")
````

Create `packages/testing/native/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# The native half of @retroplug/testing: what test binaries of more than one package share, so no test binary reaches
# another package's test tree (this package's ts/ tree is the TS harness's half). Added by retroplug_package(testing)
# (cmake/packages.cmake), which no product lists: a test binary takes it through its package's devDependency on
# @retroplug/testing, and the native boundary check reads the same devDependencies.
#
# An OBJECT library, not a static one: CountingAllocator.cpp replaces the global operator new and delete, and an archive
# member is linked only when it answers an undefined symbol, which an allocation never does. Every object goes into each
# binary that links the target.
#
# src/ is the include root, so the helpers keep the paths they are included by ("graph/CountingAllocator.hpp") wherever
# a test sits. LinkRomModel.hpp is header-only: the reliable link's ROM rules, driven by both halves' test binaries
# (the N8 pack's and the Mesen package's).
#
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL: nothing the default build needs links it (only test binaries, which are built by name), and a library
# that did would be refused by the configure (retroplug_check_test_helpers). A test binary that links it still builds it.
add_library(retroplug-testing OBJECT EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/graph/CountingAllocator.cpp)
set_target_properties(retroplug-testing PROPERTIES
    CXX_STANDARD 20
    CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON
    POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)
# PUBLIC: the helpers keep the paths they are included by, in the library's own source and in every test binary's.
target_include_directories(retroplug-testing PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
if(MSVC)
    target_compile_options(retroplug-testing PRIVATE $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:/bigobj>)
endif()
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <span>

namespace rp::sameboy {

// The Game Boy cartridge logo: the 48 bytes at $0104 that every licensed (and most unlicensed) cartridge carries
// verbatim, because the boot ROM refuses to start without them.
inline constexpr std::size_t kGameBoyLogoOffset = 0x104;
inline constexpr std::uint8_t kGameBoyLogo[48] = {
    0xCE, 0xED, 0x66, 0x66, 0xCC, 0x0D, 0x00, 0x0B, 0x03, 0x73, 0x00, 0x83, 0x00, 0x0C, 0x00, 0x0D,
    0x00, 0x08, 0x11, 0x1F, 0x88, 0x89, 0x00, 0x0E, 0xDC, 0xCC, 0x6E, 0xE6, 0xDD, 0xDD, 0xD9, 0x99,
    0xBB, 0xBB, 0x67, 0x63, 0x6E, 0x0E, 0xEC, 0xCC, 0xDD, 0xDC, 0x99, 0x9F, 0xBB, 0xB9, 0x33, 0x3E,
};

// Whether `bytes` are a Game Boy cartridge: the Nintendo logo where a cartridge puts it ($0104), which every licensed
// (and most unlicensed) cart carries because the boot ROM refuses to start without it. Magic bytes rather than the file
// extension, so a mislabelled .gb that is really a .nes is refused here rather than fed to the core as garbage. The
// embedded mGB passes: it carries a cart's logo (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 3).
inline bool isGameBoyRom(std::span<const std::uint8_t> bytes) {
    if (bytes.size() < kGameBoyLogoOffset + sizeof kGameBoyLogo) return false;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < sizeof kGameBoyLogo; ++i)
        if (bytes[kGameBoyLogoOffset + i] != kGameBoyLogo[i]) return false;
    return true;
}

}  // namespace rp::sameboy
````

````cpp
// rp.sameboy.gb, the Game Boy as a node (docs/modular-graph-phase-b1-design.md section 3.1, and
// docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 2 for the package it lives in): the node adapts SameBoySystem, builds
// its own core at activation from the ROM and seed resources its settings name (rp.host.systems/2,
// docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md), and carries its own package's build function (rp::sameboy::buildCore) in the
// request, so the host that runs it names no console.
//
// Its settings are the fields the type reads and nothing else: the system it names, the resources its core is built
// from, and the Game Boy's knobs (docs/modular-graph-phase-c2-design.md section 3), each applied to the core the node
// has, or - the model, the fast boot and the display group - a rebuild. The settings and the console's knob helpers are
// this package's, and the generic ones are the system package's (system/SystemNode.hpp).

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <iterator>
#include <optional>
#include <span>
#include <string>
#include <utility>

#include "graph/node.hpp"
#include "system/InputCapacity.hpp"
#include "system/SystemNode.hpp"
#include "system/sameboy/SameBoyBackend.hpp"
#include "system/sameboy/SameBoyConfig.hpp"
#include "system/sameboy/SameBoySystem.hpp"

namespace rp::host {

namespace {

using namespace rp::host::knobs;  // Within, Label, valueOf and moved: the system package's generic helpers

// The Game Boy's own knob helper, beside the node whose settings read it: the light temperature's range, which is
// SameBoy's own (applyDisplayConfig clamps to it). The generic helpers are the system package's
// (system/SystemNode.hpp). This unnamed namespace rather than `knobs` itself, which every package reaches: a type two
// packages defined differently would be an ODR violation no linker reports.
struct LightTemperatureRange {
    static constexpr double min = -1.0, max = 1.0;
};

using LightTemperature = rfl::Validator<double, Within<LightTemperatureRange>>;

struct GameBoySettings {
    std::uint64_t                             system = 0;
    rp::resource_ref<"rom">                   rom;
    rp::resource_ref<"sram">                  sram;
    rp::resource_ref<"state">                 state;
    std::optional<std::string>                romName;
    std::optional<knobs::Label<SameBoyModel>>           model;
    std::optional<bool>                                 fastBoot;
    std::optional<knobs::Label<SameBoyHighpass>>        highpass;
    std::optional<knobs::Label<SameBoyColorCorrection>> colorCorrection;
    std::optional<knobs::Label<SameBoyDmgPalette>>      dmgPalette;
    std::optional<LightTemperature>                     lightTemperature;
    // What the core captures of its serial port for LSDj's decoder: "listen" for master sync, "drive" for MI.OUT.
    std::optional<knobs::Label<SerialOutCapture>>       serialOutCapture;

    // What a rebuild is decided by: which system the node names, and every field the build reads (the resource refs are
    // not here: node.hpp rebuilds a moved ref by itself).
    struct Key {
        std::uint64_t              system = 0;
        std::optional<std::string> romName;
        bool operator==(const Key&) const = default;
    };
    Key key() const { return {system, romName}; }

    // The live knobs alone, which is what the node's `applied` holds (SystemNode::Applied says why).
    struct Applied {
        std::optional<knobs::Label<SameBoyModel>>           model;
        std::optional<bool>                                 fastBoot;
        std::optional<knobs::Label<SameBoyHighpass>>        highpass;
        std::optional<knobs::Label<SameBoyColorCorrection>> colorCorrection;
        std::optional<knobs::Label<SameBoyDmgPalette>>      dmgPalette;
        std::optional<LightTemperature>                     lightTemperature;
        std::optional<knobs::Label<SerialOutCapture>>       serialOutCapture;
    };
    Applied liveKnobs() const {
        return {model, fastBoot, highpass, colorCorrection, dmgPalette, lightTemperature, serialOutCapture};
    }
};

// The Game Boy's serialOut: a byte a message. While MI.OUT capture clocks the port (external clock, SC=0x80:
// SameBoySystem::writeAudioSample shifts one bit an audio frame) a byte takes eight frames, so the largest block a host
// can run (rp::graph::kMaxBlockFrames, 65536 frames; the plugin grows its plan to its buffer size) carries 8192. The
// other 64 are slack for what a block adds to that: up to 7 bits carried in from the block before, and the frames the
// core runs past its target (an instruction at a time, so rarely more than one; 64 bytes is 512 frames of it). Fixed
// rather than sized from the plan's block size, so a feedback wire from it would keep its front across every plan swap
// (no document places one). A Game Boy that clocks the port itself (internal clock, SC=0x81) shifts at its serial rate
// instead, and a CGB on its fast clock (32768 bytes a second, about 0.7 a frame at 48 kHz, twice that in double speed)
// can outrun this in a block past about 12000 frames (about 6000 in double speed): what does not fit is dropped and
// counted (GraphHost::droppedMessages), never lost silently.
constexpr rp::capacity kSerialOutCapacity{.messages = rp::kSerialOutInput.messages,
                                          .bytes = rp::kSerialOutInput.bytes};

struct GameBoy : SystemNode<GameBoy, SameBoySystem, GameBoySettings> {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.sameboy.gb";
    static constexpr const char* name = "Game Boy";
    static constexpr const char* category = "system";
    // The Game Boy's build: the package's own, which the node's request carries to rp.host.systems/2.
    static constexpr SystemBuildFn kBuild = rp::sameboy::buildCore;
    struct {
        rp::link      link;
        rp::bytes_in  serialIn;
        rp::events_in midi;
        rp::bytes_in  bytes;
        rp::events_in buttons;
    } inputs;
    struct {
        rp::audio_out<rp::stereo>                mix;
        rp::audio_out<rp::stereo>                ch1;
        rp::audio_out<rp::stereo>                ch2;
        rp::audio_out<rp::stereo>                ch3;
        rp::audio_out<rp::stereo>                ch4;
        rp::bytes_out::sized<kSerialOutCapacity> serialOut;
    } outputs;
    struct { GainParam gain; } params;
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kSerialOut = 5;  // its output index

    // The four stems (8 lanes) once any is connected, else the mix (2): finishBlock's two lane counts.
    std::size_t lanes(const rp::Block& b, std::array<float*, 2 * kMaxOutputs>& out) const {
        if (!(connected[1] || connected[2] || connected[3] || connected[4])) return mixLanes(b, out);
        for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < 4; ++k) {
            out[2 * k] = b.output(1 + k).u.audio.channels[0];
            out[2 * k + 1] = b.output(1 + k).u.audio.channels[1];
        }
        return 8;
    }

    // MI.OUT and master sync (section 3.2 of docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md): the bytes the core captured on
    // its serial port this block, each at the frame the core completed it: rp.lsdj.serial-out sends each message it
    // decodes at its completing byte's frame (docs/lsdj-serial-out-design.md), and times master sync's stop from the
    // newest byte's (docs/lsdj-master-sync-fix-design.md). A stamp can lie at or past the block's end two ways: the
    // core runs an instruction at a time, so it can complete a byte past the block's end, and the drive path counts
    // the frame before it captures (SameBoySystem::writeAudioSample), so its stamps run 1..frames and a byte
    // completed in the block's last sample is stamped `frames`. Either is stamped at the block's last frame, so a
    // block's messages always lie inside it. Copied, not drained: the core clears the log at its next prepareForBlock.
    void writeQueues(std::uint32_t frames) noexcept {
        if (!connected[kSerialOut]) return;
        for (const auto& entry : core->serialOutLog_)
            outputs.serialOut.push(std::min(entry.first, frames - 1), std::span<const std::uint8_t>(&entry.second, 1));
    }

    // The coupled group's other members, in member order: the cable the serial callbacks read and write. linkPeers_
    // reserves 8, so a cable of up to 9 Game Boys never allocates here.
    void set_peers(std::span<rp_node* const> peers) noexcept {
        core->linkPeers_.clear();
        for (rp_node* p : peers)
            if (GameBoy* gb = rp::peer_as<GameBoy>(p)) core->linkPeers_.push_back(gb->core);
    }

    // The config the core is built with: every knob the settings carry, the model and the fast boot among them, which
    // the build applies before onActivate, so a loaded non-default model boots as that model and never restarts
    // afterwards. A knob absent from the settings keeps SameBoyConfig's default, which is the role schema's.
    static SameBoyConfig config(const Settings& s) {
        SameBoyConfig c;
        if (s.model) c.model = knobs::valueOf<SameBoyModel>(*s.model);
        if (s.fastBoot) c.fastBoot = *s.fastBoot;
        if (s.highpass) c.highpass = knobs::valueOf<SameBoyHighpass>(*s.highpass);
        if (s.colorCorrection) c.colorCorrection = knobs::valueOf<SameBoyColorCorrection>(*s.colorCorrection);
        if (s.dmgPalette) c.dmgPalette = knobs::valueOf<SameBoyDmgPalette>(*s.dmgPalette);
        if (s.lightTemperature) c.lightTemperature = s.lightTemperature->value();
        return c;
    }

    // The capture mode is not part of SameBoyConfig: the core takes it through its own setter, so the build did not
    // apply it and the node's own first application must.
    void configApplied(Applied& a) const noexcept { a.serialOutCapture.reset(); }

    // The fast boot first, which waits for the next restart and so is what a model's restart boots with: a block that
    // carries both (several documents published between two blocks commit together) restarts on the new fast boot,
    // where making the edits one at a time would not have when the fast boot was published after the model. Then the
    // rest in the order the store's role config lists them, the capture last. The capture lands at the start of the
    // first block
    // of the plan that carries it, the block rp.lsdj.serial-out first runs in its new mode, so no byte captured in one
    // mode is decoded in the other.
    void apply(const Settings& to, const Applied& from) noexcept {
        if (knobs::moved(to.fastBoot, from.fastBoot)) core->setFastBoot(*to.fastBoot);
        if (knobs::moved(to.model, from.model)) core->setModel(knobs::valueOf<SameBoyModel>(*to.model));
        if (knobs::moved(to.highpass, from.highpass))
            core->setHighpass(knobs::valueOf<SameBoyHighpass>(*to.highpass));
        if (knobs::moved(to.colorCorrection, from.colorCorrection))
            core->setColorCorrection(knobs::valueOf<SameBoyColorCorrection>(*to.colorCorrection));
        if (knobs::moved(to.dmgPalette, from.dmgPalette))
            core->setDmgPalette(knobs::valueOf<SameBoyDmgPalette>(*to.dmgPalette));
        if (knobs::moved(to.lightTemperature, from.lightTemperature))
            core->setLightTemperature(to.lightTemperature->value());
        if (knobs::moved(to.serialOutCapture, from.serialOutCapture))
            core->setSerialOutCapture(knobs::valueOf<SerialOutCapture>(*to.serialOutCapture));
    }
};

// No declaration of this leaves the translation unit: the package's only public name is the `extern "C"` entry its
// manifest names.
const rp_package* sameboyPackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<GameBoy>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.sameboy","version":"1.0.0"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

}  // namespace

}  // namespace rp::host

// The package's entry, named in packages/sameboy/package.json: what a product's generated registration calls
// (rp_register_packages, graph/Packages.hpp).
extern "C" const rp_package* rp_sameboy_package(void) { return rp::host::sameboyPackage(); }
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

// The Mesen consoles' button identifiers, one table per console, each keyed by the wire byte SystemBase::pressButton
// takes. Every table is position-aligned with the others (Right=0, ..., Start=7) so the CLI's script parser and the JS
// bridge use one name table and each console reinterpret the byte; a byte outside a table drives no bit at all rather
// than falling through onto one.

// NES controller buttons. Mesen's own NesController::Buttons is ordered {Up=0, Down, Left, Right, Start, Select, B, A,
// Microphone} (deps/mesen/Core/NES/Input/NesController.h:80), so the remap in MesenNesSystem is an explicit switch
// rather than a cast.
enum class NesButton : std::uint8_t {
    Right  = 0,
    Left   = 1,
    Up     = 2,
    Down   = 3,
    A      = 4,
    B      = 5,
    Select = 6,
    Start  = 7,
    Count  = 8,
};

// GBA buttons. L and R are the Game Boy Advance's alone and live at the end of the table. Mesen's own
// GbaController::Buttons has a different order (Up=0, Down=1, Left=2, Right=3, Start=4, Select=5, B=6, A=7, L=8, R=9:
// deps/mesen/Core/GBA/Input/GbaController.h), so MesenGbaSystem does the explicit remap from this wire byte as it
// applies its queue.
enum class GbaButton : std::uint8_t {
    Right  = 0,
    Left   = 1,
    Up     = 2,
    Down   = 3,
    A      = 4,
    B      = 5,
    Select = 6,
    Start  = 7,
    L      = 8,
    R      = 9,
    Count  = 10,
};

// Master System / Game Gear buttons: a d-pad and two face buttons, so the shared table's last two bytes carry two
// consequences:
//
//   Select has no hardware equivalent at all. MesenSmsSystem::pressButton drops it rather than folding it onto a face
//   button, or a Select tap would spuriously fire button 2.
//
//   Start is not a pad button on either machine. On Master System it is the console's Pause switch, which drives the
//   Z80 NMI (deps/mesen/Core/SMS/SmsVdp.cpp:600-602); on Game Gear the same bit reads as Start at port $00 bit 7
//   (SmsMemoryManager.cpp:456-464). One wire byte, two behaviours, which is why the settings UI labels it per platform.
//
// Mesen's own SmsController::Buttons is ordered {Up=0, Down, Left, Right, B, A, Pause}
// (deps/mesen/Core/SMS/Input/SmsController.h:58), so the remap in MesenSmsSystem is an explicit switch, not a cast.
enum class SmsButton : std::uint8_t {
    Right  = 0,
    Left   = 1,
    Up     = 2,
    Down   = 3,
    A      = 4,
    B      = 5,
    Select = 6,   // no SMS/GG equivalent; dropped at apply time
    Start  = 7,   // -> Pause (SMS: NMI; GG: Start)
    Count  = 8,
};
````

````cpp
// Whether `bytes` carry the logo where a cartridge puts it, which no Mesen console runs. A buffer too short to hold it
// carries none.
inline bool carriesGameBoyLogo(std::span<const std::uint8_t> bytes) {
    if (bytes.size() < kGameBoyLogoOffset + sizeof kGameBoyLogo) return false;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < sizeof kGameBoyLogo; ++i)
        if (bytes[kGameBoyLogoOffset + i] != kGameBoyLogo[i]) return false;
    return true;
}

// iNES: 'N','E','S',0x1A at offset 0.
inline bool isNesRom(std::span<const std::uint8_t> bytes) {
    return bytes.size() >= 4 && bytes[0] == 'N' && bytes[1] == 'E' && bytes[2] == 'S' && bytes[3] == 0x1A;
}

// The GBA Nintendo logo at $0004..$009F: every licensed cart contains these bytes verbatim, since the boot ROM
// CRC-checks them and refuses to start the cart otherwise. The first 32 are unique enough to use as a signature; the
// full logo is 156 bytes.
inline bool isGbaRom(std::span<const std::uint8_t> bytes) {
    static constexpr std::uint8_t kGbaLogo[] = {
        0x24, 0xFF, 0xAE, 0x51, 0x69, 0x9A, 0xA2, 0x21, 0x3D, 0x84, 0x82, 0x0A, 0x84, 0xE4, 0x09, 0xAD,
        0x11, 0x24, 0x8B, 0x98, 0xC0, 0x81, 0x7F, 0x21, 0xA3, 0x52, 0xBE, 0x19, 0x93, 0x09, 0xCE, 0x20,
    };
    constexpr std::size_t kOffset = 0x04;
    if (bytes.size() < kOffset + sizeof kGbaLogo) return false;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < sizeof kGbaLogo; ++i)
        if (bytes[kOffset + i] != kGbaLogo[i]) return false;
    return true;
}

// Sega 8-bit: "TMR SEGA" at the END of a bank rather than at the file start. $7FF0 is the usual spot; $1FF0/$3FF0 are
// where an 8 KB/16 KB cart puts it. Each is doubled by the +$200 copier-header variant Mesen strips at load
// (SmsConsole.cpp: `(size % 0x400) == 0x200`), which boots fine, so it classifies too. This covers BOTH Sega machines:
// nothing here re-decides Master System vs Game Gear, which is TS's policy (platform.ts weighs the header's region
// nibble against the file extension). Unlike the Nintendo logos this magic is required by no boot ROM, so plenty of
// homebrew omits it, which is why buildSmsCore accepts a ROM that carries none of them.
inline bool isSegaRom(std::span<const std::uint8_t> bytes) {
    static constexpr std::uint8_t kSegaMagic[] = {'T', 'M', 'R', ' ', 'S', 'E', 'G', 'A'};
    constexpr std::size_t kCopierSkip = 0x200;
    constexpr std::size_t kBases[] = {0x7FF0, 0x3FF0, 0x1FF0};
    for (const std::size_t base : kBases) {
        for (const std::size_t off : {base, base + kCopierSkip}) {
            if (bytes.size() < off + sizeof kSegaMagic) continue;
            bool match = true;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < sizeof kSegaMagic; ++i)
                if (bytes[off + i] != kSegaMagic[i]) {
                    match = false;
                    break;
                }
            if (match) return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

}  // namespace rp::mesen
````

Create `packages/testing/native/src/LinkRomModel.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The two halves of BlipToaster's reliable link test (transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp): the ROM's own rules as a model the
// sender can be driven against, and the little frame arithmetic a case compares the wire with. The sender's half of the
// link is the N8 pack's, and the emulated cart FIFO that speaks it from the other side is the Mesen package's
// (system/mesen/roles/NesN8FifoRole.hpp), so the model lives here, in the test helper library, and both test binaries
// link it: the pack's own and the Mesen package's, which declares n8.
//
// Why HERE and not in the N8 pack: the model sits on both sides of the mesen/n8 edge, and a door in n8 for it would be a
// second mechanism for one header (n8's tests reach it through n8, mesen's through testing, and a test-support target in
// n8 would also have to be declared a devDependency by mesen beside the n8 dependency it needs for the FIFO role). One
// helper library both test binaries already link is the smaller thing.
//
// The ROM half is pinned in the BlipToaster repo (retroplug-cli/tests/link.test.ts); here the model stands in for it so
// the sender can be driven through a LOSSY channel shaped like the real one: on NTSC a DMC-DMA halt on `lda $40F0`
// repeats the read and the N8 FIFO pops a byte per read, so 1-3 consecutive bytes vanish. The property that matters is
// exact: whatever is lost, the ROM ends up applying every message once, in order.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <initializer_list>
#include <vector>

namespace rp::n8::test {

using Bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;

// The ROM's link rules (bliptoaster src/midi/main.c), as a byte-at-a-time parser. `applied` collects the messages it
// would act on; ack() reports what it would write on the back-channel when its FIFO runs empty.
struct RomModel {
    bool         linkOn = false;
    std::uint8_t next   = 0;
    bool         dirty  = false;
    enum { Idle, WantSync, WantSeq, InMsg, WantSum } st = Idle;
    std::uint8_t seq = 0;
    std::uint8_t last = 0x7F;   // the last frame header read
    unsigned     sum = 0;
    std::size_t  need = 0;   // message length incl. status; 0 = a SysEx (to F7)
    Bytes        buf;
    std::vector<Bytes> applied;

    // A frame damaged after its seq: the ROM reports the frame it expects as the last one read, since a damaged
    // frame's seq cannot be trusted (frame_hdr's damaged exit).
    void bad() { if (st == InMsg || st == WantSum) last = next; st = Idle; dirty = true; }

    void byte(std::uint8_t b) {
        if (b >= 0xF8) return;                                          // real-time: skipped (0xFF panic not modelled)
        switch (st) {
            case WantSync:
                if (b & 0x80) { st = Idle; byte(b); return; }
                linkOn = true;
                next = b; last = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((b - 1) & 0x7F); dirty = true; st = Idle;
                return;
            case WantSeq:
                // header cut short: the expected frame, damaged
                if (b & 0x80) { last = next; bad(); byte(b); return; }
                seq = b; last = b; sum = b; buf.clear(); st = InMsg; return;
            case InMsg:
                if (buf.empty()) {
                    if (!(b & 0x80)) { bad(); return; }                 // the status was lost
                    if (b == 0xF4 || b == 0xF5) { bad(); byte(b); return; }
                    need = (b == 0xF0) ? 0 : (((b & 0xE0) == 0xC0) ? 2 : 3);
                } else if ((b & 0x80) && !(need == 0 && b == 0xF7)) {
                    bad(); byte(b); return;                             // a status where data was due: cut
                }
                if (buf.size() == 40) { bad(); return; }
                buf.push_back(b); sum += b;
                if ((need && buf.size() == need) || b == 0xF7) st = WantSum;
                return;
            case WantSum:
                if (b & 0x80) { bad(); byte(b); return; }
                if (b != (sum & 0x7F)) { bad(); return; }              // the sum does not match: damaged
                st = Idle;
                if (!linkOn) { linkOn = true; next = seq; }
                if (seq != next) { dirty = true; return; }
                applied.push_back(buf);
                next = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((next + 1) & 0x7F);
                dirty = true;
                return;
            case Idle:
                if (b == 0xF4) st = WantSync;
                else if (b == 0xF5) st = WantSeq;
                else if (linkOn) { last = next; dirty = true; }          // orphaned bytes: the expected frame, lost
                return;
        }
    }

    bool ack(Bytes& out) {
        if (!dirty) return false;
        dirty = false;
        out = { 0xF5, next, last };
        return true;
    }
};

inline Bytes noteOn(std::uint8_t ch, std::uint8_t n, std::uint8_t v) { return { std::uint8_t(0x90 | ch), n, v }; }

// A frame as the sender writes it: F5 seq message sum.
inline Bytes frame(std::uint8_t seq, const Bytes& msg) {
    Bytes f = { 0xF5, seq };
    unsigned sum = seq;
    for (auto b : msg) { f.push_back(b); sum += b; }
    f.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(sum & 0x7F));
    return f;
}
inline Bytes cat(std::initializer_list<Bytes> parts) {
    Bytes o;
    for (auto& p : parts) o.insert(o.end(), p.begin(), p.end());
    return o;
}

}  // namespace rp::n8::test
````

the library it used to define and compiles `SampleCache.cpp`, `FileSync.cpp` and `lodepng.cpp` into
`retroplug-backend` directly, with the include directories, the links (`rpcpp`, `miniaudio`, `miniz`) and the DSP
include-root property they need; the backend links `retroplug-host-io` (its constants and its service struct) and no
console (they arrive through `retroplug_product`, which links every package a product lists). `Engine.cpp`'s include
of `host/graph/HostServices.hpp` now finds `EngineHostIo` in `host-io`. `cmake/test-binary.cmake` adds `/bigobj`
itself, so every test binary in a package's directory gets it; `cmake/warnings.cmake` puts `/W4 /WX` on
`retroplug-sameboy`, `-mesen`, `-host-io`, `-sameboy-test` and `-mesen-test` and drops the dead `retroplug-core` (the

and the first Windows run decides); `cmake/sameboy.cmake`'s comment points at the package's `clang-cl` step;

`host-io` include finish the shell's half.

````diff
diff --git a/cmake/packages.cmake b/cmake/packages.cmake
index b70202438..7ca16a8a3 100644
--- a/cmake/packages.cmake
+++ b/cmake/packages.cmake
@@ -1707,6 +1707,57 @@ function(retroplug_check_products)
     endif()
 endfunction()
 
+# retroplug_check_test_helpers(): refuses, at configure time, every target whose link closure reaches a package's native
+# test helpers (retroplug-testing, packages/testing/native) unless the target is a test binary (retroplug_add_test_binary
+# marks one RP_TEST_BINARY). The helpers are a replaced global operator new and the shared test fixtures: a product that
+# linked them would count allocations in production, and a library that did would hand them to every consumer. A package
+# declares @retroplug/testing a devDependency, which the boundary check also allows only a test target to use, so this
+# holds the target properties that check cannot see (a library that links a test binary's helper transitively, say).
+# Deferred as retroplug_check_products is, so a target defined anywhere is checked.
+function(retroplug_check_test_helpers)
+    set(_helper retroplug-testing)
+    if(NOT TARGET ${_helper})
+        return()  # a build without the testing package (a device image) links none
+    endif()
+    _retroplug_build_targets(_targets "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")
+    # Every target's own link names, so a closure is followed without asking the generator to evaluate a target's.
+    foreach(_t IN LISTS _targets)
+        _retroplug_linked_names(_names_${_t} ${_t} LINK_LIBRARIES INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES)
+    endforeach()
+    set(_offenders "")
+    foreach(_t IN LISTS _targets)
+        get_target_property(_test ${_t} RP_TEST_BINARY)
+        if(_test)
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        # A breadth-first walk of what the target links, through the libraries of this build alone: a name that is no
+        # target (a system library) has no closure to follow.
+        set(_pending ${_names_${_t}})
+        set(_seen "")
+        while(_pending)
+            list(POP_FRONT _pending _next)
+            if(_next STREQUAL _helper)
+                list(APPEND _offenders ${_t})
+                break()
+            endif()
+            if(_next IN_LIST _seen OR NOT TARGET ${_next})
+                continue()
+            endif()
+            list(APPEND _seen ${_next})
+            if(_names_${_next})
+                list(APPEND _pending ${_names_${_next}})
+            endif()
+        endwhile()
+    endforeach()
+    if(_offenders)
+        list(JOIN _offenders ", " _offenders)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_check_test_helpers: these targets reach ${_helper}, the native test helpers "
+                            "(packages/testing/native), and are no test binary: ${_offenders}. A product or a library "
+                            "that links them counts allocations in production; link them from a "
+                            "retroplug_add_test_binary alone.")
+    endif()
+endfunction()
+
 # Every target `dir` and the directories under it define, imported and alias targets excepted. A directory still being
 # configured counts, with what it defined so far.
 function(_retroplug_build_targets out dir)

+
+    # A package's test binary sits in the package's directory, so it does not inherit the directory-wide /bigobj that
+    # packages/native's own tests get, and reflect-cpp's instantiation passes COFF's 2^16 section limit (C1128) in any
+    # TU leaning on it. /bigobj only lifts that limit, so every test binary carries it where it means anything.

+    endif()
 endfunction()
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The tests: the two console binaries, the N8 split, and the rigs**

`retroplug-audio-test` keeps four files and 15 cases (`EngineSampleRate`, `NesSplitRouting`, `EngineInvoker`,
`Dither`) and the two new binaries hold the rest. `NodeRig` registers the packages by their `rp_*_package` entries and
places them through `Engine::addNodePackage`; the moving test files change their includes, their `RP_MGB_ROM_PATH`
expectations and their `rp_package` call sites. `N8ReliableLink.test.cpp` splits in two: the sender-only cases (11)
into the N8 pack's test tree, the three from the emulated FIFO role on into `mesen`'s, both over
`packages/testing/native/src/LinkRomModel.hpp`. `pnpm test:plugin`'s list is `package.json` and
`run-plugin-tests.mjs`, and this stage makes it thirteen binaries, so both name the two new ones.
