Create `packages/n8/native/test/N8ReliableLink.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// Guards the sender half of BlipToaster's reliable link (transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp, the pack's): messages framed
// behind one sync, the window and its acks, running status and SysEx, a re-send on the timeout, a ROM that lost track,
// and a soak through a channel that eats 1-3 byte bursts, where every message must apply once, in order. The emulated
// cart FIFO that speaks the link from the other side is the Mesen package's, and its own cases are that package's test
// binary's (packages/mesen/native/test/N8ReliableLink.test.cpp).
//
// Run via `pnpm test:n8` (retroplug-n8-test).

#include <cstdint>
#include <initializer_list>
#include <random>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "LinkRomModel.hpp"
#include "transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp"

namespace {

using rp::n8::test::Bytes;
using rp::n8::test::cat;
using rp::n8::test::frame;
using rp::n8::test::noteOn;
using rp::n8::test::RomModel;
using rp::N8ReliableSender;

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("reliable link: messages go out as frames behind one sync", "[n8][link]") {
    N8ReliableSender s;
    Bytes wire;
    s.send(noteOn(0, 60, 100).data(), 3, [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int) { wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n); });
    const Bytes cc = { 0xB1, 7, 90 };
    s.send(cc.data(), 3, [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int) { wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n); });
    CHECK(wire == cat({ { 0xF4, 0 }, frame(0, { 0x90, 60, 100 }), frame(1, { 0xB1, 7, 90 }) }));
    CHECK(s.outstanding() == 2);
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: a window that fills without an ack gives up the window and re-syncs, not grows",
          "[n8][link]") {
    // The sender's window is 48 frames. A cart that stops answering must not make it grow: at the 49th frame the
    // whole window is given up and a sync goes out ahead of the new frame, so the ROM is re-pointed at what follows.
    N8ReliableSender s;
    Bytes wire;
    int framesSentByEmit = 0;  // the seq >= 0 marker counts first sends (and later re-sends) on the wire
    const auto emit = [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int seq) {
        wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n);
        if (seq >= 0) ++framesSentByEmit;
    };
    for (int i = 0; i < 49; ++i) {
        const Bytes msg = noteOn(0, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(60 + i % 12), 100);
        s.send(msg.data(), msg.size(), emit);
    }
    CHECK(s.framesSent() == 49);
    CHECK(framesSentByEmit == 49);
    CHECK(s.outstanding() == 1);   // the 49th send cleared the window before its own frame
    // And the re-sync it gave the ROM first: F4 <next seq> immediately ahead of that 49th frame, so the ROM is
    // re-pointed at what follows rather than left expecting a frame that is never coming.
    const Bytes last = frame(48, noteOn(0, 60, 100));
    REQUIRE(wire.size() >= last.size() + 2);
    CHECK(Bytes(wire.end() - static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(last.size()), wire.end()) == last);
    CHECK(wire[wire.size() - last.size() - 2] == 0xF4);
    CHECK(wire[wire.size() - last.size() - 1] == 48);
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: running status is expanded, real-time passes through, SysEx is one frame", "[n8][link]") {
    N8ReliableSender s;
    Bytes wire;
    auto emit = [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int) { wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n); };
    const Bytes in = { 0x90, 60, 100, 64, 100, 0xF8, 0xF0, 0x7D, 0x42, 0x02, 0xF7, 0xC3, 5 };
    s.send(in.data(), in.size(), emit);
    CHECK(wire == cat({ { 0xF4, 0 },
                        frame(0, { 0x90, 60, 100 }),
                        frame(1, { 0x90, 64, 100 }),
                        { 0xF8 },
                        frame(2, { 0xF0, 0x7D, 0x42, 0x02, 0xF7 }),
                        frame(3, { 0xC3, 5 }) }));
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: a message split across sends is still one frame", "[n8][link]") {
    N8ReliableSender s;
    Bytes wire;
    auto emit = [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int) { wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n); };
    const Bytes a = { 0xF0, 0x7D, 0x42 }, b = { 0x02, 0xF7 };
    s.send(a.data(), a.size(), emit);
    CHECK(wire.empty());
    s.send(b.data(), b.size(), emit);
    CHECK(wire == cat({ { 0xF4, 0 }, frame(0, { 0xF0, 0x7D, 0x42, 0x02, 0xF7 }) }));
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: an ack frees the window; an ack naming a sent frame re-sends from it", "[n8][link]") {
    N8ReliableSender::Timing t;
    t.resendDelayNs = 1000;
    N8ReliableSender s(t);
    Bytes wire;
    auto emit = [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int seq) {
        wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n);
        if (seq >= 0) s.onSent(seq, 0);
    };
    for (std::uint8_t n : { 60, 62, 64 }) s.send(noteOn(0, n, 100).data(), 3, emit);
    REQUIRE(s.outstanding() == 3);

    const Bytes ack1 = { 0xF5, 1, 2 };   // frame 0 arrived; 1 did not - the ROM read 2 (and dropped it behind the gap)
    s.onBackChannel(ack1.data(), ack1.size(), 500);
    CHECK(s.outstanding() == 2);

    wire.clear();
    CHECK(s.poll(1000, emit) != N8ReliableSender::kNever);   // not yet: the modelled round trip is 1000 ns
    CHECK(wire.empty());
    s.poll(1500, emit);
    CHECK(wire == cat({ frame(1, { 0x90, 62, 100 }), frame(2, { 0x90, 64, 100 }) }));
    CHECK(s.resends() == 1);

    const Bytes ack3 = { 0xF5, 3, 2 };
    s.onBackChannel(ack3.data(), ack3.size(), 2000);
    CHECK(s.outstanding() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: a frame nothing answers is re-sent on the timeout", "[n8][link]") {
    N8ReliableSender::Timing t;
    t.timeoutNs = 10'000;
    N8ReliableSender s(t);
    Bytes wire;
    auto emit = [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int seq) {
        wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n);
        if (seq >= 0) s.onSent(seq, 0);
    };
    s.send(noteOn(0, 60, 100).data(), 3, emit);
    wire.clear();
    s.poll(9'999, emit);
    CHECK(wire.empty());
    s.poll(10'000, emit);
    CHECK(wire == frame(0, { 0x90, 60, 100 }));
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: a ROM that lost track (rebooted) is re-synced to the oldest frame", "[n8][link]") {
    N8ReliableSender s;
    Bytes wire;
    auto emit = [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int seq) {
        wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n);
        if (seq >= 0) s.onSent(seq, 0);
    };
    for (std::uint8_t n : { 60, 62 }) s.send(noteOn(0, n, 100).data(), 3, emit);
    const Bytes ack = { 0xF5, 90, 89 };   // a number we never sent
    s.onBackChannel(ack.data(), ack.size(), 10);
    wire.clear();
    s.poll(10, emit);
    CHECK(wire == cat({ { 0xF4, 0 }, frame(0, { 0x90, 60, 100 }), frame(1, { 0x90, 62, 100 }) }));
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: through a channel that eats 1-3 byte bursts, every message applies once, in order",
          "[n8][link]") {
    // A seeded, deterministic soak: 2000 messages (notes, CCs, the odd SysEx) in bursts, each byte on the wire
    // at ~1.5% risk of starting a burst of 1-3 losses - an order of magnitude worse than a DMC beat on NTSC.
    std::mt19937 rng(1234);
    N8ReliableSender::Timing t;
    t.resendDelayNs = 2'000'000;
    t.timeoutNs     = 20'000'000;
    N8ReliableSender s(t);
    RomModel rom;

    std::int64_t now = 0;
    Bytes inFlight;                                   // what the "FIFO" will deliver at the next delivery tick
    auto emit = [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int seq) {
        inFlight.insert(inFlight.end(), d, d + n);
        if (seq >= 0) s.onSent(seq, now);
    };
    auto deliver = [&] {
        std::uniform_int_distribution<int> pct(0, 999), burst(1, 3);
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < inFlight.size(); ++i) {
            if (pct(rng) < 15) { i += static_cast<std::size_t>(burst(rng)) - 1; continue; }   // lost
            rom.byte(inFlight[i]);
        }
        inFlight.clear();
        Bytes ack;
        if (rom.ack(ack)) s.onBackChannel(ack.data(), ack.size(), now);   // the FIFO ran empty
    };

    std::vector<Bytes> sent;
    for (int i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
        Bytes m;
        switch (i % 7) {
            case 3:  m = { 0xB1, std::uint8_t(i & 0x7F), std::uint8_t((i * 3) & 0x7F) }; break;
            case 6:  m = { 0xF0, 0x7D, 0x42, 0x02, 0xF7 }; break;
            default: m = noteOn(std::uint8_t(i % 4), std::uint8_t(36 + i % 40), 100); break;
        }
        sent.push_back(m);
        s.send(m.data(), m.size(), emit);
        if (i % 3 == 2) {                             // a sequencer step: deliver, then let time pass
            deliver();
            for (int k = 0; k < 4; ++k) { now += 1'000'000; s.poll(now, emit); deliver(); }
        }
    }
    for (int k = 0; k < 2000 && s.outstanding(); ++k) { now += 1'000'000; s.poll(now, emit); deliver(); }

    CHECK(s.outstanding() == 0);
    CHECK(s.resends() > 0);                           // the channel really did lose frames
    REQUIRE(rom.applied.size() == sent.size());       // none lost, none applied twice
    std::size_t firstDiff = 0;
    while (firstDiff < sent.size() && rom.applied[firstDiff] == sent[firstDiff]) ++firstDiff;
    if (firstDiff < sent.size()) {
        std::string a, b;
        for (auto x : rom.applied[firstDiff]) a += std::to_string(x) + " ";
        for (auto x : sent[firstDiff]) b += std::to_string(x) + " ";
        INFO("first difference at message " << firstDiff << ": applied [" << a << "] sent [" << b << "]");
        CHECK(false);
    }
    CHECK(rom.applied == sent);                       // and in order
}


TEST_CASE("reliable link: a SysEx longer than the ROM's frame buffer is not framed", "[n8][link]") {
    N8ReliableSender s;
    Bytes wire;
    Bytes big = { 0xF0 };
    for (int i = 0; i < 45; ++i) big.push_back(0x10);
    big.push_back(0xF7);
    s.send(big.data(), big.size(), [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int) { wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n); });
    CHECK(wire.empty());
    CHECK(s.outstanding() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: an ack that has not seen the frame waits; one that has re-sends it at once", "[n8][link]") {
    // <last> before <next>: the ROM has not read the frame - it is still on its way (on a cart, crossing USB; in the
    // emulator, landing while the ack is written). Re-sending on a timer then duplicated frames that were fine. <last>
    // at or past <next>: the ROM read it (or bytes it had to discard, which it reports as that frame): lost - re-send.
    N8ReliableSender s;
    Bytes wire;
    std::int64_t now = 0;
    auto emit = [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int seq) { wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n); if (seq >= 0) s.onSent(seq, now); };
    s.send(noteOn(0, 60, 100).data(), 3, emit);

    const Bytes notSeen = { 0xF5, 0, 0x7F };
    now = 1'000'000; s.onBackChannel(notSeen.data(), notSeen.size(), now);
    wire.clear();
    now = 50'000'000; s.poll(now, emit);
    CHECK(wire.empty());                         // in flight: nothing to do (well inside the 100 ms timeout)

    const Bytes seen = { 0xF5, 0, 0 };
    s.onBackChannel(seen.data(), seen.size(), now);
    s.poll(now, emit);
    CHECK(wire == frame(0, { 0x90, 60, 100 }));
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: an ack after a frame arrived settles it - no re-send", "[n8][link]") {
    N8ReliableSender s;
    Bytes wire;
    std::int64_t now = 0;
    auto emit = [&](const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, int seq) { wire.insert(wire.end(), d, d + n); if (seq >= 0) s.onSent(seq, now); };
    s.send(noteOn(0, 60, 100).data(), 3, emit);
    const Bytes early = { 0xF5, 0, 0x7F }, later = { 0xF5, 1, 0 };
    now = 1'000; s.onBackChannel(early.data(), early.size(), now);
    now = 2'000'000; s.onBackChannel(later.data(), later.size(), now);
    wire.clear();
    now = 500'000'000; s.poll(now, emit);
    CHECK(wire.empty());
    CHECK(s.outstanding() == 0);
}
````

````cpp
// Guards the emulated cart FIFO's use of BlipToaster's reliable link (system/mesen/roles/NesN8FifoRole.cpp): the role
// frames MIDI and consumes the ROM's acks, numbers frames in the order it releases them, and carries a message into the
// next block so that it is numbered when it is released. The sender's own half of the link is the N8 pack's
// (packages/n8/native/test/N8ReliableLink.test.cpp), and the model of the ROM's rules both halves drive is the shared
// test helper library's LinkRomModel.hpp (@retroplug/testing): the pack may not include this package, and this one
// declares it.
//
// Run via `pnpm test:plugin` (retroplug-mesen-test).

#include <cstdint>
#include <initializer_list>
#include <random>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "LinkRomModel.hpp"
#include "system/mesen/roles/NesN8FifoRole.hpp"
#include "transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp"

namespace {

using rp::n8::test::Bytes;
using rp::n8::test::cat;
using rp::n8::test::frame;
using rp::n8::test::RomModel;
using rp::N8ReliableSender;

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("reliable link: the emulated FIFO role frames MIDI and consumes the ROM's acks", "[audio][nes][link]") {
    NesN8FifoRole role;
    std::uint64_t cycles = 0;
    role.setClock([&cycles] { return cycles; }, 1'789'773.0);
    N8ReliableSender::Timing t;
    t.resendDelayNs = 0;
    role.enableLink(t);

    ::MidiEvent e{};
    e.frame = 0; e.size = 3; e.data[0] = 0x90; e.data[1] = 60; e.data[2] = 100;
    role.onMidi(&e, 1);
    role.pumpUntil(0);
    Bytes got;
    for (int b; (b = role.readFifoByte()) >= 0;) got.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(b));
    CHECK(got == cat({ { 0xF4, 0 }, frame(0, { 0x90, 60, 100 }) }));
    CHECK(role.link()->outstanding() == 1);

    // The ROM's ack, written as the cart does it: an Edio CMD_USB_WR with payload F5 <next>. The role takes it
    // (drainUsbTx stays empty) and the window frees.
    const Bytes cmd = { '+', std::uint8_t('+' ^ 0xFF), 0x22, std::uint8_t(0x22 ^ 0xFF), 3, 0, 0xF5, 1, 0 };
    // Writes go through the FIFO's register, as the ROM's STA $40F0 would.
    for (auto b : cmd) role.writeFifoByte(b);
    CHECK(role.drainUsbTx().empty());
    CHECK(role.link()->outstanding() == 0);

    // A lost frame: the ack says 1 is still expected and that the ROM READ frame 1 (damaged) - re-sent on the next pump.
    e.data[1] = 62;
    role.onMidi(&e, 1);
    role.pumpUntil(0);
    while (role.readFifoByte() >= 0) {}            // the "ROM" read it... and lost it
    cycles += 1000;
    const Bytes damaged = { '+', std::uint8_t('+' ^ 0xFF), 0x22, std::uint8_t(0x22 ^ 0xFF), 3, 0, 0xF5, 1, 1 };
    for (auto b : damaged) role.writeFifoByte(b);  // F5 1 1: still expecting 1, having read it
    role.pumpUntil(0);
    got.clear();
    for (int b; (b = role.readFifoByte()) >= 0;) got.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(b));
    CHECK(got == frame(1, { 0x90, 62, 100 }));
}


TEST_CASE("reliable link: the emulated role numbers frames in the order it releases them", "[audio][nes][link]") {
    // A ROM already mid-stream (one frame applied) gets three messages queued out of offset order within one block:
    // onMidi at 100, a raw pushBytes SysEx at 20, onMidi at 50. pumpUntil releases by offset, so the sequence numbers
    // must follow that order - numbered in queue order instead, the ROM drops the early arrivals as out of sequence,
    // applies them late and out of order, and the sender has to re-send them.
    NesN8FifoRole role;
    std::uint64_t cycles = 0;
    role.setClock([&cycles] { return cycles; }, 1'789'773.0);
    N8ReliableSender::Timing t;
    t.resendDelayNs = 0;
    role.enableLink(t);

    // The ROM reads everything delivered so far, then answers on the back-channel as the cart does (CMD_USB_WR).
    RomModel rom;
    Bytes got;
    auto romReads = [&] {
        for (int v; (v = role.readFifoByte()) >= 0;) {
            got.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v));
            rom.byte(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v));
        }
        Bytes ack;
        if (!rom.ack(ack)) return;
        const Bytes cmd = { '+', std::uint8_t('+' ^ 0xFF), 0x22, std::uint8_t(0x22 ^ 0xFF),
                            std::uint8_t(ack.size()), 0 };
        for (auto v : cmd) role.writeFifoByte(v);
        for (auto v : ack) role.writeFifoByte(v);
    };

    ::MidiEvent prime{};
    prime.frame = 0; prime.size = 3; prime.data[0] = 0x92; prime.data[1] = 64; prime.data[2] = 80;
    role.onMidi(&prime, 1);
    role.pumpUntil(0);
    romReads();
    REQUIRE(rom.applied.size() == 1);
    REQUIRE(role.link()->outstanding() == 0);
    rom.applied.clear();
    got.clear();
    role.rebase(512);

    ::MidiEvent a{};
    a.frame = 100; a.size = 3; a.data[0] = 0x90; a.data[1] = 60; a.data[2] = 100;
    role.onMidi(&a, 1);
    const Bytes sysex = { 0xF0, 0x7D, 0x42, 0x02, 0xF7 };
    role.pushBytes(20, sysex.data(), sysex.size());
    ::MidiEvent b{};
    b.frame = 50; b.size = 3; b.data[0] = 0x91; b.data[1] = 62; b.data[2] = 90;
    role.onMidi(&b, 1);

    for (std::uint32_t off : { 20u, 50u, 100u }) {
        role.pumpUntil(off);
        romReads();
        cycles += 1000;
    }
    CHECK(got == cat({ frame(1, sysex), frame(2, { 0x91, 62, 90 }), frame(3, { 0x90, 60, 100 }) }));

    // Well past the sender's timeout: anything still unconfirmed would be re-sent here.
    cycles += 1'789'773 / 2;
    role.pumpUntil(512);
    romReads();

    REQUIRE(rom.applied.size() == 3);
    CHECK(rom.applied[0] == sysex);
    CHECK(rom.applied[1] == Bytes{ 0x91, 62, 90 });
    CHECK(rom.applied[2] == Bytes{ 0x90, 60, 100 });
    CHECK(role.link()->outstanding() == 0);
    CHECK(role.link()->resends() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("reliable link: a message carried into the next block is numbered when it is released", "[audio][nes][link]") {
    // A message queued past the block end rides rebase into the next block. One queued there for an EARLIER offset
    // goes out first, so it must carry the earlier sequence number - framing at the carried message's first pump would
    // have numbered it first, and the ROM would drop it.
    NesN8FifoRole role;
    std::uint64_t cycles = 0;
    role.setClock([&cycles] { return cycles; }, 1'789'773.0);
    N8ReliableSender::Timing t;
    t.resendDelayNs = 0;
    role.enableLink(t);

    constexpr std::uint32_t kBlock = 512;
    ::MidiEvent late{};
    late.frame = kBlock + 100; late.size = 3; late.data[0] = 0x90; late.data[1] = 60; late.data[2] = 100;
    role.onMidi(&late, 1);
    role.pumpUntil(kBlock);
    CHECK(role.readFifoByte() < 0);   // not due this block
    role.rebase(kBlock);

    ::MidiEvent early{};
    early.frame = 20; early.size = 3; early.data[0] = 0x91; early.data[1] = 62; early.data[2] = 90;
    role.onMidi(&early, 1);
    Bytes got;
    for (std::uint32_t off : { 20u, 100u }) {
        role.pumpUntil(off);
        for (int v; (v = role.readFifoByte()) >= 0;) got.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v));
    }
    CHECK(got == cat({ { 0xF4, 0 }, frame(0, { 0x91, 62, 90 }), frame(1, { 0x90, 60, 100 }) }));
}
````

formatting is free and nothing depends on it; what has to hold is the content, product for product. The re-record

indentation: run with the update flag, it rewrites the file, and the step then puts the design commit's two spaces
back with a JSON round-trip, so the bytes the commit carries are that same content in the old shape. A misplaced hand

- [ ] **Step 8: The boundary fixtures and the program-name checks they hold**

Two fixtures and the gather project's two entries. `refused-native/MesenN8Undeclared.json` is a Mesen-shaped package
that links `retroplug-n8` and includes its tree without declaring it, refused; `read/MesenN8Declared.json` is the same
package with `n8` declared, which holds - the pair is what says the refusal is the undeclared edge and not the
package's shape. The gather project gains the `testing-dependency` case (a library that links `retroplug-testing`,
which the boundary check holds and `retroplug_check_test_helpers` refuses) and the `devDeclared` property the
definition rule reads. The TypeScript side follows the native headers' new homes: `platform.ts` and
`rom-format.test.ts` name the two packages' gates and say the ORDER of the checks is the sniffer's own,
`buildGraph.ts` names the console packages' node types and config structs, the two `ts/app.ts` files say the native
halves are their packages', and `check-boundaries.mjs` counts a dependency its CMakeLists names a file of as used
(which is how `sameboy`'s `mgb` and `mesen`'s `testing` devDependencies are marked used rather than warned about).

````diff
+**A console package's native half.** A package whose console the engine runs is a native entry like any other, plus
+three rules the two console packages (four node types between them) follow (F2,
+[modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md](../docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md) section 2):
+
+- It declares `@retroplug/system` and `@retroplug/node-sdk` beside whatever else it needs (`mesen` declares `n8`, whose
+  reliable-link header its emulated FIFO speaks). Its target is a `retroplug_package_library` linking `retroplug-system`,
+  `retroplug-node-sdk` and its third-party library (`sameboy`, `mesen`), and its include root is `src/`, so a moved
+  source keeps the include text it had.
+- Its node type declares `category = "system"` and lives on the contract's `SystemNode<Self, Core, Settings>` template
+  (`system/SystemNode.hpp`), which builds the core at activation through `rp.host.systems/2` with the build function the
+  node's own package carries (`SystemBuildFn`, `system/SystemBuild.hpp`) and the config its settings made. The engine
+  knows no console: it recognises a system node by that category alone, and holds a type that declares it to a built
+  core (a plan whose slot stayed null is refused before it is published). What the type must therefore carry is its
+  settings struct (with `system`, the resource refs and a `key()` of the fields a rebuild depends on), `config()`, its
+  lanes and its knobs' application; the console's knob helpers stay beside it.
+- What it computes is its own: the console's ROM gate (magic bytes, not the extension) and its button table live in the
+  package, and so does its audio path. A case that builds its core directly needs no `Engine`, so it belongs in the
+  package's own test binary (`retroplug-sameboy-test`, `retroplug-mesen-test`), built by `retroplug_add_test_binary` and
+  listed in `pnpm test:plugin`; a case that drives an `Engine` stays in the shell's `retroplug-audio-test`.
````

(The `TinyUSB submodule has not been initialized` hint above it is `/opt/pico-sdk`'s own: the check needs no USB, which is why it uses that SDK.)

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f2pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

Run: `bash -c 'R="(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) [ 0-9][0-9] 20[0-9]{2}"; for e in build-device/rp-device-check.elf; do arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary $e /tmp/f2-img.bin && LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -E "$R" /tmp/f2-img.bin && LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/$R/Nov  4 2026/" /tmp/f2-img.bin | sha256sum; done; rm -f /tmp/f2-img.bin'`

````bash
`sameboy` gains its native half: SameBoySystem, SameBoyConfig, SameBoyConstants and the boot ROMs, the

`mesen` gains the NES, GBA and SMS/GG systems with their configs, the global init, the boot and block
helpers, the video and audio devices, the NES debug session with Cc65DbgParser, the NES's emulated N8 FIFO

for the expansion-volume range it now reads from n8/N8Node.hpp, whose duplicate and STATIC_REQUIRE go. The
SMS gate's "another console's ROM" check keeps the Game Boy logo, which each console package holds as its own copy in
its RomFormat.hpp: a console package keeps the magic bytes it checks, and neither may depend on the other.

`host-io` is a new package holding rp.host.midi-in / -out, the engine service they read
(rp.engine.host-io/3) and the staging bounds the engine sizes from.

The shell: SystemNodes.{hpp,cpp} and system/{InputTypes,RomFormat}.hpp are gone, `retroplug-core` dissolves
(SampleCache, FileSync and lodepng join retroplug-backend, with the links and includes they need, and its two
genex links go with the code that needed them), and packages/native/package.json names its one library and
registers no node type. The backend links host-io (its constants are the engine's) and the consoles only
through retroplug_product, since the engine reaches them solely through its generated rp_register_packages.

The product list becomes core launchpad system sameboy dsp mgb lsdj lsdj-launchpad graph-runtime n8 mesen
smsggdj risa host-io native bliptoaster; the TS generator's only change is mesen's role moving after n8.

Tests: `retroplug-sameboy-test` and `retroplug-mesen-test` take the console cases out of retroplug-audio-test
(a case that drives an Engine stays there), engine-graph's MesenShared.test.cpp joins the Mesen package, and
N8ReliableLink.test.cpp splits: its sender cases to the N8 pack's binary over a shared model of the ROM's
rules (packages/n8/native/test/LinkRomModel.hpp), its role cases to retroplug-mesen-test. test:plugin runs
thirteen binaries, and the case totals across the suites are equal (the eleven sender cases moved from
test:plugin to test:n8).

Boundary fixtures: a Mesen-shaped package reaching n8 undeclared is refused, a system-shaped one reaching
the shell is refused, and one declaring what it reaches holds.

Re-recorded: the [packages] golden (product-registrations.json), the intended re-record of section 8 and
nothing else. The consoles' and host-io's node types now register at their own packages' positions rather
than `native`'s, so every product's row moves rp.sameboy.gb to just after the launchpad's types and the three
rp.mesen.* types stay beside rp.n8.nes; each row still holds the same 28 types, and no other golden, digest,
image hash or pack byte moves.

The shared C++ test helpers get a home of their own: @retroplug/testing gains a native half (packages/testing/native),
an OBJECT library holding CountingAllocator and LinkRomModel.hpp, so no test binary includes another package's test
tree and the three copies of the allocator go. The two console test binaries keep the warning level their sources
compiled at (off /W4 /WX until the owed Windows run has seen them) and take /bigobj, which their sources had from
packages/native's directory-wide option and a package's directory does not inherit.

Namespace hygiene follows the template: the consoles' knob types move out of rp::host::knobs, which every package
reaches, into each node's unnamed namespace, and so do the settings structs and the package functions, so two packages
cannot define one name differently.
````

---

### Task 3: embedded resources a package declares, and the product's table

Design section 5 and 9's third stage. The mGB ROM stops being a closed `id == "mgb"` in a header the shell owns: a
package's `retroplug` field may carry `embed: [{ "id", "file" }]`, `retroplug_package` gives a package with embeds an
OBJECT library built through `cmake/bin2c.cmake`, and `retroplug_product` generates `rp_embedded_resources()` - a table
from id to bytes over the product's packages - beside `rp_register_packages()`. `EngineRpcService::putResource` reads
the table where it read `rp::embeddedRom`, and `EmbeddedRoms.hpp` and the root `mgb-rom` target go. The ROM's move is a
binary `git mv` (never quoted; the two hashes in Step 1 are its proof).

Two decisions the design left open are the stage's: a device product emits NO table (an empty one changed both box
images through the new symbol, so the images stay byte-identical), and the symbol is computed once, from the package AND
the id, with a collision refused at configure (the review's own pair: `lsdj` + `launchpad_kit` against `lsdj-launchpad`
+ `kit`, and the `_len` objects too).

The stage also carries the boundary check's compile-definition rule and the `devDependency` door a test needs for a
fixture file: `sameboy`'s test binary opens `mgb`'s ROM by path, and its manifest declares `mgb` a devDependency, which
is what makes the reach legal. The review found the first pass blind to the quoted `-DNAME="path"` form the tree
writes, and the fix closed it with `_retroplug_unquote_path` and a quoted fixture on each side (Step 4's two
`*Quoted.json` files).

- [ ] **Step 1: The ROM's move, and the header that resolved it**

One binary `git mv`: `resources/roms/mGB.gb` becomes `packages/mgb/rom/mGB.gb`. The file is a 64 KiB Game Boy ROM, so
the plan never quotes it and the two hashes below are its proof: `git mv` moves the blob, and the blob is the one the
design commit had. `packages/native/src/EmbeddedRoms.hpp` - `embeddedRom(id)` with `id == "mgb"` written in it - is
deleted, with the root `mgb-rom` target and the `mgb-rom` link in Step 3.

The moves, as one script (each `git mv` stages its move, and `set -e` stops at the first that fails):

````bash
mkdir -p packages/mgb/rom
set -e
git mv resources/roms/mGB.gb packages/mgb/rom/mGB.gb
````

Run: `bash -c 'git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no | grep -c "^R"'`
Expected: `1`: every move of this task so far is staged (1 of them here), and none failed.

Run: `git hash-object packages/mgb/rom/mGB.gb`
Expected: `0f8fe45fddd0e92fd2e4e6a894d12d0bc6bb2b79`: the blob `resources/roms/mGB.gb` had at the design commit, so `git mv` moved the ROM's bytes and not a copy of something else.

Run: `git cat-file -s 0f8fe45fddd0e92fd2e4e6a894d12d0bc6bb2b79`
Expected: `65536`: the file's size in bytes. Its content is a Game Boy ROM, so this plan never quotes it: the two hashes above are the proof it is the same file.

- [ ] **Step 2: The manifest's embed member, the per-package arrays and the product's table**

`cmake/packages.cmake` gains `_retroplug_read_embeds`, which reads `retroplug.embed` as an array of `{ "id", "file"
}`: the id must match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` (it names the generated array), `file` is relative to the package's
own directory, must be neither absolute nor resolvable outside it, and must exist at configure, a duplicate id inside
one package is refused, and an empty list is refused (a member present and empty is an edit mistake, not a package
with no embeds). The "no contribution" refusal now also accepts `embed`, so `mgb` - which has an app, a protocol
member and an embed but no native member - is a package. `_retroplug_embed_symbol` derives `rp_embed_<package>_<id>`
once and `_retroplug_embed_entries` reads it from the package's properties instead of recomputing, refusing a second
entry with one C name (the array's `<symbol>` and its `<symbol>_len`, naming both packages). `retroplug_package` gives
a package with embeds the OBJECT library `retroplug-<package>-embeds`, one C source per entry from `cmake/bin2c.cmake`
into `build/packages/<package>/embeds/`; `retroplug_product` links those libraries and generates the product's
`rp_embedded_resources()` beside `rp_register_packages()` - a function-local `static const` table, or `*count = 0;
return nullptr;` for a product with no embeds, which a device product never emits at all. `bin2c.cmake` is tightened
while it is moved into the package path: it refuses an empty input, and formats the bytes with two regular expressions
over the whole hex string instead of a per-byte `string(APPEND)` loop (which is quadratic, and megabytes would stall a
build). `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/graph/Packages.hpp` declares the C-compatible `rp_embedded_resource`
struct, `rp_embedded_resources(size_t*)` and `rp::graph::embeddedResource(std::string_view) -> std::span<const
std::uint8_t>`. `cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake` gains the `DEFINITIONS` argument of Step 5's fixtures, and
`cmake/check-embeds.cmake` is the driver the two embed-collision projects are read through: it reads two scratch
packages with the real reader and hands them to the real `_retroplug_embed_entries`.

Create `cmake/check-embeds.cmake`:

````cmake
# cmake -DRP_EMBED_ALPHA=<package.json> -DRP_EMBED_BETA=<package.json> [-DRP_EMBED_ALPHA_NAME=<package>]
#       -DRP_EMBED_BETA_NAME=<package> -P cmake/check-embeds.cmake: reads two manifests as retroplug_package() reads them,
# in script mode, under the package names it is given (alpha and beta unless told otherwise, since the generated
# array's symbol is the package's and the id's), and asks for the embedded-resource table a product listing both would
# carry (cmake/packages.cmake's _retroplug_embed_entries), so the rules that a product may not carry one id twice, nor
# two entries whose symbols run together, are held by a fixture the way the manifest rules are
# (packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake): a rule that stopped firing fails the configure rather than going unnoticed.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.19)
if(NOT RP_EMBED_ALPHA OR NOT RP_EMBED_BETA)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "check-embeds.cmake: pass -DRP_EMBED_ALPHA=<package.json> -DRP_EMBED_BETA=<package.json>")
endif()
if(NOT RP_EMBED_ALPHA_NAME)
    set(RP_EMBED_ALPHA_NAME alpha)
endif()
if(NOT RP_EMBED_BETA_NAME)
    set(RP_EMBED_BETA_NAME beta)
endif()
include("${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/packages.cmake")
_retroplug_read_manifest(${RP_EMBED_ALPHA_NAME} "${RP_EMBED_ALPHA}")
_retroplug_read_manifest(${RP_EMBED_BETA_NAME} "${RP_EMBED_BETA}")
_retroplug_embed_entries(demo _rp_entries ${RP_EMBED_ALPHA_NAME} ${RP_EMBED_BETA_NAME})
message(STATUS "check-embeds.cmake: ${RP_EMBED_ALPHA} and ${RP_EMBED_BETA} read; the table holds ${_rp_entries}")
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The shell reads the table**

`putResource`'s `embedded` branch calls `rp::graph::embeddedResource(*spec.embedded)`, and an id the product does not
carry is refused with exactly today's words, `"<id>" is not an embedded ROM`. The root `CMakeLists.txt` loses the
`mgb-rom` target, its `bin2c` custom command and its comment block, `packages/native/CMakeLists.txt` loses the
`mgb-rom` link and its comment, and `packages/mgb/package.json` gains `"embed": [{ "id": "mgb", "file": "rom/mGB.gb"
}]`. The root `package.json`'s two CLI render scripts name the ROM's new path.

````diff
         if (rom.empty()) {
             out.error = rp::graph::jsonString(*spec.embedded) + " is not an embedded ROM";
             return out;
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The fixtures: four embed projects, the reader's refusals, and the product with no embeds**

Sixteen files are the embed fixtures' four projects, each a pair of scratch packages with one-byte-ish ROMs:
`duplicate/{alpha,beta}` (both embed `mgb`, refused), `distinct/{alpha,beta}` (`mgb` and `lsdj`, which holds and whose
table the driver prints), `symbol/{lsdj,lsdj-launchpad}` (ids `launchpad_kit` and `kit`, which run together to one
symbol, refused) and `len/{alpha,alpha_rom}` (`alpha` + `rom` and `alpha_rom` + `len`, both wanting
`rp_embed_alpha_rom_len`, refused). Ten `refused/Embed*.json` are the reader's own refusals, each with its required
reason: not a list, an empty list, no id, an id that is no C identifier, no file, a file that does not exist, one that
is absolute, one that resolves outside the package, a duplicate id, and an empty file (with `refused/Empty.bin`, which
is zero bytes: `: >` writes it and the empty blob's hash proves it). `read/EmbedOnly.json` is the package with an
embed and nothing else, which must read; `read/embeds.bin` is its bytes. The two `*Quoted.json` fixtures under `read/`
and `refused-native/` are Step 5's compile-definition rule, in the quoted form the tree writes.
`test/packages/product/` is the desktop `count = 0` branch's proof, a project of its own: `CMakeLists.txt` includes
the real `cmake/packages.cmake`, states one fixture package's properties as `retroplug_package` would for a manifest
with one native entry and no embed, and calls the real `retroplug_product(rp_fixture_product PACKAGES alpha)`;
`fixtureEntry.cpp` is the entry; `main.cpp` asserts `rp_embedded_resources` answers `nullptr` with count 0 and that
`rp_register_packages` still lists the one entry. `tests.cmake` configures, builds and runs it inside
`build/packages/product-no-embeds` at every configure, and the gather project gains the two definition cases Step 5's
rule is red on.

Create `packages/native/test/packages/product/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# A product that embeds nothing, configured as a child project by packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake: it generates the
# product source for a package list with no `embed` entry, compiles it, and runs it. No product in the tree has that
# shape (every desktop product lists mgb, whose ROM is an embed), so cmake/packages.cmake's `count = 0` branch would
# otherwise be compiled by nobody. The source is the same one a real product is generated from, so a branch that stops
# compiling, or that answers a count other than 0, fails here.
#
# The package is a fixture: its global properties are what retroplug_package() sets for a manifest with one native entry
# and no `embed`, and its target is a scratch library whose sources and links the branch under test never reads.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.19)
project(retroplug_product_no_embeds CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
# One output directory for every configuration, so the caller names the check's path once (a multi-config generator would
# otherwise put it under a per-config directory).
set(CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin")
foreach(_config Debug Release RelWithDebInfo MinSizeRel)
    set(CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_${_config} "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin")
endforeach()

if(NOT RP_ROOT)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/product/CMakeLists.txt: pass -DRP_ROOT=<the repository root>")
endif()

include("${RP_ROOT}/cmake/packages.cmake")

add_library(rp_fixture_alpha INTERFACE)
add_library(rp_fixture_entry STATIC fixtureEntry.cpp)
# graph/Packages.hpp is the graph runtime's and graph/rp_node.h the node SDK's; the two include roots are all the
# generated source and the fixture's entry read.
set(_rp_include_roots "${RP_ROOT}/packages/graph-runtime/native/src" "${RP_ROOT}/packages/node-sdk/native/src")
target_include_directories(rp_fixture_entry PRIVATE ${_rp_include_roots})

set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGES alpha)
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_alpha_ENTRIES rp_fixture_entry)
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_alpha_TARGETS rp_fixture_alpha rp_fixture_entry)
# No `embed`: _retroplug_embed_entries() finds nothing for this package, and the generated table takes the branch that
# answers a count of 0. Setting the properties explicitly states the fixture's shape rather than leaving it unsaid.
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_alpha_EMBED_IDS "")
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_alpha_EMBED_SYMBOLS "")

add_library(rp_fixture_product STATIC)
retroplug_product(rp_fixture_product PACKAGES alpha)

add_executable(rp_fixture_product_check main.cpp)
target_include_directories(rp_fixture_product PRIVATE ${_rp_include_roots})
target_include_directories(rp_fixture_product_check PRIVATE ${_rp_include_roots})
target_link_libraries(rp_fixture_product_check PRIVATE rp_fixture_product)
````

Create `packages/native/test/packages/product/main.cpp`:

````cpp
// Holds the generated table's `count = 0` branch (cmake/packages.cmake) and the registration beside it: a desktop product
// whose packages embed nothing answers a count of 0 and a null table, and still lists its one package. Run at configure
// by packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake, so the branch is compiled and executed, not merely generated.
#include <cstddef>

#include "graph/Packages.hpp"

extern "C" const rp_package* rp_fixture_entry(void);

int main() {
    std::size_t resources = 12345;
    if (rp_embedded_resources(&resources) != nullptr) return 1;
    if (resources != 0) return 2;

    std::size_t packages = 0;
    const rp_package* const* list = rp_register_packages(&packages);
    if (list == nullptr || packages != 1 || list[0] != rp_fixture_entry()) return 3;
    return 0;
}
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The tests, the paths, and the devDependency a test opens**

`EngineGraph.test.cpp`'s `[resource]` case holds that `{ embedded: "mgb" }` answers a resource whose bytes are the
ROM's file byte for byte (a `std::equal` over `readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH)`), and that an unknown id is refused with
`"nope" is not an embedded ROM`; `SystemNode.test.cpp`'s `[resource]` fixtures take the bytes from the table
(`rp::graph::embeddedResource("mgb")`) in place of `rp::embeddedMgbRom()`. `EngineSampleRate.test.cpp` and the three
sameboy test files name the ROM's new path in their `#error` texts; `sameboy`'s CMakeLists sets `RP_MGB_ROM_PATH` to
`packages/mgb/rom/mGB.gb`, and its manifest declares `@retroplug/mgb` a **devDependency**, which is what lets a TEST
target reach another package's file. `tests.cmake` sets the same path for the two shell binaries that need a path
rather than bytes (`retroplug-audio-test`'s sample-rate case and `engine-graph`'s render specs), keeps the
`retroplug-testing` links and adds the product fixture's driving. Every TypeScript path follows:
`run-native-tests.mjs` gains `__MGB_ROM__` (the file is a package's now, not a resource of `resources/`), the five
`test-native` files use it, `run-ui-tests.mjs` copies the package's file, the node test joins the new path,
`check-boundaries.mjs` and its test gain the use-attribution rule Step 4's fixtures hold, and
`boundaries-checker.test.ts` counts its one warning. `pnpm-lock.yaml` gains the dev-only edge


(The `TinyUSB submodule has not been initialized` hint above it is `/opt/pico-sdk`'s own: the check needs no USB, which is why it uses that SDK.)

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f2pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

Run: `bash -c 'R="(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) [ 0-9][0-9] 20[0-9]{2}"; for e in build-device/rp-device-check.elf; do arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary $e /tmp/f2-img.bin && LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -E "$R" /tmp/f2-img.bin && LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/$R/Nov  4 2026/" /tmp/f2-img.bin | sha256sum; done; rm -f /tmp/f2-img.bin'`

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
F2 stage 3: embedded resources a package declares, and the product's table

The mGB ROM stops being a closed `id == "mgb"` in a header the shell owns and becomes a package's declared resource
(docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 5).

A manifest's `embed` member is a list of { "id", "file" } (cmake/packages.cmake): `id` is a C identifier, since it names
the generated array, and `file` is relative to the package's own directory, resolves inside it, exists and is not empty.
A package may contribute nothing but an `embed`, which `mgb` now does: it has no native code, and its ROM is all it
gives a product. `git mv resources/roms/mGB.gb packages/mgb/rom/mGB.gb`, and its manifest names the file.
`retroplug_package` gives every package with embeds an object library `retroplug-<package>-embeds`, built through
cmake/bin2c.cmake into one array and length per entry under a symbol `_retroplug_embed_symbol` derives from the package
and the id: the one place that name is derived, so the array and the table that points at it cannot disagree.

`retroplug_product` generates `rp_embedded_resources()` beside `rp_register_packages()`, in the product's generated
source and over its packages in product order, and links their embed libraries. The table is a function-local static,
set up at the first call as `rp_register_packages` is: its rows read each array's length from the object the package's
embed library defines, which is no constant expression in the product's translation unit, so a namespace-scope table
would be one static initialiser running before any caller could ask (`nm` shows no `_GLOBAL__sub_I_` from it). Two
configure refusals: an id two of a product's packages both embed, and two of them whose ids run together to one C name
(`lsdj` with `launchpad_kit` beside `lsdj-launchpad` with `kit`), each naming both packages, since a duplicate-symbol
link error is no configure refusal. Both names an entry defines are compared, the array and bin2c's `<symbol>_len`, so
package `alpha` with id `rom` and package `alpha_rom` with id `len` are refused for wanting one length object twice
(bin2c.cmake, and cmake/check-embeds.cmake's fixture for it). graph/Packages.hpp declares the table's C-compatible type
and function beside the registration list, with an `embeddedResource(id)` span over it. EngineRpcService::putResource's
`embedded` branch looks the id up there instead of rp::embeddedRom(): an id the product does not carry is refused in
exactly the words it always was. EmbeddedRoms.hpp and the root `mgb-rom` target with its custom command go, and so do
the comments that said SameBoyBackend resolved the marker. A DEVICE product emits no table: it reaches no embedded
resource, so no device image's bytes move (the two image hashes are identical), and Packages.hpp says a device product
defines none.

The wire is unchanged. TS still sends `{ embedded: "mgb" }` (the stores' loadMgb, the CLI SDK, the menu), putResource
still answers a resource id, and every test-native suite runs it through the real host.

Tests: the putResource case holds that the marker resolves to the ROM's file byte for byte and that an unknown id is
refused with `"<id>" is not an embedded ROM`. The configure holds ten manifest refusals (an id that is not a C
identifier, a file outside the package, a missing file, an absolute path, a member that is no list, an empty list, no
id, an id twice in one package, no file, an empty file), an embed-only manifest that reads, and a script-mode fixture
(cmake/check-embeds.cmake over scratch packages) for the duplicate id across one product and for the colliding symbol,
each with a pair that must hold. Broken red first: with the table's lookup never matching, the putResource case fails on
the marker's error before the bytes are compared; with the symbol rule removed, the colliding pair's table reads with
one symbol twice.

Which binary reads mGB.gb, and why: retroplug-sameboy-test, retroplug-engine-graph-test and retroplug-audio-test keep
RP_MGB_ROM_PATH, retargeted at packages/mgb/rom/mGB.gb. The sample-rate case and the engine-job render specs need a
PATH, not bytes, so the product's table is no use to them; retroplug-engine-graph-test and -audio-test are products and
could reach either, and the console test binary links no backend at all. sameboy's package declares `@retroplug/mgb` as
a devDependency for it, and the native boundary check now reads a target's COMPILE_DEFINITIONS as well as its links and
include directories, so a test binary's path into another package's tree is judged like a link (a library target may not
take one). packages/native's own tests are the shell's, and the shell is exempt from that check and declares every
package in packages/retroplug, not in its own manifest. The value is unwrapped first (`_retroplug_unquote_path`): every
DEFS in the tree writes its path quoted, NAME="${...}", and a target property keeps those quotes, so a quoted definition
is judged as the path it names, in the boundary check and in the gatherer that feeds it. Both fixtures have a quoted
twin (refused without the mgb devDependency, holding with it), and the real case is what they now cover: dropping mgb
from sameboy's devDependencies turns the configure red on retroplug-sameboy-test's RP_MGB_ROM_PATH. The engine-graph
tests that included EmbeddedRoms.hpp reach the bytes through the product's table. test-native reaches the file through a
new __MGB_ROM__ define, the CLI's render smoke and the UI runner's copy were retargeted with it, every #error text names
the new path, and test-native/systems.test.ts names the table rather than rp::embeddedRom.

The TypeScript boundary checker gained the case its use-attribution needed: a fixture package whose native target names
one declared dependency's file by path (a use) and whose CMakeLists mentions another's in a comment (no use, and the
warning says so), so the comment stripping and the path rule are both held.

Docs: spec/06's "Adding a package" carries the `embed` member, what it is for, that mgb has no native code, and the
devDependency rule its own tests rely on; spec/02's putResource table and its shared-classes row say where a baked-in
ROM lives now.
````

### Task 4: txiki and efsw as the shell's opt-in libraries

Design section 6 and 9's fourth stage. Two shell libraries, each linked by the products that use it.
`retroplug-tjs-runtime` compiles dpf.js's `TjsHostRuntime.cpp` and links `tjs` (which brings `qjs` and libuv); its users
are the products that run the control plane on txiki - the headless host, the CLI, the SDL standalone, the plugin and
`retroplug-classid-test`. `retroplug-file-watcher` compiles `NativeFileWatcher.cpp` and links `efsw-static` with
`Threads::Threads`, and `HostRpcService` holds a `FileWatcher` interface instead of the concrete watcher, so
`enableWatching` takes one and every host but the plugin passes none.

The backend is then bare QuickJS: `TjsHostRuntime.cpp` and `NativeFileWatcher.cpp` leave its sources, `tjs` and
`efsw-static` leave its links for `qjs`, and `RenderHost.cpp`'s include of `host/QuickJsGlobals.hpp` keeps working because
that header and `GamepadPump.hpp` are reduced to `quickjs.h` - neither names the txiki class, so the split the design
asked about was not needed. A configure check, `retroplug_check_runtime_libraries`, refuses a configure in which the Node
addon, `retroplug-render-host-test`, the backend, the engine-graph test or the audio test carries `tjs`, `uv_a` or
`efsw` in its link closure, naming the whole path; a gather fixture holds it, and the real tree was proved too.

The design expected the QuickJS-only binaries to shrink by txiki's host. They shrank by about 296 KB each, and the cause
is efsw: `HostRpcService`'s constructor named `NativeFileWatcher`, so every binary that linked the backend pulled its
object and, through it, efsw's. `TjsHostRuntime.cpp.o` is 10 KB, and a binary that never created a txiki runtime never
pulled it. The report says so, and this task's fixtures hold the shapes that would hide it again.

- Create (2): `packages/native/src/host/rpc/FileWatcher.hpp`, `packages/native/test/host/HostRpcWatching.test.cpp`
- Modify (17 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 3 under `packages/native/cmake/`; 3 under `packages/native/src/host/rpc/`; 2 under `spec/`; 1 under `AGENTS.md`; 1 under `CMakeLists.txt`; 1 under `cmake/` and the rest)

- [ ] **Step 1: The two libraries, the interface, and the backend on bare QuickJS**

`packages/native/CMakeLists.txt` defines the two STATIC libraries (C++20, PIC, `src/` as the PUBLIC include root),
drops `TjsHostRuntime.cpp` and `NativeFileWatcher.cpp` from `retroplug-backend`'s sources, its dpf.js and txiki
include roots, and its `tjs` and `efsw-static` links, and links `qjs` in their place - with the comment that says what
the backend's QuickJS is (the script host, the compiler and the render host). Every includer of the txiki host links
the new library itself: the headless host, the CLI, the SDL executable, the plugin's DSP library (PUBLIC, so the UI
library and every format inherit it) and `retroplug-classid-test`. `FileWatcher.hpp` is the service's two calls
(`drainChangedPaths`, `setWatchedRoms`) and nothing else; `HostRpcService` holds a `std::unique_ptr<FileWatcher>`,
includes the interface instead of efsw, and `enableWatching(std::unique_ptr<FileWatcher>)` stores the first watcher it
is given (idempotent; a null changes nothing) - with none, `drainChangedPaths` returns `{}` and `setWatchedRoms`
returns `false`, the same three lines as before, so watching-off behaviour is byte for byte today's.
`NativeFileWatcher` implements both interfaces, and its own `efsw::FileWatcher` member stays ITS last member so the
efsw thread is joined before the state its callback touches goes. The plugin builds the only `NativeFileWatcher` in
the tree and links the library; `QuickJsGlobals.hpp` and `GamepadPump.hpp` include `quickjs.h` alone; `warnings.cmake`
puts `/W4 /WX` on the two new targets and `plugin.cmake`'s and the root's comments follow.

Create `packages/native/src/host/rpc/FileWatcher.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <string>
#include <vector>

// The file watcher a host hands HostRpcService (spec/07): the two calls the service forwards and nothing else, so the
// service, and every includer of its header, is clear of a watcher library's headers and of its link. The native one
// (retroplug-file-watcher's NativeFileWatcher, over efsw) is what the plugin builds; a host that watches nothing passes
// nothing, and drainChangedPaths then answers empty while setWatchedRoms answers false, as watching off always did.
//
// Policy is the caller's: this reports paths that changed, and the control plane's TS decides what a change means.
class FileWatcher {
public:
    virtual ~FileWatcher() = default;

    // The paths that changed since the last call, deduplicated downstream. Called on the host's UI thread.
    virtual std::vector<std::string> drainChangedPaths() = 0;

    // Replace the set of ROM files to watch, by path: a watcher watches their parent directories and filters by
    // basename, so a ROM whose sibling changes is not reported. Called on the host's UI thread, as drainChangedPaths
    // is.
    virtual void setWatchedRoms(const std::vector<std::string>& paths) = 0;
};
````

- [ ] **Step 2: The runtime-libraries check, and the fixtures that hold it**

`retroplug_check_runtime_libraries` (in `cmake/packages.cmake`, deferred beside `retroplug_check_products`) walks
every named target's link closure breadth-first, keeping the chain that reached each library, and refuses one that
carries `tjs`, `uv_a`, `uv` or `efsw` - naming the target and the whole path (`a -> b -> tjs`). Its default list is
the five targets the design names, and its optional `TARGETS` argument is how the fixture project drives it. A guarded
name no target has is refused too (a renamed binary used to drop out silently), with `retroplug-node` the one absence
allowed, and only when `RETROPLUG_NODE_ADDON` is off. The gather project gains `runtime-library` (a scratch audio test
that links a scratch `tjs`, refused), `runtime-bare` (the same with nothing linked, holds), `runtime-chain` (a scratch
interface library over `tjs`, so the message must name three steps), `runtime-missing` (a name no target has, refused)
and `runtime-addon-off` (`retroplug-node` with the addon off, holds). `packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake` drives them,
beside the boundary fixtures it already drives.

````diff
+
+# retroplug_check_runtime_libraries(): refuses, at configure time, a target that must stay a bare-QuickJS host or an
+# engine binary carrying a runtime library it does not want (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 6): txiki's
+# host (`tjs`), libuv (`uv_a`) or efsw, in the link closure of the Node addon, the render host, the backend or the two
+# engine test binaries. The two host runtime libraries are the shell's (packages/native's retroplug-tjs-runtime and
+# retroplug-file-watcher), and only the products that instantiate a txiki host or want a watcher link them; a test that
+# links the engine and so carries one anyway is a build that would hide that. The walk keeps the path that reached each
+# library, so the message says what brought it in, step by step, not only that it is there. A guarded name with no
+# target is refused, since the rule would otherwise stop covering a renamed binary; the opt-in Node addon, when it is
+# not configured, is the one name allowed to be absent.
+#
+# TARGETS is for a configure fixture to drive the rule over a scratch target (packages/native/test/packages/gather): the
+# default is the five binaries the rule is about.
+function(retroplug_check_runtime_libraries)
+    cmake_parse_arguments(C "" "" "TARGETS" ${ARGN})
+    if(C_UNPARSED_ARGUMENTS)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_check_runtime_libraries: unrecognised argument(s): ${C_UNPARSED_ARGUMENTS}")
+    endif()
+    set(_guarded ${C_TARGETS})
+    if(NOT _guarded)
+        set(_guarded retroplug-backend retroplug-node retroplug-render-host-test retroplug-engine-graph-test
+                       retroplug-audio-test)
+    endif()
+    set(_forbidden tjs uv_a uv efsw-static efsw)
+    _retroplug_build_targets(_targets "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")
+    # Every target's own link names, so a closure is followed without asking the generator to evaluate a target's.
+    foreach(_t IN LISTS _targets)
+        _retroplug_linked_names(_names_${_t} ${_t} LINK_LIBRARIES INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES)
+    endforeach()
+    set(_found "")
+    foreach(_root IN LISTS _guarded)
+        if(NOT TARGET ${_root})
+            # A name that is absent is a target this rule would stop covering, so it is refused. The one exception is
+            # the Node addon, which is opt-in and may simply not be configured.
+            if(_root STREQUAL "retroplug-node" AND NOT RETROPLUG_NODE_ADDON)
+                continue()
+            endif()
+            message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_check_runtime_libraries: `${_root}` is one of the targets this rule guards "
+                                "and this build defines no target of that name, so the rule would cover nothing; name "
+                                "the target here after renaming it (only the opt-in Node addon may be absent, when "
+                                "RETROPLUG_NODE_ADDON is off)")
+        endif()
+        # Breadth-first from the target, each queue entry "path@name": path is every step that reached this one, joined
+        # with @ so the message can name the intermediate that brought the library in (a target or library name holds
+        # no @, and a pipe would split the path itself).
+        set(_pending "${_root}")
+        set(_seen "")
+        while(_pending)
+            list(POP_FRONT _pending _entry)
+            string(FIND "${_entry}" "@" _at REVERSE)
+            if(_at EQUAL -1)
+                set(_name "${_entry}")
+            else()
+                math(EXPR _at "${_at} + 1")
+                string(SUBSTRING "${_entry}" ${_at} -1 _name)
+            endif()
+            if(_name IN_LIST _forbidden)
+                string(REPLACE "@" " -> " _path "${_entry}")
+                list(APPEND _found "${_path}")
+                break()
+            endif()
+            if(_name IN_LIST _seen)
+                continue()
+            endif()
+            list(APPEND _seen ${_name})
+            foreach(_next IN LISTS _names_${_name})
+                if(NOT _next MATCHES "-NOTFOUND$")
+                    list(APPEND _pending "${_entry}@${_next}")
+                endif()
+            endforeach()
+        endwhile()
+    endforeach()
+    if(_found)
+        list(JOIN _found "; " _found)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_check_runtime_libraries: these targets carry a host runtime library they must "
+                            "not (txiki's tjs, libuv's uv_a or efsw): ${_found}. The two host runtime libraries are "
+                            "the shell's own (retroplug-tjs-runtime, retroplug-file-watcher), and only the products "
+                            "that instantiate a txiki host or want a file watcher link them.")
     endif()
 endfunction()
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The tests: a fake watcher, and the two libraries' own cases**

`HostRpcWatching.test.cpp` moves the service's gate case out of the watcher test and into `retroplug-audio-test`, over
a `FakeFileWatcher` that counts its drains, its ROM sets and its live instances: inert with no watcher;
`enableWatching(nullptr)` changes nothing; the first watcher is forwarded to (`setWatchedRoms` true and recorded,
`drainChangedPaths` its paths, a second drain empty); a SECOND watcher is dropped at once (the live count is back
where it was) and the first keeps serving - with each fake's counters in a `std::shared_ptr` the test owns, so "the
first still serves, the second never did" is read from live memory even if `enableWatching` ever replaced the watcher.
`retroplug-watcher-test` keeps the real efsw cases over a scratch config dir (2 cases) and links the watcher library
alone, so it is no engine carrier and no longer needs an `EXEMPT` entry.

Create `packages/native/test/host/HostRpcWatching.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// HostRpcService's watcher gate (spec/07): the service forwards its two watcher calls to the watcher a host hands it,
// and is inert until one is handed over, which is what the test host and the CLI (which watch nothing) rely on. The
// watcher here is a fake, so the case pins the gate itself; the real one is efsw's, and NativeFileWatcher's own cases
// in retroplug-watcher-test hold that, in a binary that links the watcher library alone.
//
// It lives in this binary because the service is a backend object and this is a product binary that already links the
// backend and builds a host (EngineInvoker.test.cpp, beside it); a binary of its own would be a second engine carrier
// for three assertions.

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "host/rpc/FileWatcher.hpp"
#include "host/rpc/HostRpcService.hpp"

namespace {

// What a fake was asked to do, held apart from the fake itself: the case reads it AFTER handing the fake over, and if
// the service ever dropped that watcher the object would be gone, so the counts live in memory the test owns and a
// regression fails an assertion instead of touching freed memory.
struct WatcherCalls {
    std::vector<std::string> pending;
    std::vector<std::string> roms;
    int drains = 0;
    int romSets = 0;
};

// Counts the calls it is asked to forward, and hands back what it was told it had seen: enough to say which watcher a
// call reached, and that a second one never gets one.
class FakeFileWatcher : public FileWatcher {
public:
    explicit FakeFileWatcher(std::shared_ptr<WatcherCalls> calls) : _calls(std::move(calls)) { ++live; }
    ~FakeFileWatcher() override { --live; }

    std::vector<std::string> drainChangedPaths() override {
        ++_calls->drains;
        std::vector<std::string> out = _calls->pending;
        _calls->pending.clear();
        return out;
    }
    void setWatchedRoms(const std::vector<std::string>& paths) override {
        ++_calls->romSets;
        _calls->roms = paths;
    }

    // How many fakes are alive, so a watcher the service refuses is seen to be freed at once rather than served.
    static inline int live = 0;

private:
    std::shared_ptr<WatcherCalls> _calls;
};

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("HostRpcService forwards to the one watcher it was handed", "[watcher]") {
    HostRpcService svc;

    // Inert until a watcher is handed over.
    CHECK(svc.drainChangedPaths().empty());
    CHECK_FALSE(svc.setWatchedRoms({"a.gb"}));

    // Handing none is the same as never enabling watching: the opt-in call may be made with nothing to opt in with.
    svc.enableWatching(nullptr);
    CHECK(svc.drainChangedPaths().empty());
    CHECK_FALSE(svc.setWatchedRoms({"a.gb"}));

    auto firstCalls = std::make_shared<WatcherCalls>();
    firstCalls->pending = {"a.gb"};
    svc.enableWatching(std::make_unique<FakeFileWatcher>(firstCalls));

    CHECK(svc.setWatchedRoms({"a.gb"}));
    CHECK(firstCalls->roms == std::vector<std::string>{"a.gb"});
    CHECK(svc.drainChangedPaths() == std::vector<std::string>{"a.gb"});
    CHECK(svc.drainChangedPaths().empty());
    CHECK(firstCalls->drains == 2);

    // A second watcher is dropped: the first is the service's, so enabling watching twice is idempotent (and the
    // dropped one is freed at once, never handed a call). Both fakes' counts outlive their objects, which is what makes
    // "the first still serves, the second never did" an assertion rather than a read of whatever the service kept.
    const int liveBefore = FakeFileWatcher::live;
    auto secondCalls = std::make_shared<WatcherCalls>();
    svc.enableWatching(std::make_unique<FakeFileWatcher>(secondCalls));
    CHECK(FakeFileWatcher::live == liveBefore);
    CHECK(svc.setWatchedRoms({"b.gb"}));
    CHECK(firstCalls->roms == std::vector<std::string>{"b.gb"});
    CHECK(firstCalls->romSets == 2);
    CHECK(secondCalls->romSets == 0);
    CHECK(secondCalls->drains == 0);
}
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f2pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````bash
The backend stops carrying txiki's host and efsw, and the two become shell libraries that only the hosts using them link

`retroplug-tjs-runtime` (packages/native, STATIC, on the /W4 /WX list) compiles dpf.js's `TjsHostRuntime.cpp` and links

`retroplug-file-watcher` (STATIC) holds `NativeFileWatcher.{hpp,cpp}` over `efsw-static` and `Threads::Threads`. It adds
the threads itself: efsw's own CMake gives them to its shared library alone, and this library is `efsw-static`'s only
consumer now, so its link interface is whole for a host that takes it and nothing else (the root's efsw comment and the

service forwards, `drainChangedPaths` and `setWatchedRoms`, and a virtual destructor, so no includer of

answers empty and `setWatchedRoms` false, exactly as watching off did. The plugin's PluginDSP.cpp builds the one
NativeFileWatcher in the tree and hands it over (`make_unique<NativeFileWatcher>(configDir())`), and links the library.
The teardown rule is NativeFileWatcher's, and is stated where it holds: its `efsw::FileWatcher watcher_` is its LAST
member, so the efsw thread is joined before the state its callback touches (`mutex_`, `changed_`, `watchedRoms_`) is
destroyed. HostRpcService's member order is no rule at all: nothing calls back into the service, whose two watcher calls

`retroplug-backend` links `qjs` (bare QuickJS) instead of `tjs`, and `efsw-static` is gone: its script host, its
compiler and its render host are bare QuickJS, and its own include list drops dpf.js's src root and txiki's src now that

in which retroplug-backend, retroplug-node, retroplug-render-host-test, retroplug-engine-graph-test or
````
