### Task 5: Mesen's per-console compile-out, and the docs pass

Design sections 4, 10 and 9's fifth stage, plus the phase's prose. The Mesen library stops carrying the consoles
RetroPlug never runs, by an option per console: `MESEN_ENABLE_SNES`, `MESEN_ENABLE_PCE` and `MESEN_ENABLE_WS`, declared
in `deps/mesen/CMakeLists.txt` **default ON** (upstream's behaviour, so the vendored directory still builds as Mesen) and
set **OFF** by the root `CMakeLists.txt` before `add_subdirectory(deps/mesen)`, so a `-D` overrides them and
`build.sh`/`build.bat` pass `-D` through. `SNES` covers the Game Boy (Super Game Boy couples them both ways); NES, GBA and
SMS are always built. Each option is a PUBLIC compile definition of the `mesen` target, so the translation units that
include Mesen's headers see the same guards the library was built with.

The filter is a table of console, directories, evaluator CPUs and units kept, one row per switch, written so a further
switch is one more row; it drops `Core/<Dir>/` for each disabled console (nested directories included) and its CPUs'
`Debugger/ExpressionEvaluator.<Cpu>.cpp` files, and keeps two SNES shims that other consoles construct
(`SNES/Input/SnesController.cpp` is the input hub, `SNES/SnesDefaultVideoFilter.cpp` the video fallback). Only `.cpp`
sources are filtered: headers stay, so every `#include` keeps compiling and only a call or a construction into a dropped
unit needs a guard.

The guards are 123 `#if MESEN_ENABLE_*` blocks, about 260 added lines, in six files, each run marked `// RetroPlug:` as
the vendored tree's other edits are (the tree has no `.git` of its own; upstream is SourMesen/Mesen2 at `b9fa69d`). The
design's estimate was ~300 lines over the same six files, and the count is the report's: 3 in `Emulator.cpp`, 72 in
`Debugger.cpp`, 14 in `MemoryDumper.cpp`, 25 in `DisassemblyInfo.cpp`, 3 in `Disassembler.cpp` and 6 in
`ExpressionEvaluator.cpp`. A guarded switch that has a `default` keeps it; one without falls past the switch, which is
unreachable because the console cannot be constructed. `MemoryDumper`'s `dynamic_cast` chain is the one kept passage whose
text moved: it is re-split around its guards, with the same tests in the same order.

The risk the guards carry is that a plain `switch` over a template parameter references every arm at `-O0`, so a missed
guard links under Release and fails under Debug. That is why the proof is two-way and why both ways are a script: the ON
mode builds the library and the CLI in Release with the three ON and asserts the four console symbol counts in the CLI,
and `--off` builds the library alone at `-O0` with the three OFF and fails on any undefined symbol that names a
compiled-out unit. The library drops 138 of 426 translation units and 12.3 MB of 31.1 MB of objects.

**Files:**

- Create (1): `tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh`
- Modify (23 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 6 under `spec/`; 5 under `deps/mesen/Core/Debugger/`; 5 under `docs/`; 1 under `.gitignore`; 1 under `AGENTS.md`; 1 under `CMakeLists.txt` and the rest)

- [ ] **Step 1: The options, the table, and the root's defaults**

`deps/mesen/CMakeLists.txt`'s header comment is rewritten (an archive member is pulled whole, the consoles reference
each other, and this pass IS the per-system pruning the old text deferred), the three options are declared, the filter
table is defined, and the source list is filtered per disabled console before the target is made. The table's rows are
`|`-separated and their fields `,`-separated because a `;` would split a row into another list item - the first draft
did exactly that, and the configure died on `list index out of range`, which the table's comment records. The
directory match is anchored to the source root, which is escaped first so a checkout path is a literal, so a path that
happens to contain `/Core/SNES/` does not lose unrelated units. The root `CMakeLists.txt` sets the three `OFF CACHE
BOOL` (no `FORCE`) before `add_subdirectory(deps/mesen)`, and its comment says what release builds get: the root's
defaults, which are OFF, and only a configure that passes `-D...=ON` (the script) builds the rest.

````diff
diff --git a/CMakeLists.txt b/CMakeLists.txt
index 73cdb8eb5..be3e8a842 100644
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -227,6 +227,13 @@ include(cmake/serial.cmake)
 include(cmake/rtmidi.cmake)
 
 # --- Mesen: NES emulator core (multi-system upstream; we use the NES path) ---
+# The consoles RetroPlug never runs are compiled out (deps/mesen/CMakeLists.txt): the Super Nintendo with the Game Boy
+# (Super Game Boy couples them), the PC Engine and the WonderSwan. These are cache defaults, so a -D overrides any of
+# them: a release build uses these OFF defaults, and only a configure that passes -D...=ON builds the rest
+# (tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh, which proves that side). NES, GBA and SMS are always built.
+set(MESEN_ENABLE_SNES OFF CACHE BOOL "Build Mesen's Super Nintendo and Game Boy cores")
+set(MESEN_ENABLE_PCE OFF CACHE BOOL "Build Mesen's PC Engine core")
+set(MESEN_ENABLE_WS OFF CACHE BOOL "Build Mesen's WonderSwan core")
 add_subdirectory(deps/mesen)
 
 # --- r8brain-free: high-quality SRC for LSDJ kit compilation.
diff --git a/deps/mesen/CMakeLists.txt b/deps/mesen/CMakeLists.txt
index 6f40b3a64..059ba5e36 100644
--- a/deps/mesen/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/deps/mesen/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -1,10 +1,12 @@
 # Vendored Mesen2 emulator core, built as a static lib for RetroPlug.
 #
-# Per the porting plan: include the whole tree as-is. Mesen's internal coupling
-# makes per-system pruning a project on its own; binary-size optimisation is
-# deferred to a later pass. We just glob every .cpp/.c under the four roots
-# (Core/, Utilities/, Lua/, SevenZip/) and let the linker drop unreferenced
-# objects from the final plugin.
+# We glob every .cpp/.c under the two roots (Core/, Utilities/) plus Lua's and SevenZip's C sources, and drop the
+# consoles RetroPlug never runs through the MESEN_ENABLE_* options below: RetroPlug emulates the NES, the GBA and the
+# SMS/GG, so the root CMakeLists sets the Super Nintendo (with the Game Boy), PC Engine and WonderSwan options OFF.
+# An object the linker never pulls would not have cost the build anything, but an archive member IS pulled whole:
+# mesen's consoles reference each other (Super Game Boy, the ST018 coprocessor), so the cut is a compile-out and every
+# console costs its own translation units until it is switched off. The filter's table is the record of what each
+# switch drops, so a further console is one more row.
 
 file(GLOB_RECURSE MESEN_CPP_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
     "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/Core/*.cpp"
@@ -15,6 +17,56 @@ file(GLOB_RECURSE MESEN_C_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
     "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/Lua/*.c"
     "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/SevenZip/*.c")
 
+# Mesen's console compile-outs: one option per console RetroPlug may drop, ON by default, which is how upstream Mesen
+# builds (the vendored directory still builds as Mesen). Each is a PUBLIC compile definition, so a consumer including
+# Mesen's headers sees the same guards the library was built with (Emulator.cpp's ROM detection among them).
+#
+# SNES covers the Game Boy too: the two are coupled through Super Game Boy (a SNES constructs a Game Boy, and the Game
+# Boy's SGB support calls back into SNES), so one switch is honest about both. NES, GBA and SMS are always built: this
+# filter has no switch for them, and nothing in this tree would turn one off.
+option(MESEN_ENABLE_SNES "Build Mesen's Super Nintendo and Game Boy cores" ON)
+option(MESEN_ENABLE_PCE "Build Mesen's PC Engine core" ON)
+option(MESEN_ENABLE_WS "Build Mesen's WonderSwan core" ON)
+
+# The filter's table: one row per switch, `|`-separated as option | directories | evaluators | units kept, each list
+# comma-separated so a row stays one list item (a `;` would split the row into another item, since CMake lists are
+# `;`-separated). A disabled console drops every .cpp under its directories (nested ones included) and its CPUs'
+# ExpressionEvaluator, and keeps the units listed in the fourth field. Only .cpp files are filtered: the headers stay on
+# disk, so every #include keeps compiling and only a call or a construction into a dropped unit needs a guard (the
+# `// RetroPlug:` blocks in Core).
+set(_mesen_console_filter
+    # The SNES's own debugger evaluators are its CPUs', the SPC among them; `/Core/SNES/Input/SnesController.cpp` is
+    # the input hub every console's control manager builds (NES included) and `/Core/SNES/SnesDefaultVideoFilter.cpp`
+    # is Emulator::GetVideoFilter's fallback, so both stay.
+    "MESEN_ENABLE_SNES|Core/SNES,Core/Gameboy|Snes,Spc,Gsu,Cx4,NecDsp,St018,Gameboy|Core/SNES/Input/SnesController.cpp,Core/SNES/SnesDefaultVideoFilter.cpp"
+    "MESEN_ENABLE_PCE|Core/PCE|Pce|"
+    "MESEN_ENABLE_WS|Core/WS|Ws|")
+# A directory is matched at the start of each path, so a checkout whose own path happens to contain `/Core/SNES/` does
+# not lose unrelated units. The root is escaped first, so it is a literal rather than a pattern.
+string(REGEX REPLACE "([][+.*()^$?\\\\])" "\\\\\\1" _mesen_source_root "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}")
+foreach(_row IN LISTS _mesen_console_filter)
+    string(REPLACE "|" ";" _row "${_row}")
+    list(GET _row 0 _mesen_option)
+    list(GET _row 1 _mesen_dirs)
+    list(GET _row 2 _mesen_evaluators)
+    list(GET _row 3 _mesen_kept)
+    string(REPLACE "," ";" _mesen_dirs "${_mesen_dirs}")
+    string(REPLACE "," ";" _mesen_evaluators "${_mesen_evaluators}")
+    string(REPLACE "," ";" _mesen_kept "${_mesen_kept}")
+    if(${_mesen_option})
+        continue()
+    endif()
+    foreach(_dir IN LISTS _mesen_dirs)
+        list(FILTER MESEN_CPP_SOURCES EXCLUDE REGEX "^${_mesen_source_root}/${_dir}/")
+    endforeach()
+    foreach(_evaluator IN LISTS _mesen_evaluators)
+        list(FILTER MESEN_CPP_SOURCES EXCLUDE REGEX "/ExpressionEvaluator\\.${_evaluator}\\.cpp$")
+    endforeach()
+    foreach(_unit IN LISTS _mesen_kept)
+        list(APPEND MESEN_CPP_SOURCES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/${_unit}")
+    endforeach()
+endforeach()
+
 # Lua bundles its own `lua.c` (the standalone REPL) which has a `main()`.
 # Drop it — we link Lua as a library only.
 list(FILTER MESEN_C_SOURCES EXCLUDE REGEX "/lua\\.c$")
@@ -87,15 +139,24 @@ set_target_properties(mesen PROPERTIES
     POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON
 )
 
+# PUBLIC, so every consumer's TUs - MesenNesSystem.cpp and the rest - compile against the same console set as the
+# library they link, and `#if MESEN_ENABLE_*` in a Core header means the same thing on both sides.
+target_compile_definitions(mesen PUBLIC
+    MESEN_ENABLE_SNES=$<BOOL:${MESEN_ENABLE_SNES}>
+    MESEN_ENABLE_PCE=$<BOOL:${MESEN_ENABLE_PCE}>
+    MESEN_ENABLE_WS=$<BOOL:${MESEN_ENABLE_WS}>
+)
+
 # LTO for optimized configs only (Debug stays fast to build). Intra-mesen cross-TU inlining across the
 # hot CPU/PPU/APU stepping loop, which is ~99% of the audio-thread cost. Measured ~10% faster NES core
 # on the Cortex-A53 handheld (nes-bench: xRT 0.83 -> 0.92 over plain -O3). The single biggest safe lever
 # for NES perf there — JS is ~0.5% of the block, the emulator core dominates. Free at runtime.
 #
-# Not free at BUILD time, though: it makes every mesen object LTO bitcode, so each of the nine binaries
-# that link this lib re-runs codegen over all ~430 of them. That's why it's opt-in (RETROPLUG_MESEN_LTO,
-# declared in the root CMakeLists) rather than always-on — release.yml turns it on so shipped binaries
-# get the speedup, and the dev loop doesn't pay for it. Toggling the option recompiles mesen.
+# Not free at BUILD time, though: it makes every mesen object LTO bitcode, so each of the thirteen binaries
+# that link this lib re-runs codegen over its objects (288 with the consoles RetroPlug does not run compiled
+# out, 426 with MESEN_ENABLE_SNES/-PCE/-WS all on). That's why it's opt-in (RETROPLUG_MESEN_LTO, declared in
+# the root CMakeLists) rather than always-on - release.yml turns it on so shipped binaries get the speedup,
+# and the dev loop doesn't pay for it. Toggling the option recompiles mesen.
 if(RETROPLUG_MESEN_LTO)
     set_target_properties(mesen PROPERTIES
         INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION_RELEASE ON
@@ -103,7 +164,7 @@ if(RETROPLUG_MESEN_LTO)
     )
     # Under LTO the codegen happens at LINK time, in a process that takes its warning flags from the LINK
     # command line - so the -w further down, which is a per-TU compile option, does not reach it. Two of
-    # Mesen's warnings come back at every one of the nine links, and one of them (-Wodr on
+    # Mesen's warnings come back at every one of the thirteen links, and one of them (-Wodr on
     # Utilities/NTSC/nes_ntsc_impl.h) is a whole-program check that exists ONLY at link time and has no
     # compile-time form at all. That pair is what "mesen scrolls past on every build" has always been.
     #

- [ ] **Step 2: The guards, one file per block**

Six files, each with its own diff below, in the vendored tree's own style: the directives at column 0, a `//
RetroPlug:` comment on each run's `#if`, and added lines only but for `MemoryDumper`'s chain re-split.
`Emulator.cpp`'s three are `TryLoadRom`'s per-console signature checks (a console that is not built may not claim a
ROM). `Debugger.cpp`'s 72 are the debugger-construction switch, the CPU switches (cycle count, instruction, read and
write, memory access, idle, PPU read/write/cycle, scanline step, the debugger-enabled flags, the state copies, the PPU
state get and set, the ROM save), the `_DEBUG` evaluator self-test and the explicit instantiations.
`MemoryDumper.cpp`'s 14 are its `dynamic_cast` chain and the memory switches' per-console arms.
`DisassemblyInfo.cpp`'s 25 are the disassembler-data switches, `Disassembler.cpp`'s 3 `GetLineData`'s CPU switch, and
`ExpressionEvaluator.cpp`'s 6 the token switches, the nested CPU switch included.

- [ ] **Step 3: The two-way build script**

`tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh` has two modes and exits non-zero on any failure. With no argument it configures
`build-mesen-all/` in Release with the three options ON, builds `mesen` and `retroplug-cli`, and asserts each of
`SnesPpu`, `GbPpu`, `PceVdc` and `WsPpu` is non-zero **in the CLI** (a run whose options did not take effect now fails
instead of printing four zeros). With `--off` it configures `build-mesen-all-off/` as Debug (`-O0`) with the three
OFF, builds the `mesen` library alone, asserts the four counts are 0 in the archive, then reads every member's
undefined symbols against every member's defined ones, demangles the difference and fails on any remaining name with a
`::` that is no `std::`, `__cxxabiv1::` or `__gnu_cxx::` one - a call into a compiled-out unit, printed by name. `pnpm
build:mesen-all` is its ON mode, `.gitignore` ignores both directories beside the other build trees, and its
parallelism falls back the way `build.sh`'s does (`nproc`, else `sysctl -n hw.ncpu`).

Create `tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh`:

````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds Mesen with every console it emulates switched ON (MESEN_ENABLE_SNES / -PCE / -WS), which is upstream Mesen's
# own default and the one configuration RetroPlug's root CMakeLists turns off, and builds the OFF side a second way that
# catches a missed guard: at -O0 with the options OFF. The per-console compile-out is two-way, and the guards around a
# compiled-out console rot unnoticed if only the OFF Release build is ever compiled.
#
#   tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh [build dir]    # every console ON, Release (default build-mesen-all)
#   tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh --off [dir]    # every console OFF, Debug (-O0), default build-mesen-all-off
#
# The ON run configures a build directory of its own (the root's cache defaults are OFF, and this passes the three -D
# options through), builds the `mesen` library and `retroplug-cli`, and asserts each of the four consoles' symbols is in
# the CLI. Release, because that is what ships: the proof is that the ON side's guards hold where the drop is real.
#
# The OFF run configures its own directory as Debug and builds the `mesen` library alone. At -O0 a switch over a
# template parameter emits every arm instead of folding the unreachable ones away, so a call into a compiled-out console
# that Release left invisible is a reference in the archive. The archive is then held self-contained: no C++ symbol a
# member references may be one another member does not define (the C library's and libstdc++'s symbols resolve at the
# link, which this run does not do). A missed guard fails here even though it links in Release.
#
# Both modes exit non-zero on any failure, and print what they checked.
set -euo pipefail
repo="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$repo"

if command -v nproc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    jobs="$(nproc)"
else
    jobs="$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)"   # macOS / BSD
fi

mode="on"
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--off" ]]; then
    mode="off"
    shift
fi
case "$mode" in
    on) dir="${1:-build-mesen-all}" ;;
    off) dir="${1:-build-mesen-all-off}" ;;
esac

fail() {
    echo "tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# The four consoles' symbols, counted in <target> (a binary or an archive), printed one line: the OFF mode wants every
# count 0, the ON mode wants none of them 0, and a count 0 is the difference between the drop and its proof.
check_console_symbols() {
    local target="$1" want="$2"
    local snes gb pce ws
    snes="$(nm -C "$target" 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'SnesPpu::' || true)"
    gb="$(nm -C "$target" 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'GbPpu::' || true)"
    pce="$(nm -C "$target" 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'PceVdc::' || true)"
    ws="$(nm -C "$target" 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'WsPpu::' || true)"
    echo "SnesPpu $snes GbPpu $gb PceVdc $pce WsPpu $ws"
    local pair name count
    for pair in "SnesPpu:$snes" "GbPpu:$gb" "PceVdc:$pce" "WsPpu:$ws"; do
        name="${pair%%:*}"
        count="${pair#*:}"
        if [[ "$want" == "on" && "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
            fail "$name is absent from $target, so the all-consoles options did not take effect"
        fi
        if [[ "$want" == "off" && "$count" -ne 0 ]]; then
            fail "$name is in $target with the consoles OFF, so a console was not compiled out"
        fi
    done
}

if [[ "$mode" == "on" ]]; then
    cmake -S . -B "$dir" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -DMESEN_ENABLE_SNES=ON -DMESEN_ENABLE_PCE=ON -DMESEN_ENABLE_WS=ON
    cmake --build "$dir" --target mesen -j"$jobs"
    cmake --build "$dir" --target retroplug-cli -j"$jobs"
    check_console_symbols "$dir/bin/retroplug-cli" on
    echo "tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh: $dir built Mesen and the CLI with every console ON"
    exit 0
fi

cmake -S . -B "$dir" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DMESEN_ENABLE_SNES=OFF -DMESEN_ENABLE_PCE=OFF -DMESEN_ENABLE_WS=OFF
cmake --build "$dir" --target mesen -j"$jobs"

archive="$dir/deps/mesen/libmesen.a"
[[ -f "$archive" ]] || fail "$archive was not built"
check_console_symbols "$archive" off

scan="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${scan:?}"' EXIT
# An archive's references are per member: an undefined symbol of one member may be defined by any other (which is what
# pulls that member in at a real link), so the two sets are read over the whole archive and the difference is what
# nothing there defines. Weak undefined symbols are left out: they resolve to 0, which is not a dropped console.
nm "$archive" | awk 'NF == 2 && $1 == "U" { print $2 }' | sort -u > "$scan/undefined"
nm "$archive" | awk 'NF == 3 && $2 != "U" { print $3 }' | sort -u > "$scan/defined"
missing="$(comm -23 "$scan/undefined" "$scan/defined")"
# A mesen symbol is a C++ name in a class or namespace. What the archive legitimately leaves undefined is libstdc++'s
# and the C++ ABI's, their typeinfo and vtables included; anything else with a `::` is a member this archive lacks.
unresolved=""
if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
    unresolved="$(printf '%s\n' "$missing" | c++filt \
        | sed -E 's/^(typeinfo for|vtable for|VTT for|non-virtual thunk to|virtual thunk to) //' \
        | grep -E '::' | grep -Ev '^(std|__cxxabiv1|__gnu_cxx)::' || true)"
fi
if [[ -n "$unresolved" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$unresolved" >&2
    fail "$archive references $(printf '%s\n' "$unresolved" | wc -l) C++ symbol(s) no member defines, so a call into a compiled-out console was left unguarded"
fi
echo "tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh: $dir built Mesen at -O0 with every console OFF, and the archive references nothing it does not define"
````

 //     resolved, and a package's `files`/`publishConfig` is nobody's boundary here.
 //   - the ORDER a dependency's spec or an import reaches a package in, and anything a build's tooling decides: this
 //     check judges the declaration, not the build.
+//   - a `#` inside a quoted string in a CMakeLists: the comment stripper removes from a `#` to the end of its line
+//     whatever quotes surround it, so a target named after one is not seen as a use.
+//   - a multi-line bracket comment (`#[[ ... ]]`): the stripper removes the `#` line alone, so a target named inside
+//     one counts as a use.
 //
 // A declared dependency no file uses is a warning, not a refusal: the native check (cmake/packages.cmake) reads the same
 // declaration, so a package whose native targets link a dependency's library declares it without its TS importing

 # RetroPlug — architecture spec

+## 11. As built (the prototype)
+
+The prototype, on `proto/f2-native` over the design commit `a1373899d`, is five commits, one per stage, each built, reviewed
+(by Opus) and amended until its review passed. The review's fix passes were folded into the commit they belong to by
+fixup and autosquash, so the five trees stand as final; the sections above were corrected in place to what the build
+found. The plan is written against this record and executes on `feature/modularize`.
+
+**The stages**, by commit subject:
+
+1. `F2 stage 1: the system package, and a core built by the function its node carries`: `packages/system`, the request's
+   `build` and `config`, `rp.host.systems/2`, `Engine::buildSystem` on `request.build`, category-based recognition, the
+   deleted factory, backends and kind check, the null-build and fixture-console cases.
+2. `F2 stage 2: the consoles, host I/O, the product order and the tests`: `sameboy`, `mesen` (with the `n8` edge),
+   `host-io`, `retroplug-core` dissolved, the product list, the `[packages]` re-record, `retroplug-sameboy-test` and
+   `retroplug-mesen-test`, the moved clang-cl step and the boundary fixtures.
+3. `F2 stage 3: embedded resources a package declares, and the product's table`: the `embed` member, the per-package
+   object library, `rp_embedded_resources()`, `putResource` on it, `mGB.gb` in `packages/mgb`, the configure fixtures.
+4. `F2 stage 4: txiki and efsw as the shell's opt-in libraries`: `retroplug-tjs-runtime`, `retroplug-file-watcher`, the
+   `FileWatcher` interface, the backend on `qjs`, `retroplug_check_runtime_libraries`, the empty `EXEMPT` list.
+5. `F2 stage 5: Mesen's per-console compile-out, and the docs pass`: the three options, the filter table, the 123
+   guards, `tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh`, the measurements, the stale comments and the living docs.
+
+**Departures from the design as committed, and why.**
+
+- **A system node that built no core is refused before the plan publishes.** The design trusted the descriptor's category;
+  the stage 1 review found a node declaring it and building nothing would leave a null slot for the audio thread to
+  dereference in a release build. The planner gained a `PlanCheck` seam (`GraphHost::setGraph` threads it), and a script
+  pack declaring the category is refused by `ScriptHost::loadInto` and `MqjsHost::openControl`. A red-first rollback case
+  holds it; the planner path cannot show red by removing the check alone, since `setGraph` drops a refused outcome, so the
+  case is red by removing `~SystemNode`'s destroy.
+- **The Game Boy logo is private to `mesen`.** Stage 2 first put a shared `RomLogo.hpp` in `system` for the SMS gate; the
+  review found it made `system` know a console, and each package's `RomFormat.hpp` now holds its own.
+- **The test dependency rule.** Stage 3 needed `sameboy`'s tests to open `mgb`'s ROM, which the boundary check refused. A
+  test may declare another package as a `devDependency` for a fixture file, judged by target properties; the review found
+  the compile-definition door blind to the quoted form the tree uses, and fixtures now hold both sides.
+- **The `testing` package has a native library.** The shared C++ test helpers the two console test binaries need could not
+  live in either; `retroplug-testing` holds them and the products guard leaves it out. `LinkRomModel` stays there, with the
+  reason recorded.
+- **Embed symbols and the table.** The symbol is computed once as `rp_embed_<package>_<id>` and two entries that collide
+  are refused (the review found `lsdj` + `launchpad_kit` and `lsdj-launchpad` + `kit` would clash); the table is a
+  function-local static; a device product emits none (an empty one changed both box images through the symbol).
+- **The runtime-libraries check names the whole path.** It first reported only target and library, cutting at the first
+  edge; it now names the chain. The file watcher library also gained the `Threads` link it lacked.
+- **`EXEMPT` is empty.** The class-id test links no backend; the watcher test drives `HostRpcService` with a fake
+  `FileWatcher`, which the interface made possible. `QuickJsGlobals.hpp` did not split.
+- **The size result's cause.** Every backend product lost about 296 KB in stage 4 because `HostRpcService`'s
+  `NativeFileWatcher` constructor had pulled efsw into it, not txiki's host (10 KB, never pulled by a binary that makes no
+  runtime). The design's expectation held in bytes and not in cause.
+- **The compile-out is bigger on paper and smaller in lines.** 123 blocks and about 260 lines in six files, against the
+  design's 300. A `-O0` Debug build found two guards the Release link had folded away, and became a repeatable mode:
+  `tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh --off` fails on any call into a compiled-out unit by name (red shown with a guard
+  removed). The `ON` mode asserts the four counts in the CLI, so a run whose options did not take effect fails. The filter
+  regex is anchored to the source root, escaped so a checkout path is literal.
+- **`N8ReliableLink`'s test split is eleven and three,** not the design's eight and the rest.
+- **The console test binaries are `/bigobj` and off `/WX`** on Windows, a deliberate exclusion held in `spec/07`.
+- **The build function is a plain pointer and the config a `const void*`,** as designed; no caller needed more.
+
+**The re-records as they landed:** `product-registrations.json` alone, in the stage 2 commit's tree (the order of the
+console and host-I/O types; no id or descriptor moved). The parity, kit and render baselines, the `buildGraph` and role
+goldens, the script and protocol digests and `edio-golden.json` were never re-recorded.
+
+**Measurements** (`measure.sh`, recorded and not gated; the design commit against the final tree):
+
+| | base | final |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `libmesen.a` | 32,655,244 | 19,674,662 (-39.75%) |
+| mesen objects | 426 files, 31,050,928 B | 288 files, 18,783,112 B (-138, -39.5%) |
+| `retroplug-cli` | 34,293,952 | 30,641,680 |
+| `retroplug-cli` `.text` | 29,047,040 | 25,916,562 (-10.78%) |
+| `retroplug` / `-host` / `-sdl` | 33,389,568 / 28,512,952 / 34,904,176 | 30,029,608 / 24,865,848 / 31,256,368 |
+| `retroplug-ui-test` / `-render-host-test` | 31,117,840 / 21,663,464 | 27,465,544 / 17,316,784 |
+| `.so` / `.clap` / `.vst3` | 33,198,792 / 33,212,728 / 33,272,272 | 29,830,640 / 29,848,608 / 29,908,216 |
+| `-engine-graph-test` / `-audio-test` | 29,242,440 / 23,367,832 | 24,995,648 / 18,500,136 |
+| `SnesPpu` / `GbPpu` / `PceVdc` / `WsPpu` in the CLI | 200 / 55 / 40 / 52 | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
+
+The products are about 3.4 MB smaller. With `RETROPLUG_MESEN_LTO=ON` the `mesen` target compiles in 13 s with the three
+consoles ON and 8 s OFF, and relinking `retroplug-cli` alone takes 11 s against 9 s (a full CLI build is about 77 s either
+way). The all-ON script takes 113 s cold and 57 s warm; `--off` takes 31 s cold and 5 to 6 s warm.
+
+**Verification.** A baseline run at the design commit and a run at the final tree were each 43 legs (F3's 42 plus the
+measure), every one exit 0, and the summaries are byte-identical at every stage:
+
+- the device images, hashed: box native `af36f223` and PIO `4b4f9abc`, the device check `38665e2c`, and the `bliptoaster`
+  pack's three hashes (`066c7980`, `fd1daf9b`, `b5017c7c`), identical to the baseline;
+- strict parity unchanged (30 files, 250 cases, `RP_FAIL_ON_SKIP=1`), the kit, render and `buildGraph` goldens, the
+  protocol digests and the CLI suites;
+- `pnpm test`: 190 files, 1998 cases at the baseline and 1999 now (one new case); `pnpm test:plugin`: 11 binaries at the
+  baseline and 13 now, 926 cases at the tip, the console cases equal before and after (543) and `test:plugin` plus
+  `test:n8` totalling 1029 then 1031 (the two stage 1 cases); `test:native` 629 with resources and 629 with 144 skips in
+  the CI picture; `test:ui` 46; `device:check`, `device:box`, `device-mode-test` (96 cases), `sdl:smoke`,
+  `sdl:controller`, and the thread and address sanitizer legs; `check:docs` (91 files) and `check:boundaries` (no
+  exception, no warning).
+
+Windows, macOS and arm64 builds were never run, and CI was not triggered.
+
+**What the plan's acceptance must add,** because no stage ran it: `sdl:pipewire`, `reaper:all`, a fresh-clone build (the
+embeds, the generated tables and the configure fixtures from nothing), `pnpm build:mesen-all` and
+`tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh --off`, and BlipToaster's and NESVJ's suites against the rebuilt CLI.
+
+**Owed.** The nine Windows items, in `spec/07-remaining-work.md`: the moved clang-cl `SameBoySystem.cpp` step; `/W4 /WX`
+on the four new package targets, with the console test binaries' exclusion; the Mesen options under MSVC (the cache
+variables, the `$<BOOL:>` definitions, the six guarded files, LTO in `release.yml`); `retroplug-tjs-runtime`'s first
+compile; `retroplug-file-watcher` with efsw and `Threads::Threads`; `PluginDSP.cpp`'s new `efsw.hpp` include; the
+`retroplug-mgb-embeds` object library and its generated table; `packages.cmake`'s path logic on Windows paths; and
+`HostRpcWatching.test.cpp`, `LinkRomModel.hpp` and `retroplug-testing` under `cl`. Also the first macOS and arm64 builds
+and the first CI run.

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f2pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

F2 stage 5: Mesen's per-console compile-out, and the docs pass

The Mesen archive stops carrying the consoles RetroPlug never runs, and every doc the phase changed says
what the tree now is (docs/modular-graph-phase-f2-design.md section 4).

deps/mesen/CMakeLists.txt declares one option per console RetroPlug may drop, ON by default as upstream
Mesen builds: MESEN_ENABLE_SNES (the Super Nintendo AND the Game Boy, which Super Game Boy couples both
ways), MESEN_ENABLE_PCE and MESEN_ENABLE_WS. The root CMakeLists sets all three OFF as cache defaults
before add_subdirectory(deps/mesen), so a -D overrides them (tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh, pnpm
build:mesen-all, configures them on and builds the library and the CLI). NES, GBA and SMS are always
built, and nothing in this tree turns them off. Each option is a PUBLIC compile definition,
MESEN_ENABLE_<X>=0/1, so a consumer's translation units (MesenNesSystem.cpp and the rest) compile against
the same console set as the library they link, and a header's #if means the same thing on both sides.

The filter is one table next to the existing list(FILTER ...) calls: option | directories | evaluators |
units kept. A disabled console drops every .cpp under its directories (Core/SNES and Core/Gameboy for
SNES, nested directories included) and its CPUs' Core/Debugger/ExpressionEvaluator.<Cpu>.cpp (Snes, Spc,
Gsu, Cx4, NecDsp, St018, Gameboy / Pce / Ws - the design's assignment is right, Nes, Gba and Sms stay),
and keeps the two SNES units NES code and Emulator.cpp build: SNES/Input/SnesController.cpp (the input hub
every console's control manager constructs) and SNES/SnesDefaultVideoFilter.cpp (GetVideoFilter's
fallback). Only .cpp files are filtered; the headers stay on disk, so every #include keeps compiling. A
further console is one more row.

The call sites into a dropped console are guarded #if MESEN_ENABLE_* in six files, each guard marked
// RetroPlug: as the tree's earlier edits are: Core/Shared/Emulator.cpp (three TryLoadRom<> arms; the
SnesDefaultVideoFilter fallback stays), Core/Debugger/Debugger.cpp (the debugger construction switch, the
CPU switches, the state copies, the ROM save, the _DEBUG evaluator self-test and the explicit
instantiations), MemoryDumper.cpp (the dynamic_cast chain, one branch per console, and the memory
switches' per-console arms), DisassemblyInfo.cpp, Disassembler.cpp and ExpressionEvaluator.cpp (its
token switches, the nested CPU switch included). 123 guarded blocks across the six, about 260 lines. A
switch that had a default keeps it: GetCpuCycleCount returns 0, Emulator's GetVideoFilter falls back to
the kept filter, the debugger construction's `default:` throws "Unsupported CPU type", and
MemoryDumper's memory switches reach their existing default with a dropped MemoryType, which answers a
null buffer instead of dereferencing a null manager. A switch without a default falls past the switch
where its arm is gone: a void one becomes a no-op for that CPU (the instruction and memory accessors,
the state copies, PauseOnNextFrame, Disassembler::GetLineData), and a value one reaches the code after
it (IsDebugWindowOpened's false, GetAvailableTokens' nullptr, SaveRomToDisk's `return false`,
DisassemblyInfo::GetEffectiveAddress's throw, the op-size and jump/return predicates' throws among
them). None is reachable with the console compiled out, since the console cannot be constructed, and no
value-returning function runs off its end. Nothing NES, GBA or SMS changed: no kept case, default or
fallthrough sits inside a guard, and the one kept passage whose text moved is MemoryDumper's
dynamic_cast chain, re-split around its guards with the same tests in the same order.

Proof, each in a scratch build directory of its own, deleted afterwards:
- build/ (the dev loop, console options OFF, Release) builds the whole tree, and

  retroplug-engine-graph-test. That is the leg that matters: a plain switch over a template parameter
  references every arm at -O0, so a missed guard fails there and passes in Release. It did expose the
  arms the first Release link had folded away (MemoryDumper's dynamic_cast chain, ExpressionEvaluator's
  nested switch). tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh --off now holds it without either binary: it builds

- a Release configure with all three options ON (now tools/build-mesen-all-consoles.sh) builds the mesen
  library and retroplug-cli and asserts the four consoles' symbols are back in the binary, so the guards
  are two-way. The script's whole run (configure, library, CLI) took 111 s here, and 113 s with the
  counts asserted.
- LTO, RETROPLUG_MESEN_LTO=ON, two Release configures: the mesen target alone compiles in 13 s with every
  console on and 8 s with them off (LTO bitcode is cheaper to emit than -O2 code), and relinking the CLI

From a removed dir both variants compile the firmware, so the SDK's warnings print.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f2pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

- [ ] **Step 10: Not runnable here: Windows, macOS and CI**

**The Windows items are owed to the user**: F2 was built and reasoned about on Linux only, and the carve is the phase
that moves the most code a Windows compiler treats differently. `spec/07-remaining-work.md` lists the nine, and this
step quotes them as the tree holds them:

- The moved clang-cl custom command that compiles `SameBoySystem.cpp` (`retroplug-samebsys`, under `if(WIN32)` in
  `packages/sameboy/native/CMakeLists.txt`): its rewritten include roots, its header glob and its `DEPENDS` on the
  boot-ROM target.
- `/W4 /WX` on `retroplug-system`, `-sameboy`, `-mesen` and `-host-io`: the sources `retroplug-core` compiled at
  that level, now in four targets with new include sets. Also the deliberate exclusion of `retroplug-sameboy-test` /
  `-mesen-test` from that list (`packages/native/cmake/warnings.cmake`), which the first Windows run decides.
- The Mesen options under MSVC: the cache variables, the `$<BOOL:>` PUBLIC definitions, the six guarded files under
  mesen's MSVC warning treatment, and `RETROPLUG_MESEN_LTO` with the three options OFF in `release.yml`'s Windows
  job.
- `retroplug-tjs-runtime`: `TjsHostRuntime.cpp`'s first compile in a target of its own, at `/W4 /WX`.
- `retroplug-file-watcher`: `efsw-static` and `Threads::Threads` on Windows, at `/W4 /WX`.
- `PluginDSP.cpp`, which now includes `NativeFileWatcher.hpp` and so `efsw/efsw.hpp` under `/W4 /WX`; before the
  carve only the backend's two sources saw it.
- The embed object library `retroplug-mgb-embeds` (bin2c's `.c` built by cl) and the generated
  `rp_embedded_resources()` table (`extern "C"` arrays and a function-local static) in each product.
- `packages.cmake`'s new path logic on Windows paths: `_retroplug_unquote_path` on MSVC-escaped `\"` definitions,
  `file(RELATIVE_PATH)` with drive letters, and the runtime-library walk's target names.
- `HostRpcWatching.test.cpp` and `LinkRomModel.hpp` / the `retroplug-testing` library, compiled by cl.

On a Windows machine with this tree (the user's Windows agent), run `build.bat` and then `test.bat` (all four suites)
and report both. What is most likely to find something there: the moved clang-cl command's include roots, the Mesen
options' `$<BOOL:>` definitions under MSVC (a guard that reads as 0 where the library was built with 1 would fail at
link), `retroplug-tjs-runtime`'s first `/W4` compile of a vendored file, and `bin2c`'s generated `.c` under `cl`.
`build:mesen-all` and its `--off` mode are the two Windows legs worth running by hand as well, since the compile-out
is where MSVC's preprocessor and CMake's cache variables meet. **macOS and the arm64 Linux job** have not run either,
and the first macOS build is the riskiest of the three: the `sameboy` package's clang-cl block is Windows-only, but
the two new libraries' `POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE` and efsw's framework-free assumptions are not, and the SDL
standalone's `pipewire` leg is Linux-only in any case. **CI was not triggered**: `build.yml` runs on
`workflow_dispatch`, pull requests and pushes to `main` only, so `feature/modularize` runs none of it; the first CI
run is owed to a dispatched run or a PR the user starts. **And no step in this task needs a real device, and none may
touch one.** The NES, the N8, the Pico box, the probe and the Zoom L6 stay untouched: every device leg here is a
build, `sdl:controller` is the only port-listing run and it lists only its own fakes, and the Sanitizer and consumer
legs open nothing at all.
